## Kernel round: the hot paths compiled twice

Rejected by its bar CD-5 (the result is at the end): not merged. The
code stays on `rejected/h264-coarse-dispatch` (at `49a1cecc`: the code
measured, `def6f84a`, rebased onto `75d77dc`, with review notes and CI
jobs), on `main` at `40f29a6`, with a row in
`docs/measurements/h264-rejected.md`; what follows describes that branch,
its CI jobs, script and fuzz target included.

"Round 20: an x86-64-v3 build tier" measured the whole decoder built
for x86-64-v3 against the baseline build: 0.958 locally, and on the
2.90 GHz class 0.9650 [0.9555, 0.9690] at one thread (discard, 32 of 32
streams faster) and 0.9638 at eight. That build stays an opt-in for
source builds. What ships is one binary (round 20's Design, point 3):
the hot paths compiled twice, for the baseline and for x86-64-v3, and the
instance chosen once at a coarse level (the slice, or larger) rather
than at each kernel call. This round builds that, and measures it
against the v3-only build as its upper bound.

### What the measurement says

Local, as information (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/coarse-dispatch/local/`;
the development VM of the 2.90 GHz class, not a bar run). The builds are
`dist` builds of `main` at `40f29a6d`, without flags (`base`) and with
`-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3` (`v3`).

- **Where the v3 build's time goes** (`functions-v3.txt`: `perf`
  cpu-clock samples per function, eight training streams, two per class,
  two rounds, one thread, discard): 0.9715 of the baseline's samples.
  - The CABAC residual blocks hold most of the gain: `cabac::levels` and
    `cabac::significance_map` lose 2.1% of the baseline's samples
    together (`levels::<64>` 0.83%, `levels::<16>` 0.71%, the maps
    0.60%). Their decoding engine is shifts, leading-zero counts and
    table loads, which BMI2 and LZCNT shorten.
  - Motion compensation's call into the kernels is next: the baseline's
    `x86::predict::predict` (2.0%) is inlined into `predict_fast` in the
    v3 build, where both have AVX2, for a net 0.67%.
  - The other kernels' wrappers (`idct8x8_add`, `idct4x4_add_quad`,
    `filter_chroma_mb`, the intra predictions) are inlined the same way,
    and their samples move with them: about even. `Cabac::mvd` and
    `MbData::reset` gain 0.15% and 0.16%. The rest of the control code,
    `decode_cabac` above all, is unchanged.
- **A v3 entry at the slice loop alone gains nothing.** A
  `#[target_feature]` function wrapping `SliceDecoder::decode`, with the
  loop inlined into it (`e4`, an experiment, not kept), is 3.6 KB: the
  loop is in it, and every function the loop calls is still out of line
  and compiled for the baseline. A `#[target_feature]` function passes
  its features only to what the compiler inlines into it.
- **The functions with the gain, compiled twice, recover it**
  (`local-timing.txt`: CPU time, one thread pinned, all 32 streams, five
  rounds; median per-stream ratio to `base`; this VM moves a stream by
  several percent between runs):

  | Build | Median | Faster |
  |---|---|---|
  | `v3` | 0.976 | 27 of 32 |
  | this round (`after`) | 0.972 | 27 of 32 |
  | this round without `fast` (`safe`) | 0.998 | 18 of 32 |

- **Instructions** (`instructions.txt`, callgrind, three streams): the
  `v3` build executes 3.2% to 4.9% fewer than `base`, this round 1.5% to
  2.5% fewer; `safe` 0.15% to 0.28% more (register allocation in the
  kernel's `predict`, whose body this round moves into a function of its
  own). The v3 build's count overstates its time: much of what it removes
  is register moves that its three-operand forms make unnecessary.

### Design

1. **What is compiled twice.** Three functions, the ones the profile
   names: `cabac::significance_map` and `cabac::levels` (each block shape),
   and `SliceDecoder::predict_fast`. Each has a body (`..._body`,
   `#[inline(always)]`) and two instances: the baseline one, the function
   as before, and a v3 one in `fast` (`fast::v3`), a safe function with
   `#[target_feature(enable = "avx,avx2,bmi1,bmi2,f16c,fma,lzcnt,movbe,popcnt,sse3,ssse3,sse4.1,sse4.2")]`,
   the x86-64-v3 level's features that change code generation, whose
   body is the same body inlined. The source of each body exists once.
2. **The instance is a type.** `tier::Tier` names the three functions;
   `tier::Base` implements it with the baseline instances and `fast::V3`
   with the v3 ones. The callers on the way from the slice loop to them
   take a `T: Tier` (`decode_slice_data`, the CABAC and CAVLC loops,
   `decode_mb`, the inter prediction's functions down to `predict_list`,
   and `CabacSyntax`, which carries one for `Cabac::residual`), so the
   compiler builds that chain once per instance, and each call into the
   three functions is static: no branch on the CPU below the slice loop.
3. **Chosen once.** `Decoder` detects the CPU's features when it is made
   (`tier::Choice`, `V3::detect`) and hands the choice to each picture's
   work; `SliceDecoder::decode` runs one instance of the chain per slice.
   `Decoder::with_x86_64_v3(false)` keeps the baseline instance, for
   comparing the two (the fuzz target below).
4. **The helpers of the chain are per instance too.** With the chain
   built twice, a helper that `main` inlines into its one caller has two
   callers, one per instance, and the compiler then calls it out of line
   in both: in a first build `fill_ctx::<2>`, `fused_ops`,
   `combine_modes`, `combine_predictions`, `parse_inter_pred` and
   `start_intra` were out of line, 1.6% more instructions on an sd
   stream with the CABAC functions twinned alone. Each takes the
   `T: Tier` as well (unused, a type parameter only), so that each
   instance has its own copy with `main`'s one caller, and the compiler
   inlines it as before; so do `parse_mb_pred`, `parse_sub_mb_pred` and
   `parse_mvd`, below them. The out-of-line functions of this round's
   build are then `main`'s, the v3 instances, five functions run once
   per decoder, per slice or per I_PCM macroblock, and `average_into`, a
   small helper of the kernels' 4-wide averaged blocks (`symbols.txt`).
5. **The kernel inlined into the v3 `predict_fast`.** In the v3 build the
   kernel's `x86::predict::predict` is inlined because it has one caller.
   Here it has two, one per instance, and is too large to inline into
   either. `Kernels::predict_inlined` is `Kernels::predict` for a caller
   compiled for x86-64-v3: the dispatching kernels call the vector
   kernel's body (`x86::predict::predict_body`, `#[inline(always)]`,
   without the attribute; `predict` is now that body under the attribute)
   so that it is inlined into such a caller. The baseline instance calls
   `Kernels::predict`, as before. Inlined into a caller without AVX2 the
   body would still be sound, since a `Simd` proves AVX2, only slower;
   no such caller exists.
6. **`unsafe`.** Calling a `#[target_feature]` function from code
   compiled without its features is `unsafe`. `V3`'s implementation of
   `Tier` makes the three calls, one `unsafe` block each, in `fast`: the
   site `v3-entry` (`docs/unsafe-sites.md`). The precondition is the
   CPU's features; a `V3` exists only where `V3::detect` found all
   thirteen. The site forms no pointer and reads nothing; the code it
   calls is the safe bodies. The kernel crate gains one `unsafe` call of
   the kind it has (`Simd::predict_inlined`, sound because a `Simd`
   exists only where AVX2 does).
7. **Safe mode.** A build without the feature `fast` has no `fast`
   module and no `V3`: `Choice` holds nothing and the decoder runs the
   baseline instance, compiling no `unsafe` of its own. `fast` is a default feature, as planned for the hot-path sites:
   the speed is the reason for the site, and the safe mode is one flag
   away for a direct user of the crate (`coreav-backend-h264`, and the
   CLI through it, take the default). The crate copies the workspace's lint table with
   `unsafe_code = "deny"`; `fast` allows it, and every other module is
   `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
8. **Evidence of sameness.** The two instances compile the same source,
   integer code only, so their results are the same by construction;
   the checks are the hot-path exception's. A unit test decodes 2,000 random slices'
   residual blocks with both instances of `Cabac::residual` and compares
   every result, block and engine state, errors included
   (`the_v3_instance_decodes_what_the_baseline_decodes`, about 75,000
   blocks); the fuzz target `instances` decodes each input with both and
   compares every call's result and every picture; the CI conformance job
   runs the suite in both modes (`scripts/h264_conformance.py --mode
   safe`), and lints and tests the safe mode. `scripts/h264_modes_identity.py`
   decodes a set of streams with both builds at 1 and 8 threads and
   compares the output: in CI on ten synthetic streams the pinned FFmpeg
   encodes there with libx264 (CABAC and CAVLC, B slices, both direct
   modes, explicit and implicit weighting, 8x8 transforms, several slices
   a picture, a cropped height, quantizers from 2 to 45; job
   `modes-identity`), and on the 32 training streams (job
   `training-identity`, which reads corpus v1 and runs only where the
   corpus credentials are set). Each round's gating run also compares
   both builds' output on the training streams with `main`'s (CD-9).

### Rejected

- **A build tier chosen at install or load time** (round 20's options):
  ruled out, since distribution ships one binary; the v3 build stays
  an opt-in for source builds.
- **A v3 entry at the slice loop alone** (`e4` above): the loop's
  callees stay baseline.
- **The whole macroblock layer inlined into one v3 entry**
  (`#[inline(always)]` down the call tree): one function the size of the
  decoder, built twice, where the gain sits in three; not built.
- **A closure the kernel crate enters** (`Kernels::hot`, branch
  `perf/h264-kernels-hot`): no `unsafe` in the decoder, but everything
  under the AVX2 entry has to be inlined into the closure. With motion
  compensation's prediction entered per block, it measured level with
  `main` (554.5 million instructions against 554.8 million on an sd
  stream; callgrind, local, not kept) where an entry around `predict_fast` reached 540.8 million:
  passing the task into the closure cost what the inlining saved.
- **The instance as a run-time value** (an `Option<V3>` tested at each
  call of the three functions): a branch per kernel call is what the
  decision rules out; the type costs no branch.
- **Source twins by macro or by including a file twice:** each needs the
  bodies written inside a macro or a second module, out of `rustfmt`'s
  reach, or a procedural macro crate; the trait keeps each body as
  ordinary code and costs one forwarding function per instance.
- **More functions compiled twice** (`Cabac::mvd`, `MbData::reset`, the
  other kernels' wrappers): 0.15% or 0.16% each, or nothing, in the profile; not
  worth a call in the site.
- **Fewer features** (BMI2 and LZCNT only, which round 20 measured at
  0.982 as a whole build): the v3 set is what the upper bound was
  measured with, and detecting it costs no more.

### Bars

Fixed before the A/B run, on the 2.90 GHz class by the rounds' method
("Round A/B runs on more than one class"; `--require-cpu 'Intel(R)
Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.90GHz'`, the host-health gate before and after each
call, the training set, one call per class with its frame count), FFmpeg
9.0.2 (BtbN `n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068`) as the reference of every call. Four
arms, built on the run's host with one toolchain, `cargo build --locked
--profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`:

- `main`: `main` at this round's base, `RUSTFLAGS` unset;
- `v3`: the same commit with `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3"`, the
  upper bound;
- `after`: this round's commit, default features;
- `safe`: this round's commit with `--no-default-features`, the safe
  twin.

Calls: `g`, `--pin 2 --rounds 5`, all four arms; `gm`, the same with
`MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072` for the whole call ("Where the allocator
puts the planes": `Decoder` and each picture's work hold the choice, a
change of size), `main` and `after`; `t8`, `--threads 8`, unpinned, ten
rounds ("Rounds at eight threads"), `main`, `v3` and `after`. Each bar is a
median of per-stream ratios with its 95% bootstrap interval;
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/coarse-dispatch/analyze.py` reads them
(`python3 -I analyze.py DIR g gm t8`).

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| CD-1 | `after` over `main`, one thread (`g`), discard, all 32 streams | at most **0.980**, upper end of the interval below 1.000 |
| CD-2 | the same, write | at most **0.985** |
| CD-3 | the same, discard and write, each class | at most **1.000** in each |
| CD-4 | `after` over `main`, eight threads (`t8`), discard, all 32; and each class, discard and write | at most **0.990**; at most **1.005** in each |
| CD-5 | `after` over `v3`, discard, at one thread (`g`) and at eight (`t8`): all 32, and each class | at most **1.010** overall and **1.020** in each class, at both |
| CD-6 | `after` over `safe` (`g`), discard, all 32 | at most **0.980**, upper end of the interval below 1.000 |
| CD-7 | `safe` over `main` (`g`), discard, all 32 | at most **1.005** |
| CD-8 | `after` over `main` with the mapped allocator (`gm`), discard, all 32 | at most **0.985**, upper end of the interval below 1.000 |
| CD-9 | output | `after` and `safe` byte-identical to `main` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads in both modes, and with the scalar kernels |

CD-1 to CD-4 ask for an improvement over the baseline build at one
thread and at eight, overall and per class (P1's and P3's conditions);
CD-1 is about half the v3 build's measured gain (0.965). CD-5 asks for
the v3 build's gain itself, within 1% overall and 2% in a class, at both
thread counts. CD-6 is the A/B of the site against its safe twin that
the hot-path exception requires, and CD-7 that the twin keeps `main`'s speed. The site is
adopted (the code, `fast` as a default feature, the site's row, this
section) only if CD-1 to CD-9 all pass; otherwise this section records
the result, the ledger keeps the branch, and nothing else changes: no
unused `unsafe` stays.

## Round 22: a neighbour cache

The MB layer is the stage furthest from FFmpeg's time, in every class
("Again at `40f29a6`": 1.81 times overall, 1.68 to 2.02 by class), and
round 18's records kept from picture to picture did not move it. This
round changes how a macroblock reads what its neighbours left and how
much it leaves for them.

### What the measurement says

- **What a macroblock leaves is mostly read by nobody.** `MbInfo` was
  124 bytes: the intra prediction mode, CAVLC's TotalCoeff and CABAC's
  absolute mvd of all sixteen 4x4 blocks (104 bytes). Its neighbours read
  only the bottom row (the macroblock below) and the right column (the
  macroblock to the right): seven of the sixteen blocks. A picture's
  records are 4 MB at 4k (1 MB at 1080p), read again by the deblocking
  filter.
- **Shrinking the record alone does not pay** (local, as information,
  `round22/local/`). A prototype kept the edges in a 56-byte record and
  the current macroblock's whole arrays beside it, so every neighbour read
  asked whether the block was the current macroblock's, then looked up the
  edge slot: 0.9 to 1.1% more instructions on two 720p streams
  (`instructions.txt`), and a CPU-time median of 1.0016 over the 32
  training streams, seven rounds (`ab-record-only.txt`; 4k 0.990, 720p
  1.005).
- **The reads themselves are branches.** Each neighbour read derives the
  neighbouring block (`neighbour_4x4`: inside the macroblock, or in A or
  B, or missing), then asks the macroblock's kind (skipped, intra, I_PCM)
  before it loads the value; these are `neighbour_4x4`, `info` and the
  closures around them in the profile's MB layer items.

### Design

1. **One cache per quantity** (`nb.rs`). For the macroblock being
   decoded, a five by five array holds A's right column in column 0, B's
   bottom row in row 0 and the macroblock's sixteen blocks inside, so the
   left and upper neighbours of block (x, y) are one and five places
   before it, whichever macroblock they belong to. Chroma's TotalCoeff has
   a three by three array per component. A neighbour that is missing is a
   value in the array: `nb::NA` for TotalCoeff and the intra mode,
   whose rules ask whether it is available (clauses 9.2.1 and 8.3.1.1),
   0 for mvd, which counts a missing, skipped or intra neighbour as 0
   (clause 9.3.3.1.1.7). A read is then one load and no branch.
2. **Filled when read, from the neighbours' edges.** Each cache is filled
   just before the syntax that reads it: the mvd caches before mb_pred or
   sub_mb_pred of a CABAC inter macroblock (not for B_Direct_16x16), the
   TotalCoeff caches before a CAVLC residual, the intra cache before the
   modes of an Intra_4x4 or Intra_8x8 macroblock. A skipped macroblock
   fills none. The intra cache resolves the neighbour's kind once, at the
   fill: its modes if Intra_4x4 or Intra_8x8, 2 if coded another way,
   `NA` if missing or excluded by constrained_intra_pred. Equation 8-72's
   block for an Intra_4x4 neighbour of an 8x8 block is, for a block in A
   or B, the adjacent one, so one cache serves both block sizes.
3. **The record keeps edges only.** `MbInfo` keeps each quantity's bottom
   row and right column (`nb::Edge`, eight bytes) and is 60 bytes, within
   a cache line. TotalCoeff and mvd share one array (`entropy`), since an
   available neighbour is in the macroblock's own slice (clause 6.4.9) and
   a slice has one entropy coding mode; a macroblock that codes neither
   leaves zeros, which is what a skipped or intra macroblock contributes
   to the mvd context and to nC. I_PCM writes TotalCoeff 16 only in a
   CAVLC slice. The CABAC 8x8 block no longer stores a TotalCoeff, which
   CABAC never reads.
4. **A partition's run of blocks is written with a width the compiler
   knows** (`nb::put::<N>`, N of 1, 2 or 4): a first build used `fill`
   on a runtime-length slice, which became a call to `memset` per row
   and cost 0.7 to 0.9% more instructions than `main`
   (`instructions.txt`).

Rejected: a cache filled for every macroblock at its start, as a
neighbour derivation would be (the skipped macroblocks, the most common
kind in P and B slices, read none of it); keeping the record whole and
adding the cache (the 4 MB of records at 4k stays); and the record-only
prototype above. Local, as information (`round22/local/ab.txt`; CPU time,
one thread, pinned, seven rounds, base `main` at `40f29a6`): the cache
0.977 over the 32 streams (sd 0.964, 720p 0.980, 1080p 0.995, 4k 0.955),
faster on 26; 0.17 to 0.23% fewer instructions than `main` on the two
720p streams. Output identical, 32 of 32 at one and eight threads, on
`main` at `75d77dc` (`identity-local.txt`).

Prior art: none read for this round. A per-macroblock cache of the
neighbours' values is a common structure in decoders; FFmpeg's profile
names one (`fill_decode_caches`, "Again at `40f29a6`"), and only its
name and time were looked at.

## Motion round: the reference's lines requested ahead, cheaply

The profile at `40f29a6` puts inter prediction at 1.26 times FFmpeg's time
in the 4k class, where it is 1.07 to 1.22 in the others. This round asks
where that goes and takes the part that a request for memory buys back.

### What the measurement says

Local, as information (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/mc-ahead/local/`; a
development VM of the 2.50 GHz class, not a bar run). The variants were
measured on the branch of "Kernel round: the hot paths compiled twice"
(rejected), `main`'s decoding with three functions compiled twice; the build kept is timed again
on `main` (`local-timing.txt`).

- **The class is not one picture size.** Its eight streams' pictures hold
  1.3 to 12.7 MiB of samples (690x1458 to 4096x2160); three are larger
  than a 1080p picture (3.0 MiB).
- **Motion compensation waits for memory there** (`profile-4k.txt`:
  `perf` samples per function, the eight streams, one thread, `main` at
  `75d77dc`; FFmpeg 9.0.2's `ffmpeg_g` at function level). `luma_block`
  and `chroma_block` take 0.23 and 0.15 of FFmpeg's time, against about
  0.08 in FFmpeg's copies and interpolation and 0.10 in the C function
  around them (`mc_part_420_simple_8`); on `3b1b441e23ae` almost all of
  `luma_block`'s samples sit on the full-sample copy's loads of reference
  rows and the stores after them.
- **The same misses, hidden in FFmpeg and not here**
  (`cachegrind-3b1b.txt`: simulated caches, which do not model prefetch
  instructions; 60 pictures of `3b1b441e23ae`, a 1 MiB last level). Both
  decoders execute about as many instructions (2.15 and 2.09 billion), and
  the two kernels' read misses at that level, 7.5 million, are about those
  of FFmpeg's assembly (its copies, interpolation and filters, which the
  simulation does not name), 7.7 million; yet the decode takes 1.47 times
  FFmpeg's time on that stream. FFmpeg's prefetch function holds up to
  0.10 of its samples at 4k (0.04 on average; function level only): it
  asks for the lines ahead. Huge pages for the whole run do not move the
  ratio to FFmpeg one way (`thp.txt`), so the wait is not the address
  translation.
- **Round 12's part R, again, and why it cost.** Part R asked for the
  window's rows of the next four macroblocks at each block's own vector;
  on the bar machine, on top of part D, it measured 0.851 [0.799, 0.966]
  at 4k and failed its bar over 720p to 4k. Each hint goes through
  `prefetch::rows_for_read`, which checks a row's index and adds its
  stride with overflow checks: several instructions a row, and some 80
  rows a call for a window's rows at both ends in three planes. Re-created
  here, hints at every macroblock cost 10% to 14% on the class
  (`variants.txt`, 1); with one range check and a strided walk, and one
  hint a row of the block, hints every fourth macroblock give 0.915 (7 of
  8 streams faster; 2).
- **Where the hints pay** (`variants.txt`, 3 and 4): over all 32 streams,
  hints for every picture cost on the sd class (1.028) and the 720p class
  (1.010); under round 12's rule (pictures above 1 MiB) the median is
  0.992 (25 of 32 faster): 1080p 0.987 and 0.980, 4k 0.980 and 0.957 in
  two runs. `af38b0cfd840` (720x1280, four references) loses 6% to 8%
  in every run.

### Design

1. **A hint costs a few instructions.** `prefetch::rows_for_read` and
   `rows_for_write` check where their rows start once and then walk the
   plane `stride` at a time until the rows or the slice end: the same
   rows hinted as before (a test compares them with the checked form's
   for every start, stride and count it tries), one `prefetcht0` and an
   add or two each. Part D's hints, which go through `rows_for_write`,
   cost less too.
2. **What is asked for.** `Planes::request(x, y, h)` hints `h` luma rows
   from luma sample (`x`, `y`) and `h / 2` rows of each chroma plane from
   (`x >> 1`, `y >> 1`), one hint a row at that column; a position outside
   the picture, or rows the reference's slices do not hold (a band), is
   not hinted. It is out of line: inlined into `predict_fast`, its
   three walks cost that function registers on every block, hinted or
   not (on an sd stream, which asks for nothing, 6.8% more of its
   instructions; out of line 0.4%, the test; `instructions-sd.txt`).
3. **When.** In `predict_fast`, a block at a luma `x` that is a
   multiple of 64 (the first macroblock of each four, at its left edge)
   asks for its own rows, at its own vector, 64 samples to the right: the
   luma line the next four macroblocks read if they move alike, and half
   of the chroma line they read. The block's rows, not the window's: most
   blocks are full-sample copies, which read none of the five extra rows.
4. **Where.** Pictures above 1 MiB of samples, round 12's rule (`ahead`),
   which part D already follows: no new threshold.
5. **No dispatch, no new `unsafe`.** The hint sits in `predict_fast`, for
   whole and banded references alike; it adds no branch on the CPU, and
   the hints are the kernel crate's `hint_read`, as before.

Hints change no value: the output is the same by construction, and the
32 training streams decode byte-identical to the base at 1 and 8 threads
(`identity-after.txt`).
Locally this round's build takes 0.999 of `main`'s time over the 32
streams (16 faster; sd, which runs no hint, 1.004, 720p 1.005, 1080p
0.973, 4k 0.939); two earlier runs, with `request` inlined, gave 0.987
and 0.991, 4k 0.917 and 0.942 (`local-timing.txt`).

Rejected (`variants.txt`):
- **Every macroblock asking for the next one's lines** (every 16, 16
  samples ahead): 0.961 on the class with the cheap walk, 1.14 with the
  checked one; the same line is asked for four times.
- **The window's rows** (`h + 5`): 0.936 against 0.915; the extra rows
  are read only by interpolated blocks.
- **Half the chroma hints** (every eighth macroblock, a chroma line ahead):
  0.987 against 0.988 over 720p to 4k; one call for the three planes is
  simpler.
- **Luma only:** 0.999 against 0.986 with the checked walk; the chroma
  copies wait as long.
- **A rule above 1080p's size:** the 1080p class gains too (0.980 and
  0.987).
- **Huge pages** (`madvise`): no change in either decoder (`thp.txt`), and
  a system call is not the decoder's to make.

### Bars

Fixed before the A/B run, by the rounds' method on the 2.90 GHz class
(`--require-cpu 'Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.90GHz'`, the host-health
gate before and after each call, the training set, one call per class with
its frame count), FFmpeg 9.0.2 (BtbN `n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068`) the reference
of every call. Two arms built on the run's host with one toolchain, `cargo
build --locked --profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`: `before`,
this round's base, and `after`, this round's commit. Calls: `g`, `--pin 2
--rounds 5`; `t8`, `--threads 8`, unpinned, ten rounds. The arms allocate
alike, so there is no mapped-allocator call.
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/mc-ahead/analyze.py` reads them (`python3
-I analyze.py DIR g t8`); each bar is a median of per-stream ratios with
its 95% bootstrap interval, over all 32 streams of each call.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| MA-1 | `after` over `before`, one thread (`g`), discard, all 32 | at most **1.000**, upper end of the interval below 1.005 |
| MA-2 | the same, write | at most **1.000**, upper end below 1.005 |
| MA-3 | the same, discard, the 4k class; and the 1080p and 4k classes together | at most **0.975**; at most **0.985**, upper end below 1.000 |
| MA-4 | the same, each class, discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| MA-5 | eight threads (`t8`), discard, all 32; and each class | at most **1.000**; at most **1.010** in each |
| MA-6 | output | `after` byte-identical to `before` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads, in both modes; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads in both modes, and with the scalar kernels |

MA-3 asks for the gain where the round aims, the pictures above 1080p's
size and at it; MA-1 and MA-2 that it costs nothing over all 32 streams,
discarding or writing (half of them, the sd class and most of 720p, run
no hint or gain little, so the overall median sits near 1.000 by
construction; locally 0.991, 0.987 and 0.999 in three runs); MA-4 and
MA-5 that no class and no thread count loses. The change is adopted only if MA-1 to
MA-6 pass; otherwise this section records the result and the ledger keeps
the branch.

## Kernel round: the hot paths compiled twice, wider

"Kernel round: the hot paths compiled twice" was rejected by CD-5: its
three functions, compiled twice and chosen once a slice, took 0.973 of
`main`'s time at one thread, where the v3 build took 0.962; it stayed
1.38% behind that build overall, 2.35% in the sd class and 1.77% in
720p. This round finds where that remainder is, widens what is compiled
twice to hold it, and measures again with new bars and a new run. It
starts from that round's code (`rejected/h264-coarse-dispatch`), whose
design ("Design", points 1 to 8 of that section) it keeps except where
this section says otherwise.

### What the measurement says

Local, as information (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/dispatch-wide/local/`).
The development VM of this round is not of the bar class (an Intel Xeon at
2.50 GHz, family 6, model 85): a stream's time moves by several percent
between runs there, more than the gap sought, so the local evidence is
instruction counts, and the bar-class evidence is what earlier runs
committed.

- **CAVLC streams got none of the gain** (the rejected round's gating
  run, `coarse-dispatch/gating/analysis.txt`, per stream): four of the
  eight sd streams and one 720p stream are CAVLC. Their `after` took
  0.990 to 1.005 of `main`'s time and 1.024 to 1.055 of the v3 build's;
  the CABAC sd streams took 1.008 to 1.023 of the v3 build's. The three
  functions are the CABAC residual blocks and motion compensation's
  block prediction; a CAVLC slice ran the baseline everywhere but in the
  latter.
- **Where the v3 build's instructions go beyond the three functions**
  (`functions-rejected.txt`: callgrind, instructions per compiled
  function, five streams, two sd and three 720p, CABAC and CAVLC, 120
  pictures each; the rejected round's commit built without flags and
  with `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`, the same source, so that the functions
  match by name): the v3 build executes 1.5% to 3.0% fewer. Beyond the
  three functions it saves in the slice loops (`decode_cabac`, with
  `decode_mb` and the CABAC parse inlined into it, and the CAVLC loop),
  in the CAVLC residual block (`CavlcSyntax::block`), in the work at the
  start of each slice (`LevelScale::new`, whose `params.rs` holds 0.7% and
  1.1% of the two sd streams' instructions, `files-rejected.txt`, and
  `Cabac::new`'s context initialization), and in
  `start_mb`, `MbData::reset` and `Cabac::mvd`. The rest is the kernel
  crate's dispatching wrappers (`filter_chroma_mb`, the intra predictions
  and the inverse transforms), into which the v3 build inlines the
  vector kernels: instructions move from the kernel to the wrapper, and
  the bar-class profile of the rejected round
  (`coarse-dispatch/local/functions-v3.txt`) shows no time gained by it
  (each pair of wrapper and kernel within 0.1% of the run).
- **This round's code** (`instructions.txt`, the same five streams, as
  a share of `main`'s instructions; `v3` is `main` built for x86-64-v3,
  the bar's upper bound):

  | Stream | `v3` | rejected round | this round (`after`) | `after` built for v3 | `safe` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | sd, CABAC | 0.9493 | 0.9725 | 0.9537 | 0.9555 | 1.0027 |
  | sd, CAVLC | 0.9554 | 0.9911 | 0.9696 | 0.9626 | 1.0035 |
  | 720p, CABAC | 0.9649 | 0.9863 | 0.9767 | 0.9611 | 1.0004 |
  | 720p, CABAC | 0.9635 | 0.9873 | 0.9771 | 0.9582 | 1.0007 |
  | 720p, CAVLC | 0.9741 | 0.9935 | 0.9848 | 0.9774 | 1.0011 |

  The gap to `v3` falls from 2.0%–3.7% to 0.5%–1.5%; most of what
  is left is the kernel wrappers above (`functions.txt`).

### Design

1. **One entry for any function: `Tier::enter`.** The rejected round
   wrote each v3 instance by hand, a `#[target_feature]` function with
   the function's arguments. This round adds a generic one:
   `Tier::enter(f)` runs a closure in the instance. `Base` calls it in
   place; `V3` calls `v3::enter`, one `#[target_feature]` function
   generic over the closure, into which the closure, marked
   `#[inline(always)]` and holding the function's body (`..._body`,
   `#[inline(always)]`), is inlined, so that the compiler builds the body
   for x86-64-v3. A function the round compiles twice is then a wrapper,
   `fn f<T: Tier>(.., t: T) { t.enter(|| self.f_body(..)) }`: for `Base`
   it is `main`'s function, for `V3` a call into its v3 body. `v3::enter`
   is left to the compiler's inlining, as `main` leaves the function:
   inlined into a caller of the same instance where the compiler inlines
   it in the v3 build.
2. **What runs through it**, the functions the profile names, each once
   a slice or once a macroblock: the slice loops (`decode_cabac` and
   `decode_cavlc`, and with them everything `main` inlines into them:
   `decode_mb`, the syntax elements of both entropy coders, the CABAC
   residual's parse), `start_mb`, `MbData::reset`, `Cabac::new_in` (the
   contexts of clause 9.3.1.1), `Cabac::mvd`, the CAVLC residual block
   (`CavlcSyntax::block`, which now carries the instance as
   `CabacSyntax` does) and the CAVLC residual's parse (`parse_residual`
   with CAVLC, out of line in `main`; with CABAC it is inlined into its
   loop, so it is left there), and the level scales of each slice
   (`LevelScale::new`, through `Choice::level_scale`, chosen with the
   slice's instance).
3. **The by-value instances stay for the blocks.** A closure's captures
   reach a function that stays out of line through memory: `enter` suits
   a function called once a slice or a macroblock with a few arguments,
   and not one called for each block with eight. A first build that put
   `predict_fast`, `significance_map` and `levels` through it too (`w1`
   in `local/`) spent 0.3% to 1.2% more of each run's instructions in
   `predict_fast` alone than the hand-written instance with its arguments
   in registers (`functions-w1.txt`). Those
   three keep the rejected round's by-value instances, and `Tier` keeps
   their methods beside `enter`.
4. **The helpers of the chain, again** (the rejected round's point 4).
   The functions now compiled twice inline helpers that then have two
   callers, one per instance, and went out of line in the first build:
   `request_destination` in `start_mb`, `Cabac::exp_golomb_bypass` and
   the instance of `Cabac::unary` for `mvd`'s closure. The first two are
   `#[inline(always)]`, which is what `main` does with them; `mvd`'s
   body takes the `T` so that each instance has its own closure, and
   with it its own `unary`.
5. **The baseline instance stays `main`'s.** With the loops behind
   `enter`, the compiler inlined `decode_cabac` into `decode_slice_data`
   in the safe build and took `Cabac::terminate` and the residual's parse
   out of line instead (0.8% more instructions on an sd stream than
   `main`); `decode_cabac` is `#[inline(never)]`, as the compiler leaves
   it in `main`, and the safe build executes 0.04% to 0.35% more than
   `main` on these five streams (the table above). The rejected round's
   safe build executed 0.15% to 0.28% more on three other streams, at
   another base, and passed CD-7 at 0.9995.
6. **`unsafe`.** The site `v3-entry` gains one call, `v3::enter`, beside
   the three of the rejected round. Its precondition is theirs, the CPU's
   features, which a `V3` proves; `v3::enter` forms no pointer and reads
   nothing: it calls the closure. The closures are the safe bodies.
7. **What is not compiled twice.** The kernel crate's wrappers (no time
   in the bar-class profile, above); `inter_pred` and
   `motion_compensate` above `predict_fast` (under 0.2% of instructions
   in the profile); the deblocking (outside the slice loop, and no
   faster in the v3 build: 0.16% more instructions there);
   `BitReader::ue`, out of line and shared with the headers' parse (under
   0.1%).
8. **Evidence of sameness**, as the rejected round's point 8, with three
   more differential tests of the v3 instance against the baseline's:
   CAVLC residual blocks on random bits, every block shape, nC class and
   maxNumCoeff
   (`cavlc::tests::the_v3_instance_decodes_what_the_baseline_decodes`,
   about 97,000 blocks); the engine's start and mvd_lX on random data,
   every cabac_init_idc and slice QP
   (`the_v3_instance_starts_and_reads_motion_as_the_baseline_does`); and
   the level scales of random scaling lists
   (`each_instance_derives_the_same_level_scales`). The fuzz target
   `instances`, the conformance suite in both modes and the
   modes-identity jobs cover the rest, as before.

### Rejected

- **Everything through `enter`** (`w1`): point 3.
- **A hand-written instance for each function** (the rejected round's
  method, widened): ten more `#[target_feature]` functions, each with
  its arguments, for what `enter` gives once a slice or a macroblock at
  no measurable cost.
- **The level scales once a parameter set** instead of once a slice: a
  change that every build gains from, not a dispatch; the round would
  then measure two changes. It is a candidate for a round of its own.
- **The kernel wrappers compiled twice**: no time to recover (above).
- The rejected round's own list, which stands.

## Kernel round: a macroblock's luma residual in one call

### What the measurement says

The profile of `main` at `40f29a6` ("Again at `40f29a6`") puts reconstruction at 0.090 of FFmpeg 9.0.2's time
against FFmpeg's 0.074, 1.46 times FFmpeg's at 1080p; its largest items are the luma transforms
(`idct4x4_add_quad` 0.0199, `idct8x8_add` 0.0077) and the glue around them (`residual_4x4_luma` 0.0026 in the
decoder and 0.0019 inlined from the kernels; `profile-40f29a6/items-rest.txt`). At `6a4ff38` (callgrind, one
thread, `--discard`, twelve pictures), the 8x8 transforms are 64.9 million of 1,624 million instructions of
`175433794e02.0.1080p` and their glue in `reconstruct_inter` most of its 15.0 million; on
`a6af290d9053.0.1080p` the 4x4 transforms are 36.7 million and `residual_4x4_luma` 11.6 million of 2,106
million (`luma-dc/functions.txt`). Each quadrant of 4x4 blocks and each 8x8 block costs a view, an extent check and a call through the
dispatch.

Many of these blocks have nothing to transform but their DC. Counting at `6a4ff38` over the training set at the
class frame counts (a counting build, not kept; `luma-dc/counts.txt`): 28% of the inter 8x8 blocks with a
residual, 35% of the inter 4x4 blocks (33% of the horizontal pairs have nothing else in any block they add),
81% of the Intra_16x16 blocks (77% of the pairs), 29% of the Intra_4x4 blocks and 13% of the Intra_8x8 ones;
per stream the inter shares run from 1% to 100%. The chroma round's identity holds for luma: a 4x4 or 8x8
inverse transform of a block whose only coefficient is its first, `d`, gives `d` in every sample before
rounding (in each pass a line holding `d` and zeros gives `d` in every position: Equations 8-338 to 8-345
and 8-351 to 8-366).

Unlike chroma, the decoder does not know which blocks these are, except an Intra_16x16 block without AC
levels, whose DC comes from the DC transform. Marking them where the entropy decoder stores a block (one level
and a non-zero first coefficient; `luma-dc/variants/mark.diff`) was measured: in `decode_cabac` it costs 3.95
million instructions on the twelve pictures of `a6af290d9053` (about 7.5 a coded block), more than the
transforms it saves there, where 10% of the blocks are DC-only (`luma-dc/functions.txt`); on top of the
kernel's own test (item 3 below) it raises the instructions of 26 of the 32 streams, a median 1.0005
(`luma-dc/variants/instructions.txt`). A kernel already holds a pair's or an 8x8 block's coefficients in registers, and
testing them there costs six instructions a pair and ten a block.

### Design

As measured at `e49998b` (`luma-dc/k.diff`); the round was rejected and none of it is in `main` (the result below).

1. **Two calls per macroblock.** `Kernels::luma4x4_residual_mb(dst, coeffs, nz, dc)` adds the 4x4 blocks of a
   16x16 view whose bits of `nz` are set, `Kernels::luma8x8_residual_mb(dst, coeffs, nz, dc)` the 8x8 ones.
   The decoder makes one call where it made up to four, with one view; the x86 kernel checks the
   macroblock's sixteen rows once (`rows_at_mut`) and steps over the quadrants (or 8x8 blocks) with a bit set,
   lowest first, adding a quadrant's two horizontal pairs as `idct4x4_add_quad` did.
2. **Blocks marked as having their DC alone.** Where bit `k` of `dc` is set too, block `k`'s coefficients
   other than its first are taken as 0 (the trait's semantics), and the kernel adds `(d + 32) >> 6` without a
   transform. The decoder marks what it knows for nothing, the Intra_16x16 blocks without AC levels, and
   passes 0 for the rest. A marked pair is its two DCs; a pair with one marked block transforms the other,
   the marked one's lane masked to zero, and adds the DC to that lane before rounding.
3. **Blocks found to have their DC alone.** For an unmarked pair, the kernel ORs its four rows with each
   block's first value blended out and tests the result (`vptest`); for an 8x8 block, its eight rows. Where
   nothing else is set, the block is added as its DC. The Intra_8x8 kernel makes the same test of each block
   with a residual (`only_dc8`).
4. **A DC added with saturation.** The residual `r = (d + 32) >> 6`, saturated to 16 bits, gives two byte
   vectors: `r` and `-r`, each clamped to 0 to 255. Added and subtracted with unsigned saturation they give
   `Clip1(p + r)` for every sample `p`: one of the two is 0, and a residual beyond 255 or -255 takes every
   sample to 255 or 0 either way (a saturated 16-bit value keeps its sign and stays beyond that range). For a
   pair the two residuals are spread to each block's four samples of a row by one byte shuffle; four rows
   then cost a load, an add, a subtraction and a store per two rows.

Arm64 and the portable build run the trait's reference bodies: a quadrant's unmarked blocks through
`idct4x4_add_quad`, the marked ones through `idct4x4_dc_add`, and 8x8 blocks through `idct8x8_add` or the
reference's DC addition; they make no test of their own.

Rejected:

- **The decoder marks every DC-only block** (a mask beside `luma_nz`, set where the entropy decoder stores a
  block): measured above, it costs more in the entropy decoder's inner path than the kernel's test, on every
  coded block, and it touches the entropy decoder for a reconstruction change.
- **The test in the Intra_4x4 kernel**: measured, instructions at a median 1.0000 of the build without it,
  22 of 32 streams above, at most 1.0014 (a block there is transformed alone in half a vector, so a skipped
  transform saves little against a test on every block). Intra_8x8's test measured a median 1.0000 of the
  build without it, at most 1.0002 and as low as 0.9973, and stays (`luma-dc/variants/instructions.txt`).
- **A loop over the eight pairs by their bits**: about 30 scalar instructions a pair for its position and
  masks, against the quadrant loop's few.
- **A DC-only pair through `add_residual8` with four equal rows**, the chroma round's path: about twice the
  instructions of the saturating addition.

Prior art: none. The identity is the transforms' equations; the saturating addition is item 4's argument.

Bit-exact by construction and by test: `luma_residual_mb_matches_the_reference` runs both calls through `Simd`
against `Scalar`, and against the residual built block by block from the trait's description (blocks with
coefficients, with a DC alone, with a zero DC, with a DC and one other coefficient, and empty; every kind of
`nz` and `dc` mask; strides from 16; planes that end at the macroblock's last sample), and views of another
size are left unchanged; `intra_kernels_match_the_reference` now has Intra_8x8 blocks with a DC alone. Eleven
mutations of the kernels (the spread shuffle, either test's blend mask, a quadrant's or a block's position, the
marked lane, the negated residual, the rounding, the marked pair's mask, the found DC's lane, the Intra_8x8
DC path) each fail them (`luma-dc/mutations.txt`). A new fuzz target, `luma_residual_mb`, compares `Simd` and `Auto` with `Scalar` for
both calls, with blocks shaped as above. The Miri harness `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/luma-dc/tools/miri`
runs both calls through `Simd` and `Auto` against the reference in planes that start at the macroblock's first
sample and end at its last, from misaligned bases.

Instructions (callgrind, one thread, `--discard`, the first pictures of each of the 32 training streams;
information, not a bar; `luma-dc/instructions.txt`): `k` over `base` 0.9977 at the median, from 0.9839 to
0.9999, every stream fewer.

## Round 23: the CAVLC level loop

Rejected by its bars L-1 and L-2 (the result is at the end): not merged.
The code measured stays on `rejected/h264-cavlc-levels` (at `1a282b6`,
on `main` at `ddb34e9`), with a row in
`docs/measurements/h264-rejected.md`; what follows describes that branch.
Bundle 2 ("Bundle 2: ten small changes together") wrote its design anew
on `cavlc::block_body` and brought it into `main` as item A.

The levels change of round 21 alone, as a new round with its own bars
and a new run. Round 21 measured it inside a round that failed as one
(its E-1 was met, 0.9849 on the six CAVLC streams); that run is not
reused here. The mvd change of round 21 is not part of it.

### What the measurement says

- After round 19 the fused block decoder is still the largest single
  function on the CAVLC streams (round 21, "What the measurement says").
  Per level, the loop read level_prefix, skipped it, chose level_suffix's
  size among three cases, read the suffix, and turned levelCode into a
  level with two branches. Below a prefix of 14, which is nearly every
  level, the suffix's size is suffixLength and levelCode has no other
  term.
- Local, as information (`round23/local/`; a development VM with the bar
  class's CPU, CPU time at one thread pinned, `main` at `75d77dc`,
  before round 22): 0.9865 on the six CAVLC streams over five rounds, five of six faster
  (0.979 to 1.000); over all 32 streams at three rounds, 0.9972, the 26
  CABAC streams, whose code is unchanged, 0.9993.

### Design

As round 21's first part, unchanged (the code of
`rejected/h264-entropy-small`'s `cavlc.rs`, nothing from its `cabac.rs`).
Below a prefix of 14, level_prefix, its terminating one and the
suffixLength bits of level_suffix are read as one field, and one skip
consumes them. levelCode becomes a level without a branch: the magnitude
is levelCode / 2 + 1 for either parity (clause 9.2.2.1), negated where
levelCode is odd. suffixLength's step up is a table by suffixLength. A
prefix of 14 or more goes to an out-of-line function that keeps the
clause's three cases and its checks, unchanged.

Output is unchanged: identical to `main` at `ddb34e9` on the 32 training
streams at one and eight threads (`round23/identity-local.txt`, the
branch merged with that `main`). The unit
tests compare the fused block with the clause-by-clause decoder on

## Kernel round: Intra_4x4 edges in vectors, and level scales built once

### What the measurement says

At 720p and 1080p, where the gap to FFmpeg 9.0.2 is now largest, the profile of `main` at `40f29a6` split by class
(the samples of "Again at `40f29a6`", FFmpeg's functions from a recording of the same attribution build, function
level only; `intra-scales/profile-by-class.txt`) puts the kernels of this area level with FFmpeg's, except intra
prediction. In FFmpeg's total time, 720p then 1080p, CoreAV against FFmpeg:

| Item | 720p | 1080p |
|---|---|---|
| luma deblocking filter (`luma_columns`, `luma_rows`; FFmpeg's four luma filters) | 0.104 against 0.117 | 0.040 against 0.041 |
| chroma deblocking filter (`filter_chroma_mb`; FFmpeg's four chroma filters) | 0.050 against 0.048 | 0.022 against 0.021 |
| 4x4 inverse transforms (`idct4x4_add_quad`; FFmpeg's 4x4 additions) | 0.023 against 0.024 | 0.028 against 0.026 |
| 8x8 inverse transforms | 0.005 against 0.005 | 0.017 against 0.016 |
| intra prediction, Intra_4x4 and Intra_8x8 with their residual (FFmpeg's prediction functions with their luma glue) | 0.038 against 0.019 | 0.021 against 0.013 |
| building the scaling of a QP (`prepare_level_scales`, `CoeffScale::new`) | 0.008 | 0.008 |

The deblocking driver (`deblock_row`, `new`, `edge_strengths`) runs 0.121 against FFmpeg's 0.090 at 720p and 0.077
against 0.058 at 1080p, more than all of these; it is the next round's. The 4x4 transforms are not on top, so the
transposed coefficient layout the luma residual round named stays out of scope, and so does an AVX-512 transform.

Of intra prediction, `intra4x4_mb` is the largest part. On a microbenchmark of a row of macroblocks (not kept; stride 1280,
every neighbour present, random modes) an Intra_4x4 macroblock without residual costs 2,314 instructions in the `dist`
build, 145 a block: each block works out its position and its neighbours' availability (`blk_xy`, `block_avail`,
about 24 instructions), gathers its column left from four byte loads and its line from scalar shifts (about 25), and
writes its rows through four address computations, each with its multiplication. Building the scaling of a QP
happens wherever a macroblock's QP differs from the one before, which under adaptive quantisation is most
macroblocks, for the luma blocks and each chroma component; `LevelScale::new`, the level scales of a slice, runs for
every slice.

### Design

As measured at `914729f` (`intra-scales/k.diff`); the round was rejected and none of it is in `main` (the result below).

1. **Edges in vectors (`x86::intra4x4_mb`).** The kernel keeps each block's prediction, with its residual, in a
   vector of its own (sixteen bytes on the stack), and builds the next blocks' edge lines from those vectors. Every
   neighbour sits in the same bytes of the vector it comes from: a block's bottom row in bytes 12 to 15, its right
   column in bytes 3, 7, 11 and 15, its bottom right sample in byte 15. The samples around the macroblock are put in
   ten vectors of the same layout once, before any block is written: four of the row above (one 16-byte load, shifted),
   the four above and right (a 4-byte load, or p[15, -1] repeated where the macroblock has no top right), four of the
   column left (four 4-byte loads from p[-1, y] each, shifted by three bytes) and p[-1, -1]. A neighbour the macroblock
   lacks is a vector of zeros, which is what the reference predicts from. A constant table gives each luma4x4BlkIdx
   the slots of its four neighbours and its position, and four fixed shuffles OR the line together; a block whose top
   right is decoded after it (clause 6.4.11.4) takes its top neighbour's last sample, repeated, by a fifth shuffle.
   DC sums the line's eight side samples with `psadbw`, a missing side adding zero, and divides by which sides the
   block has (two 16-bit masks per macroblock). Rows are written from one pointer per block. On the microbenchmark
   (not kept) a macroblock takes 102 ns where it took 161 without residual, and 149 where it took 205 with half its
   blocks coded.
2. **Views whose edges overlap the macroblock** go to the reference: reading the edges first is the reference's order
   only where none of those samples lies inside the macroblock, which a stride below 17 breaks for the column left
   (p[-1, y] is then the last sample of row y - 1) and one below 20 for the top right (p[16..19, -1] are then
   samples of row 0). A decoder's picture has neither neighbour at such a stride, its macroblock being the picture's
   width.
3. **Level scales built once per set of lists.** `LevelScale` also holds each list's `CoeffScale` at every QP from 0
   to 51 (`q4`, six lists, and `q8`, two; 50 KB), built in `LevelScale::new` by `CoeffScale::new` itself, and the
   scaling lists it was built from. The worker keeps it in its `Spare` from one slice and picture to the next and
   builds it again only where a slice's picture parameter set has other lists (`LevelScale::is_for`).
   `prepare_level_scales` copies the prebuilt scaling where it built one; for a QP outside 0 to 51, which 8-bit
   decoding never has, it builds it as before.

Rejected:

- **Store-forwarding-friendly reads of the row above** (two 4-byte loads in place of the 8-byte one that spans two
  earlier stores): measured on the microbenchmark, no change; the per-block instructions, not stalls, were the cost.
- **Neighbours from the previous block in registers**: a block's left neighbour is the previous block only for half
  of them in decoding order; slots indexed by a table serve every block alike.
- **Applying the QP's shift as levels are scaled** (the qP % 6 factors alone, and the shift per level): it adds a
  variable shift to every level the entropy decoder stores, against a copy per QP change.
- **The scaling held by reference into `LevelScale`** instead of copied: it saves the copy of 72 or 264 bytes per
  change but changes `CoeffScales` and its readers in the macroblock layer; the copy keeps the change to the level
  scales and their builder.
- **A table built per slice**: 11,648 entries for every slice costs more than the per-macroblock building it replaces
  on sd streams, whose pictures are small.

Prior art: none. The neighbour layout is the clause's own derivation (6.4.11.4) put in a table; the scaling is the
equations of clauses 8.5.12.1 and 8.5.13.1 as `CoeffScale::new` computes them.

Bit-exact by construction and by test: `intra_kernels_match_the_reference` now draws strides 18 and 19 as well (the
top right's boundary) besides 16, 17, 20, 32 and 48, every combination of neighbours, out-of-range modes and every
kind of `nz`; making the fallback's bounds 16 or 19 fails it. `the_scaling_of_every_qp_is_built_from_the_level_scales`
checks every list and QP against `CoeffScale::new` with non-flat lists, and `is_for`;
`a_prebuilt_scaling_is_the_one_built_on_demand` checks `scale_at` from QP -7 to 69 against building on demand. The
fuzz target `intra` compares `Simd` with `Scalar` for `intra4x4_mb`.

Instructions (callgrind, one thread, `--discard`, the first pictures of each of the 32 training streams; information,
not a bar; `intra-scales/instructions.txt`): `k` over `base` 0.9929 at the median, every stream fewer; sd
0.9782, 720p 0.9935, 1080p 0.9937, 4k 0.9961. On `c7ecda16e4a7.0.1080p` `intra4x4_mb` falls by 31% (34.8 to 24.0 million instructions)
and `CoeffScale::new` (4.1 million) goes; on `5185721dda11.0.sd` the slice setup falls by 2.2 million of 10.6 million, and `memset` by 0.5 million, the level
scales no longer built per slice (`intra-scales/functions.txt`).

## Round 24: the macroblock layer's bookkeeping

Not gated, and not merged: on the `main` it would have been measured
against, two local runs did not show the gain its first bar asks for (the
result is at the end). The code stays on `rejected/h264-mb-layer` (at `3535661`, on
`main` at `056bd25`), with a row in `docs/measurements/h264-rejected.md`;
what follows describes that branch.

The MB layer is still the stage furthest from FFmpeg's time ("Again at
`40f29a6`": 1.81 times). Its items are each small, so this round takes
three of them together, in the code every macroblock runs before and
after its syntax: `MbData::reset`, `start_mb` and `finish_mb`.

### What the measurement says

- **Where the time is** (`main` at `e18f85c`, local, perf at one
  thread, `round24/local/perf.txt`): `start_mb` 1.1% to 2.5% of the samples on four training
  streams, `MbData::reset` 1.0% to 1.4%; `finish_mb` is inlined into the
  slice loops. In `start_mb`, the lookups of the four neighbours are
  about a third of its samples, and the rows it asks for ahead
  (round 12) most of the rest.
- **`MbData::reset` clears a coded macroblock's mvd**, 256 bytes, every
  time. Nothing reads them unless the same macroblock wrote them: the
  syntax (`parse_mb_pred`, `parse_sub_mb_pred`) writes mvd_lX of each
  partition and list its prediction mode uses, and the prediction
  (`predict_partitions`, `predict_sub_partitions` in `inter.rs`) reads
  exactly those, by the same modes (Tables 7-13, 7-14, 7-17 and 7-18);
  a direct sub-macroblock reads none.
- **Three of the four neighbours are known already.** Along a row of one
  slice, macroblock A is the last one, and B and D are the last one's C
  and B; the row above does not change while a row is decoded.
- **An intra macroblock's motion was a fill**: sixteen twelve-byte
  values, each stored in two. A copy of all sixteen from a constant
  compiles to a call to `memcpy` (192 bytes).
- Instructions (callgrind, 40 pictures, `round24/local/`): 0.9975,
  0.9858, 0.9956 and 0.9938 of `main` on four streams with a first build
  that copied the intra motion in one `memcpy` call, 0.9848 and 0.9939 on
  two of them with this round's code; most of it in `start_mb` (29.2
  million to 25.4 million on `a81de82106be`).
- Local time, as information (`round24/local/ab.txt`; a development VM
  with the bar class's CPU, CPU time at one thread pinned, five rounds):
  0.9936 over the 32 streams, 31 of them faster (0.984 to 1.001); sd
  0.9925, 720p 0.9950, 1080p 0.9940, 4k 0.9931.

### Design

1. **No mvd clear.** `MbData::reset` no longer clears `mvd`; the comment
   at the reset names the writers and readers it relies on. The other
   fields it clears are unchanged.
2. **Neighbours carried along a row.** When a macroblock follows the
   last one in the same row (the case `start_mb` already finds without
   dividing), A, B and D come from the last macroblock's neighbours and
   only C is looked up; at a row's start, a slice's first macroblock or
   any other address, all four are derived as before. Debug builds
   check the carried neighbours against a full derivation at every
   macroblock.
3. **An intra macroblock's motion in four copies** of a constant row of
   four (48 bytes each, three sixteen-byte stores), which stay inline.

Rejected: storing mvd as `i16` (the range check already bounds them to
that type, but with the clear gone the size matters only to the cache,
and nothing reads more than it wrote); deriving the neighbours once a
row for the whole row (a slice can start inside a row); making
`start_mb` inline into the slice loops (two copies of a large function,
whose compiled instance is the dispatch's choice); a cheaper walk of
the rows asked for ahead, which is the prefetch module's (`prefetch.rs`,
"Motion round: the reference's lines requested ahead, cheaply").

Output is unchanged: identical to `main` at `056bd25` on the 32
training streams at one and eight threads, the branch merged with it
(`round24/identity-local.txt`).

### Bars

Fixed before the A/B run, on the method of round 23:
`scripts/h264_parity.py` on the 2.90 GHz class (`--require-cpu
'Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.90GHz'`), the host gate before and after
each call, the training set at the class frame counts, FFmpeg 9.0.2 last;
a cloud container of that CPU only if no VM passes the gate before the
start, recorded. Two builds alike (`dist`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS`
unset): `main` at the commit this branch is based on when the run starts
(`before`), named in the result, and this branch (`after`). No allocation
changes, so no mapped-allocator call. Two calls per class: `g`, `--pin 2
--rounds 5`; `t8`, `--threads 8`, unpinned, fifteen rounds.

Every bar is over all 32 streams or a whole class, none over a few
streams: in round 23 single streams of the 1080p class moved from 0.84 to

|---|---|---|
| B-1 | one thread (`g`), median per-stream ratio `after` over `before`, discard, all 32 streams | at most **0.997**, upper end of the 95% interval below 1.000 |

### Result: not gated

The bars above were committed on `main` at `e18f85c`, where the local
A/B gave 0.9936. Before the run, `main` moved to `056bd25`, which compiles
`start_mb` and `MbData::reset` (among others) a second time for x86-64-v3
("Kernel round: the hot paths compiled twice, wider"). On that base the
instructions saved are the same (0.9941, 0.9848 and 0.9956 of `main` on
three streams; `start_mb`'s v3 instance 28.1 million to 24.5 million on
`a81de82106be`, `round24/local/instructions.txt`), but the time is not:
two local runs of the same method (`round24/local/ab-056bd25.txt`) gave
0.9969 [0.9953, 1.0030] (20 of 32 faster; 4k 1.0003) and 0.9982
[0.9936, 1.0001] (21 of 32; 1080p 1.0014), with the interval of
`analyze.py`'s bootstrap, against B-1's 0.997 with the upper end of its
interval below 1.000; on `e18f85c` it had been 0.9936 [0.9909, 0.9956].
Neither run on the new base meets B-1 as a whole, so no gating run was
requested: a gating run takes about two hours on the bar-class VM, and
this round requests one only where a local run shows its first bar's
gain. Output on that base:
identical to `main` on the 32 training streams at one and eight threads
(`identity-local.txt`), the same in the default and the safe build
(`modes-identity.txt`), conformance 97 of 97 in every mode
(`conformance.txt`).

What it shows: on the base with the v3 instance, the same instruction
saving no longer showed in time locally, where on `e18f85c` it had; why
was not measured, and single streams moved by up to 4% between the two
runs on the new base (`ae16bb7c7192`, 1.032 and 0.990). A hypothesis for a next round in this stage, not a finding:
that its remaining excess over FFmpeg is more in what the macroblock
layer waits for than in the work it does, which a measurement of stalls
rather than of instructions would test.

## Kernel round: an inter macroblock's 8x8 luma residual in one call

Not queued for a gating run; nothing merges from it
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/luma8x8/`; code on
`rejected/h264-luma8x8-mb` at `1685ba23`). "Kernel round: a macroblock's
luma residual in one call" was rejected by LD-1 and left one lead: the
8x8 path alone, where its time had moved (4k 0.9915). This round is new
code for that lead, not the measured arm of that round.

### Design

`Kernels::luma8x8_residual_mb(dst, coeffs, nz)` adds the 8x8 blocks of an
inter macroblock whose bits of `nz` are set to its 16x16 luma view, one
call where `reconstruct_inter` made up to four. Its default body calls
`idct8x8_add` on each quadrant (Scalar, Neon and the portable build). The
AVX2 kernel (`simd/x86/residual8.rs`) checks the macroblock's sixteen rows
once; for each block it loads the coefficient rows the transform loads
anyway, tests whether any coefficient but the first is set (the rows ORed
with the first lane blended out, one `vptest`), and adds a DC-only block's
`(d + 32) >> 6` with saturating byte arithmetic and no transform: an 8x8
block whose only coefficient is `d` gives `d` at every position before the
final rounding (clause 8.5.13.2). Output identical to `main` on the 32
training streams at 1 and 8 threads; unit tests against the reference,
with nine mutations of the kernel each caught; a fuzz target against
`Scalar`.

### What the local measurement says

Inter 8x8 blocks occur in 15 of the 32 training streams, in 4 of the 8 4k
streams, and DC-only ones in number in one, `f8d92a911e72` (12.8 million
blocks, 51% DC-only; `luma-dc/counts.txt`). Instructions fall by 1.9%
there and by 0.2% to 0.45% on three other streams (`instructions.txt`).
Over the 32 streams, five interleaved rounds (`local-ab.txt`), the median
is 0.9963 [0.9926, 1.0003], with the sd class, where two streams have a
few inter 8x8 blocks, moving as much (0.9958) as 720p (0.9912; four
streams with them, half or more DC-only in three) and more than 4k
(1.0022); the 15 streams with inter 8x8 blocks read 1.0000
[0.9851, 1.0042], and `f8d92a911e72` 1.0042, slower in three of five
rounds. Timed alone with one other stream for ten rounds
(`local-ab-one.txt`), `f8d92a911e72` reads 0.9845, faster in each round,
as its instructions say, and `175433794e02` 1.0080. So the one stream
where the change is large gains when it is timed in a quiet run, and over
the training set the effect is below this host's noise: no bar on all 32
streams, on a class or on the streams the change reaches could be met
with a resolved interval. A gating run is requested only when an
interleaved local timing of the 32 streams shows a gain at the level of
the round's primary bar; this one did not, and the round was not queued.

## Kernel round: Intra_8x8 edges read once per macroblock

### What the measurement says

The per-class profile of `main` at `40f29a6` (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/intra-scales/profile-by-class.txt`) left
Intra_8x8 (`x86::intra8x8_mb`, its residual included) at 0.0073 of FFmpeg 9.0.2's time at 720p and 0.0063 at 1080p,
against about 0.003 for FFmpeg's 8x8 luma prediction, the largest intra item after Intra_4x4 once the chroma round
(after `40f29a6`) is counted. Function-level instruction counts on `914729f`, the Intra_4x4 round's branch (`fb893fd`
plus that change; callgrind, one thread, `--discard`, the first 120 pictures; `intra8-edges/functions.txt`) agree: on
`1d4b1775d78a.0.720p`, Intra_8x8 prediction is 37.0 million instructions for CoreAV against 9.5 million for FFmpeg's
`pred8x8l` functions, chroma intra 19.1 against 4.8 million, Intra_16x16 4.7 against 3.0 million; on
`175433794e02.0.1080p`, 127 against 27 million, 70 against 19 million and 14 against 10 million.

A line-level profile of the 720p stream (line tables, `--dump-instr`; not kept) put most of the kernel's
instructions outside the transform of coded blocks in gathering each block's neighbours: the column left as eight
byte loads with a row multiply each, `intra::block_avail`, the corner and the row above, where the prediction's own
shuffles or DC are a small part. For blocks 1 to 3 every one of those neighbours was written by an earlier block of
the same macroblock a few instructions before, and is read back from memory. Chroma intra gathers its two columns
the same way.

### Design

As measured at `a3e9e9a` (`intra8-edges/k.diff`); the round was withdrawn before its gating run and none of it is in
`main` (the result below).

1. **The macroblock's edges read once.** `x86::intra8x8_mb` reads p[-1, 0..15] (`column16`: one `pinsrb` a
   sample, each address one stride on), p[-1, -1], p[0..15, -1] and p[8..23, -1] before any block, each only where
   the view's flags name it, as the reference zeroes the others.
2. **Inside the macroblock, edges from registers.** Each block's eight rows stay in four vectors after its
   residual is added (`block8x8`). Block 1's column left is block 0's last column (`last_column8`: four `pshufb`
   from a static table and three `or`); block 2's row above and top right are row 7 of blocks 0 and 1 (one
   `punpckhqdq`), its column left the second half of the macroblock's; block 3's row above is row 7 of block 1
   and its column left block 2's last column. The corners are byte 7 of p[0..15, -1] (block 1), p[-1, 7] (block 2)
   and p[7, 7] (block 3).
3. **Availability per block written out.** `block_avail`'s result for an 8x8 block is a fixed function of its
   index and the macroblock's flags (block 0: the macroblock's flags with the top right equal to its top; block 1:
   left always, top and top left where the macroblock has a top, the macroblock's top right; block 2: top and top
   right always, left and top left where the macroblock has a left; block 3: all but the top right). The four
   blocks are written out, so these are constants or copies of the macroblock's flags.
4. **Aliasing views go to `Scalar`.** The reference reads each block's neighbours after the blocks before it are
   written. With a stride under 17 the column left of a row is the last sample of the row before, inside the
   macroblock, and with a stride under 24 the top right of block 1 reaches into the macroblock's first row; there
   the samples read once would be stale. Such views (no picture has one; the decoder's stride is the picture's
   padded width) take `Scalar`, as the Intra_4x4 kernel's narrow views do.
5. **`predict8x8`'s shuffles in a function of their own.** With the four blocks written out, LLVM stopped
   inlining the `map` closure over the two halves of the mode shuffle, and its loads, shuffles and `or`s became
   calls. `shuffle_half`, `#[inline(always)]`, does one half.
6. **The same column read for chroma and Intra_16x16.** `intra_chroma_mb` and `intra16x16` read their columns
   left with `column8` and `column16`. They read every edge before writing, so nothing else changes.

Rejected: keeping the block loop and taking the in-macroblock edges from the previous iteration's vectors (a loop
carried state per block index, which needs the same per-block selections as the written-out form and keeps the
loop's own overhead); reading the column left as eight 64-bit row loads and a transpose (more instructions than
eight inserts for one column); and leaving `block_avail` and computing it once before the loop (written out, the four
calls cost nothing).

Instructions (first pictures of the 32 training streams, callgrind; `instructions.txt`): `k` over `base` median
0.9988, every stream fewer (0.9832 to 0.9998); per class sd 0.9992, 720p 0.9992, 1080p 0.9982, 4k 0.9955. On the first
30 pictures of `1d4b1775d78a.0.720p` (`functions.txt`), 930.7 million less 10.9 million: `intra8x8_mb` 25.7 million
less 9.5 million, `intra_chroma_mb` 12.3 less 1.2 million, `intra16x16` 2.8 less 0.14 million. The gain is small at
the median, since sd streams and many others have little Intra_8x8; the bars below decide whether it ships.

### Bars

Fixed before any timing of `k`, on the method of the Intra_4x4 round: two decoders in the same rounds, built alike
(`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset) from one
tree each, on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106; the run records it, and the script stops on any other host).
`base` is `main` at `fb893fd`; `k` is the branch's code commit `a3e9e9a`, `base`'s tree plus this round's change to
`crates/coreav-kernels-h264/src/simd/x86.rs`. The run is `scripts/h264_parity.py` of the base tree on the training
set, FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference command, each call between two host gates (a failed gate after a call voids it
and it runs again), the class frame counts (sd 1800, 720p 900, 1080p 300, 4k 150): per class, one call at one
thread pinned to core 2 at twenty rounds, and one at eight threads, unpinned, at ten. The gate is the class's own
(`hostgate.py` of `HOST-GATE.md`, unchanged). The script is `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/intra8-edges/run-ab-helper.sh`,
and `analyze.py` beside it prints the bars. The change allocates nothing, so the allocator-placement guard does not

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| IE-1 | median per-stream ratio, `k` over `base`, one thread, discard (the primary) | at most **1.000**, and the upper end of its 95% interval below **1.000** |

| IE-3 | the same per class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |

### Result: withdrawn before the gating run

A local timing A/B (`intra8-edges/local-ab/`: `run.sh`, the reports, `summary.txt`; information, not a bar), on a VM

## Round 25: five small changes together

### What the measurement says

Five changes were each shown correct (identical output on the training
set, conformance, their tests and fuzz targets) and each left out because
its gain alone was below what a run resolves:

- **Round 24's macroblock-layer bookkeeping** (`rejected/h264-mb-layer`
  `3535661`): instructions 0.985 to 0.996 of `main`'s on three streams;
  local timing on `056bd25` 0.9969 and 0.9982, not gated.
- **The inter 8x8 luma residual in one call** (`rejected/h264-luma8x8-mb`
  `1685ba23`): instructions 1.9% fewer on one stream, 0.2% to 0.45% on
  three others; local timing 0.9963 over the 32 streams, not gated.
- **Round 23's CAVLC levels** (`rejected/h264-cavlc-levels` `1a282b6`):
  gated, CAVLC streams 0.9797 and all 32 0.9902, rejected by its
  interval's upper end (one 1080p stream) and 1080p write.
- **Intra_4x4 edges in vectors and level scales built once**
  (`intra-scales/k.diff`, `914729f`): gated, 0.9997 at one thread, sd
  0.9882; rejected by IS-1.
- **Intra_8x8 edges read once per macroblock** (`intra8-edges/k.diff`,
  `a3e9e9a`): withdrawn before its gating run, its local timing showing
  no gain at IE-1's level.

Each takes a different part of the decoder (the macroblock layer, inter
reconstruction, the CAVLC residual, intra reconstruction and the slice
setup), so their gains, if real, add. The rejected-changes ledger asks for
such combinations ("Re-test these after any structural change"); this
round measures the five together once.

### Design

One arm, `bundle`: `main` at `456f1ff` with the five changes applied in
the order above, each as its branch's or diff's change to `crates/` and
`docs/unsafe-sites.md`, and nothing else. The composition is fixed here,
before any timing (the fifth was added to the four first committed, also
before any timing): no part is added or removed after a measurement, and the
round is measured once; its result is final for this combination. Where
`main` had moved under a change, the merge keeps both: round 23's level
loop now sits in `cavlc::block_body` (the body the wider dispatch compiles
twice); the level scales are reused when a slice's picture parameter set
is the one they were built for, and otherwise built through
`Choice::level_scale` in the slice's instance, as `main` builds them; the Intra_4x4 and Intra_8x8 changes to
`simd/x86.rs` touch different kernels and merge without overlap.
