## Motion round: fewer or cheaper requests for the reference's lines

Not queued for a gating run; nothing merges from it
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/request/`; the variants on
`rejected/h264-request-variants` at `ec285f51`). The profile at `6c9e240`
puts `Planes::request`, the hints of "Motion round: the reference's lines
requested ahead, cheaply", at 0.0175 of FFmpeg's time over the 32 streams,
against 0.0134 in FFmpeg's prefetch function, and the measurement of round
24 at 6.6% of the time of the 4k stream `3b1b441e23ae` with a relative IPC
of 0.73 (`mb-stalls/mb-items.txt`). This round asked whether fewer hints, or
cheaper ones, give that time back.

### What the measurement says

- **The time is the wait, not the instructions** (`profile-4k.txt`, `main`
  at `056bd25`, whose crates are `3d60f0bf`'s). A call costs 317 to 329
  instructions for its 32 hints, 16 luma rows and 8 of each chroma plane
  (27,066 calls on 30 pictures of the 720p stream `1d4b1775d78a`, 158,558
  on 30 of `3b1b441e23ae`). On `3b1b441e23ae` (2400x1500) 54% of the
  function's samples sit on the instruction after the luma walk's
  `prefetcht0` and 13% after the chroma walks': a hint waits there for the
  memory system to take it, the 16 luma rows being 16 lines 2,400 bytes
  apart, in about ten pages.
- **That wait is the round's gain, moved earlier** (`screen1.txt` to
  `screen3.txt`; local CPU time at one thread pinned, five interleaved
  rounds over the 24 streams of the 720p, 1080p and 4k classes, the sd
  class asking for nothing; the control a build of the same branch with
  no variant). No variant gains beyond the local noise, which two builds
  of the same logic put at about half a percent (`screen2.txt`, `oldbase`,
  screen 1's control built again: 720p 0.9949, 1080p 1.0034); spreading
  the hints loses at 4k with an interval above 1.000.

| Variant | All 24 | 720p | 1080p | 4k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a lean walk: the last row's index checked once, then an unrolled loop with no check a row, and one position check (and a row bound) for the three planes; the walk is shared, so the destination's write hints take it too (`lean`) | 1.0005 [0.994, 1.004] | 0.9932 | 1.0004 | 1.0088 |
| the same hints spread over the four macroblocks, a quarter of the rows each (`spread`) | 1.0185 [1.011, 1.034] | 1.0069 | 1.0149 | 1.0557, 0 of 8 faster |
| spread, and 128 samples ahead (`spreadfar`) | 1.0071 [0.998, 1.024] | 1.0044 | 1.0110 | 1.0073 |
| spread and lean (`spreadlean`) | 1.0144 [1.005, 1.026] | 1.0027 | 1.0119 | 1.0392 |
| asked for after the block's prediction, not before (`after`) | 1.0117 [1.000, 1.020] | 1.0084 | 1.0081 | 1.0206 |
| 128 samples ahead (`d128`) | 0.9991 [0.996, 1.002] | 0.9999 | 1.0009 | 0.9952 |
| 192 samples ahead (`d192`) | 1.0041 [0.999, 1.008] | 1.0026 | 1.0017 | 1.0051 |
| lean, 128 ahead (`lean128`) | 0.9991 [0.998, 1.011] | 0.9994 | 1.0012 | 0.9988 |
| the hints to the second level (`prefetcht1`, `t1`) | 0.9997 [0.997, 1.003] | 1.0030 | 0.9984 | 0.9960 |
| half the chroma hints: every eighth macroblock, a chroma line ahead (`c8`) | 1.0016 [0.999, 1.006] | 1.0044 | 1.0023 | 1.0006 |

The lean walk takes 29% of the function's instructions away (8.59 to 6.11
million on 30 pictures of `1d4b1775d78a`; 0.27% of the decode's, 0.57%
with the destination's hints) and no time. Spreading the hints, which
issues three quarters of them one to three macroblocks later, loses at 4k
(1.056 and 1.039, intervals above 1.000; 128 samples ahead it is level),
and asking after the block, which puts them behind the block's own loads,
reads 1.021 there, unresolved. 64 samples ahead is as good as any distance
tried (128 is level, 192 reads 1.004, no better), the cache level makes no
difference (`prefetcht1` is level), and the chroma hints that repeat a
line asked for four macroblocks before cost nothing measurable. This round
registered no bar; a round here would aim at the 4k class, where the
earlier round's bar (MA-3) asked 0.975, and the best variant reads 0.9952
there, inside the noise. A gating run is requested only when an
interleaved local timing shows a gain at that level; none did, and the
round was not queued.

What it leaves: the function's share of the profile is the price of the
misses it moves forward, and FFmpeg pays a like one (its prefetch function
and the C function that calls it, 0.0134 and 0.0071 of its time). The
gap in reference fetch sits in the kernels, not the requests: `luma_block`
and `chroma_block` hold 0.10 and 0.08 of the samples on `3b1b441e23ae`
(`profile-4k.txt`), and the misses that remain there are the likely
cause.

## The reference hints against FFmpeg's prefetch: stall or issue

The PMU profile at `dd85b381` put CoreAV's `prefetch::for_rows` at 2 to 3 times the cycles of FFmpeg's
`ff_prefetch_*` a macroblock (39.8 against 15.3 at 4k, both callers together). The round above had judged that time
to be memory wait moved ahead of the reads. A run with stall events on Compute Engine checked that at function level
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/prefetch-stalls/`, rules committed before each run).

- **Split by caller.** The reference hints (`rows_for_read`) issue about FFmpeg's instructions at 720p and 4k (67.5
  against 67.7 a macroblock at 4k; 1.55 times at 1080p) at 1.07, 1.65 and 1.40 times its cycles (720p, 1080p, 4k).
  The output hints (`rows_for_write`, `request_destination`) are a cost FFmpeg shows no function for: 14 to 21 cycles
  a macroblock.
- **Less than half stall.** Cycles with nothing executing are 0.22 to 0.25 of the reference hints' cycles and 0.37
  to 0.40 of the output hints'; FFmpeg's, 0.07 to 0.12. The rest overlap other work, which can include a hint waiting
  for a fill buffer while later instructions run. CoreAV's hints find the fill buffers full 3.5 to 6.6 cycles a
  macroblock against FFmpeg's 0.06 to 0.59, for as many hints issued over the decode.
- **The rule.** The excess of the cycles that are not stall cycles (X, output hints counted whole) cleared 0.75% of
  the class's cycles at 4k only (12.0 against 9.6 a macroblock), so a part-only probe followed.
- **The probe.** It added 5 one-uop instructions after every hint, the straight walk's predicted cut. Result: 4k
  **1.0209 [1.0075, 1.0335]**; the sd null control 0.9980. The rule was met, so the cut was built.
- **The cut (C).** Once the last row's index is checked, hints for 16, 8, 4 and 2 rows go straight from the first
  row's address: about 1.7 instructions a hint against 7, and 3.0% fewer instructions on a 4k stream. Result: 4k
  **0.9938 [0.9799, 1.0064]**, all 32 0.9989. It is not queued and stays on `rejected/h264-prefetch-straight` as a
  bundle candidate. Bundle 3 carried it and was rejected ("Bundle 3: one thread's inter prediction at 1080p and
  4k").

So the question is closed: the hints' instructions cost more when added than they return when removed. What is left
of the excess over FFmpeg is the output hints, and cycles that overlap other work, where the hints meet full fill
buffers far more often than FFmpeg's do; that the fill buffers are the cause is likely but not measured here. The
hints' count and placement were the round above's variants, none of which gained beyond the noise.

## Deblocking round: thresholds by average QP, and only live edges

The deblocking driver (`deblock.rs`: `deblock_row` with what it inlines, `Thresholds::new`, `edge_strengths`), the
largest item of the 720p and 1080p ranking that has no kernel behind it: CoreAV 0.121 of FFmpeg 9.0.2's total at 720p
against FFmpeg's 0.090 for the same work (its strength routine, its filter caches, its loop-filter driver and border
copies), and 0.077 against 0.058 at 1080p (`intra-scales/profile-by-class.txt` on `measured/h264-intra-scales`).

### What the measurement says

- On `1d4b1775d78a.0.720p` (120 pictures, callgrind, `main` at `fb893fd`) the driver, kernels excluded, runs 406
  million instructions, 14.5% of the decode and about 940 a macroblock. No line dominates: per source line (inlined
  frames folded to the innermost line of `deblock.rs`), the thresholds and the kernel parameters (`Thresholds::new`,
  `params`) take about 80 million, the loops over the eight luma edge slots and their tests of bS 0 about 37 million,
  the strengths about 70 million, and the slice's offsets, clamped again for every macroblock, 4 million.
- Two lookups and a clamp give each edge's thresholds: `Offsets::new` per macroblock, then `BY_INDEX_A` and
  `BY_INDEX_B` by the average QP plus each offset, and α set to 0 where β' is. Every input but the average is the
  slice's, and the slices of a picture almost always share their offsets.
- The luma loop walks all eight edge slots of a macroblock that has any edge to filter, most of them bS 0 on inter
  content.

### Design

As measured at `e2bc974` (`deblock-driver/k.diff`); the round was rejected (the result below). Bundle 2 ("Bundle 2:
ten small changes together") brought point 1, the table by average QP, into `main` as item F, rewritten on an earlier change's
`Thresholds`; point 2, the live-edge masks, was not taken.

1. **A table of thresholds by average QP** (`ThresholdTable`): the 64 `Thresholds` of one pair of filter offsets,
   entry `a` what `Thresholds::new` gives for an average QP `a`, rebuilt only where a macroblock's slice brings another
   pair; an edge's thresholds are one lookup by `(qp_p + qp_q + 1) >> 1`, masked to six bits (every average the filter
   forms is 0 to 51). The decoder keeps the table in `Spare`, boxed, from one call of the filter and one picture to the
   next: kept in `PictureWork` by value, it made each picture's state 1 KiB larger, and the moves of that state cost
   more instructions on sd than the table saved (0.35% more on `6f7799768413.0.sd`, in malloc and memcpy).
2. **Only the live edges.** Per direction, a four-bit mask of the edges whose word is not 0; the loop takes its set
   bits, and the left or upper neighbour's QP is read only for edge 0.

Bit-exact by construction: the table's entries are `Thresholds::new`'s, and a test compares the table with it at
every QP pair and at offsets in the order slices could bring them, a pair repeated after another. The order of the
edges a macroblock filters is unchanged. First-picture instructions (callgrind, 32 training streams,
`deblock-driver/instructions.txt`): median 0.9923, 29 of 32 fewer; sd 0.9964 (highest 1.0021), 720p 0.9889, 1080p
0.9943, 4k 0.9922.

Rejected, measured on three streams: one lookup for a macroblock's internal edges, reused across the loop (0.76% more
instructions on `6f7799768413.0.sd`, the struct kept on the stack across the loop); the original loop over all eight
slots with the table (0.9% more instructions than the live-edge loop on `1d4b1775d78a.0.720p`). Not tried here: one
kernel call for a macroblock's luma edges, as chroma has (a kernel change, for a later round), and the strengths in
vectors.

### Bars

Fixed before any timing of `k`, on the method of the Intra_4x4 and level-scale round: two decoders in the same
rounds, built alike (`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS`
unset) from one tree each, on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106; the run records it, and the script stops on any
other host). `base` is `main` at `fb893fd`; `k` is the branch's code commit `e2bc974`, `base`'s tree plus this round's
change to `deblock.rs`, `mb.rs` and `work.rs` of `crates/coreav-h264`. The run is `scripts/h264_parity.py` of the
base tree on the training set, FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference command, each call between two host gates (a failed gate
after a call voids it and it runs again), the class frame counts (sd 1800, 720p 900, 1080p 300, 4k 150): per class,
one call at one thread pinned to core 2 at twenty rounds, and one at eight threads, unpinned, at ten. The script is
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/deblock-driver/run-ab-helper.sh`, and `analyze.py` beside it prints the bars. The change
adds one allocation per decoding worker (the boxed table, 1 KiB), none per picture.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| DD-1 | median per-stream ratio, `k` over `base`, one thread, discard (the primary) | at most **1.000**, and the upper end of its 95% interval below **1.000** |
| DD-2 | the same, write | at most **1.000** |
| DD-3 | the same per class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| DD-4 | the median over the 32 streams at eight threads, discard and write | at most **1.005** (per class, information) |
| DD-5 | output | the 32 training streams byte-identical to `base` with `k` at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads and with scalar kernels, on `k` |

The change ships if `k` meets DD-1 to DD-5; otherwise this section records the result and the change stays out. One
run decides: a re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a recorded host fault. The ratio to FFmpeg 9.0.2 and the
share of streams faster than it, overall and per class, for both builds, are reported as information, each naming its
build's commit; the 720p and 1080p classes are the ones the round aims at.

### Result: rejected, by DD-4

`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/deblock-driver/gating/` (`README.md`, `analysis.txt`, the reports, `identity.txt`,
`hostgate.log`, `provenance.txt`; branch `measured/h264-deblock-driver-gating` `e26e8a0`): one run of

before-check (of `t8.1080p`), which waited and then passed, and three after-checks that voided their calls (`g.1080p`

| Bar | Result | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| DD-1, 1 thread (20 rounds), discard | 0.9948 [0.9895, 0.9989], 22 of 32 faster: met | at most 1.000, upper end below 1.000 |
| DD-2, 1 thread, write | 0.9944 [0.9907, 0.9976], 25 of 32: met | at most 1.000 |

The change stays out, as the bars say; `deblock-driver/k.diff` holds the code measured (`git diff fb893fd e2bc974`

Against FFmpeg 9.0.2 on that host (median per-stream ratio, `base` then `k`, share of streams where CoreAV is

## CABAC round: the rangeLPS tables in half the lines, a probe

Not queued for a gating run; nothing merges from it
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cabac-compact/`). The profile against FFmpeg
at `6c9e240` leaves entropy decoding 0.031 of FFmpeg's time behind, the
second largest stage gap. The ledger already holds the decision chain in
assembly, with BMI2 and with the offset at a fixed bit position, branch-free
significance maps and levels, both next rows loaded ahead, the two tables as
one table of pairs, and context states held in registers for mvd and the
level prefix. This probe takes the one lever those left: the tables' cache
footprint. Round 27 put the chain's excess time at the `LPS_NORM` load and
the state store, with simulated L1 read misses at the table loads, and the
table of pairs, which doubled the lines touched, cost 1.5%.

1. **Where the instructions are** (`lines.txt`; `lines.py` and `groups.py`
   over callgrind of `main` built with line tables, 100 frames of
   `a81de82106be`, 200 of `1d4b1775d78a`). The decision chain (`cabac.rs`
   190 to 216) is 15.6% of the 1080p-class CABAC stream's instructions and
   7.8% of the 720p one's. Every other CABAC part is below 2.2% on either
   stream: the level loop's own lines 2.15%, the significance map's 1.83%,
   consume and refill 1.87%, bypass 1.84%, `syntax.rs` 1.1% and 2.0%, the
   unary, table and mvd glue 0.7% and 1.0% (each plus the standard library
   lines inlined into it, counted under their own files).
2. **The tables indexed by `(state << 2) + (codIRange >> 6)`**
   (`rejected/h264-cabac-compact` `9ea78b2e`). The quarter `codIRange >> 6`
   is 4 to 7; added to `state << 2` rather than or-ed into `state << 3`, a
   state's four entries sit next to the next state's, so the live part of
   `LPS` is 512 bytes and of `LPS_NORM` 1 KB, half the lines, with the same
   instructions on the chain (cachegrind counts
   0.1% to 0.5% fewer in all, from the compiler's code around the loads, not
   examined). Output identical, 32 of 32 at one and eight
   threads (`identity.txt`). Cachegrind with the host's L1 (48 KB, 12-way;
   `cachegrind.txt`): instructions 0.52%, 0.24% and 0.09% fewer on the
   1080p, 720p and 4k streams, L1 read misses 2.2%, 2.0% and 0.7% fewer.
   Local timing (`ab.txt`; a development VM of the 2.90 GHz class, five
   interleaved rounds, one thread pinned, the 32 streams): **1.0001
   [0.994, 1.015]**, 16 of 32 faster; sd 0.9884, 720p 1.0030, 1080p 1.0126,
   4k 1.0185.

The misses removed did not show in time, so the table loads' misses are not
what holds the chain; likely its latency is the arithmetic from one
decision's range to the next. (The table of pairs' 1.5% loss is then more
likely its larger table evicting other data than the chain's own misses.)
With the chain's instruction cuts also neutral in time (the assembly round,
0.9995) and no other CABAC part near 1.5% of a stream's instructions, no
CABAC round is queued.

## Kernel round: the 8x8 path at 4k and a per-macroblock call, a probe

Not built; nothing merges from it (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/luma8x8-probe/`). "Kernel round: a
macroblock's luma residual in one call" left one lead, the per-macroblock call with the 8x8 DC-only test
(4k 0.9915 in that run), and "an inter macroblock's 8x8 luma residual in one call" then measured no gain
over the training set. Before writing a third version, this probe bounds what such a round can remove,
against the threshold "Why the MB layer's instruction cuts move little time" sets: a round of plain
instructions shows at its bars only if it removes about 1.5% of the instructions of the streams of the
classes it touches.

Callgrind of `main` built with line tables (the decoder code the profile at `6c9e240` measured), one
thread, `--discard`, 240, 120, 60 and 30 pictures by class, all 32 training streams (`cg.sh`, `edges.py`,
`bound.py`; `bound.txt`). Per stream, as shares of its instructions: the inter 8x8 transforms
(`idct8x8_add`, called only from `reconstruct_inter`), the glue (the self instructions of
`reconstruct_inter` and `residual_4x4_luma`, with all they inline: the block offsets, the views, the
dispatch, and the macroblock's other code there), the 4x4 pairs and Intra_8x8. The bound gives the round
all of the glue, more than a per-macroblock call can remove (it still makes one view and steps over the
blocks), and 80% of the transforms of the DC-only share of 8x8 blocks (`luma-dc/counts.txt`), leaving a
fifth for the test and the DC addition (an allowance, not a measurement; the earlier rounds' DC path is a
few instructions a row). The 4x4 pairs and Intra_8x8 are listed, not counted: the DC-only path for 4x4
pairs is the other lead the luma-dc round left (with a cheaper 4x4 transform), and the Intra_8x8 test
measured a median 1.0000 of the instructions there.

| Class | bound, median | largest | streams at 1.5% or more |
|---|---|---|---|
| sd | 0.46% | 0.84% | 0 of 8 |
| 720p | 0.79% | 0.96% | 0 of 8 |
| 1080p | 0.96% | 1.33% | 0 of 8 |
| 4k | 0.40% | 3.01% | 1 of 8 |

Over the 32 streams the bound's median is 0.73%. It holds against what was built: the inter 8x8 round
removed 1.9% of `f8d92a911e72`'s instructions (bound 3.01%) and 0.45%, 0.35% and 0.19% of
`175433794e02`, `1d4b1775d78a` and `b41f70a7fa60`'s (bounds 1.32%, 0.96% and 0.90%). The DC-only shares
are the class frame counts', the instructions the first pictures'; with every inter 8x8 block taken as
DC-only, the class medians are still 0.52%, 0.87%, 1.44% and 0.51%.

Inter 8x8 blocks are where the 8x8 transform's time is at 4k, and they are in 4 of the 8 4k streams; one,
`f8d92a911e72`, holds nearly all of them: 2.19 million transforms in 30 pictures, 4.48% of its
instructions (207 a transform under Valgrind, which runs the AVX2 kernels), the glue 1.18% (55 a block,
at most) and half the blocks DC-only, a bound of 3.01%. The next 4k streams with inter 8x8 blocks are
0.92% (`af38b0cfd840`) and 0.24%; the glue alone gives `4b54de28c2b3` 1.15%. Even with the inter 8x8
transform removed outright, 3 of 32 streams would lose 1.5% or more (`175433794e02` 4.65%,
`f8d92a911e72` 4.48%, `6e90422a670a` 3.37%) and the 4k median nothing, so a faster transform (16-bit
lanes, as the specification's range for 8-bit samples allows) cannot reach a class bar either. In time,
the profile at `6c9e240` has reconstruction at 4k at 0.66 of FFmpeg's; the 4k gap is the MB layer (1.67)
and deblocking (1.28).

The luma-dc round's 4k reading, 0.9915 [0.9873, 0.9943], is several times what its 4k instruction
cuts (a median of 0.27%, 0.10% to 1.61%; `luma-dc/instructions.txt`) give at the threshold's rate of about
half; the inter 8x8 round's local timing read
4k 1.0022, and `f8d92a911e72` 1.0042, over the full set. It is taken as that run's noise, not as a gain a
4k-class bar would see again. So no round on the 8x8 path or the per-macroblock call is built: no class
reaches the threshold even with the bound's allowances, and the 4k median bound is 0.40%, under a third
of it. The lead stays recorded for a corpus or class with many DC-only 8x8 blocks; for the training set,
the gap at 4k is elsewhere.

## Kernel round: chroma intra prediction from one view of both planes

Not queued for a gating run; nothing merges from it (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/intra-chroma/`; code on
`rejected/h264-intra-chroma` at `b9824c9`, kept for a later bundle).

The chroma intra kernel (`x86::intra_chroma_mb`, both components' prediction and residual in one call) is the
largest intra item against FFmpeg 9.0.2 at 720p: 0.0132 of FFmpeg's total against 0.0042 for FFmpeg's 8x8 chroma
predictions; 0.0053 against 0.0020 at 1080p, 0.0041 against 0.0016
at sd, 0.0052 against 0.0019 at 4k (`intra-chroma/probe/items-recon-by-class.txt`, function names only; DC is
FFmpeg's largest chroma mode in every class, `ff-pred-modes.txt`).

### What the measurement says

- **What one call costs in place.** A probe build that makes the call twice (with the two views built twice; the
  kernel is idempotent, so the output is the same) against `main` at `fc2521a`, five interleaved rounds over the 32
  training streams, one thread pinned (`probe/plan.txt`, written before the run; `ab.txt`, `ab-classes.txt`): the
  second call adds 2.65% at 720p (streams from 0.9895 to 1.0523), 1.51% at 1080p, 0.91% at sd and 0.90% at 4k, 1.12%
  over the 32 (streams from 0.9844 to 1.0523, 7 of 32 faster). The same probe for `intra16x16` reads 0.9980, so
  Intra_16x16 has no round of its own and is not changed here.
- **Where the call's time goes** (AVX2 tier; the AVX-512 tier has no intra kernels). In a perf annotation of the
  kernel on `main` at `23b45d4` (`probe/ann-chroma.txt`, 189 samples, so coarse), 20.6% of its samples sit on the
  instruction after the load of the two views' flags: the caller builds each `IntraAvail` with byte and word stores
  and the kernel compares the two as one wider load (`b.avail == r.avail`), which cannot be forwarded from those
  stores. Per instruction (callgrind, `probe/instr-*.txt`, four streams), a call runs the two views' checks and that
  comparison, then gathers each plane's column left with sixteen byte loads, shifts and `or`s for every mode,
  vertical included, before the prediction, the residual and the stores; on `main` at `b6a0bc6` a call is 322
  instructions on `1d4b1775d78a` (`instructions.txt`).

### Design

As measured at `b9824c9` (`intra-chroma/k.diff`) (the result below). Bundle 2 ("Bundle 2: ten small changes together") brought it into `main` as item B.

1. **One view of both planes.** `ChromaIntraMut::new(cb, cr, offset, stride, avail)` computes the range once (the
   same computation as `IntraMut::new`, now one function, `intra_range`) and takes the same range of each plane;
   `Kernels::intra_chroma_mb(dst, ...)` takes it in place of two `IntraMut`. A picture's chroma planes share their
   offset, stride and neighbours, so nothing the decoder could pass is lost; the reference, `Scalar` and the other
   tiers split it into the two `IntraMut` (`into_parts`) and run as before.
2. **The flags as one byte.** The view keeps `IntraAvail::bits`, so its constructor stores one byte and the kernel
   loads that byte; no comparison of the two planes' flags is left.
3. **One check in the kernel.** `x86::IntraRows::pair` checks, as `IntraRows::of` does for one view, that the
   block's rows and every neighbour the flags name lie inside the shorter of the two slices (both are the same range
   of their plane), and gives each plane's `IntraRows`.
4. **The column left by inserts.** `column8` puts p[-1, 0..7] into the high half of the edge vector with eight
   `pinsrb`, each from one byte load, where the row above is one `movq`.
5. **Each mode reads its own edges.** Horizontal reads the column alone, vertical the row alone; DC and plane read
   both, as before. The predictions themselves (`predict_chroma`, `plane_parameters`) are unchanged.

Rejected: keeping two `IntraMut` and comparing their flags field by field (removes the stall but keeps two range
checks in the caller and two in the kernel); passing the flags beside the views as an argument (a second source of
the flags the kernel would have to trust, where the view ties them to the range it checked); and reading the column
as eight row loads and a transpose (more instructions than eight inserts for one column, as the Intra_8x8 round
found).

### Bars

Fixed before any timing of `k`, on the method of the Intra_8x8 round: two decoders in the same rounds, built alike
(`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset) from one
tree each, on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106; the run records it, and the script stops on any other host).
`base` is `main`, the commit the branch is based on; `k` is the branch's code commit, `base`'s tree plus this
round's change to the kernels crate and `recon.rs`. The run is `scripts/h264_parity.py` of the base tree on the
training set, FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference command, each call between two host gates (a failed gate after a call
voids it and it runs again), the class frame counts (sd 1800, 720p 900, 1080p 300, 4k 150): per class, one call at
one thread pinned to core 2 at twenty rounds, and one at eight threads, unpinned, at ten. The gate is the class's
own (`hostgate.py` of `HOST-GATE.md`, unchanged). The script is
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/intra-chroma/run-ab-helper.sh`, and `analyze.py` beside it prints the bars. The
change allocates nothing, so the allocator-placement guard does not apply.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| IC-1 | median per-stream ratio, `k` over `base`, one thread, discard (the primary) | at most **1.000**, and the upper end of its 95% interval below **1.000** |
| IC-2 | the same, write | at most **1.000** |
| IC-3 | the same per class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| IC-4 | the median over the 32 streams at eight threads, discard and write | at most **1.005** (per class, information) |
| IC-5 | output | the 32 training streams byte-identical to `base` with `k` at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads and with scalar kernels, on `k`; the Miri harness over `intra_chroma_mb` and the `chroma_mb` fuzz target clean |

The change ships if `k` meets IC-1 to IC-5; otherwise this section records the result and the change stays out. One
run decides: a re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a recorded host fault. The ratio to FFmpeg 9.0.2 and the
share of streams faster than it, overall and per class, for both builds, are reported as information, each naming
its build's commit.

A gating run is requested only after a local interleaved timing shows IC-1's gain: `base` and `k` in the same
rounds, one thread pinned, six rounds over the 32 training streams at the class frame counts, discard; the request
is made if the median over the 32 is at most 1.000 with the upper end of its bootstrap 95% interval below 1.000.
Otherwise the change, if correct, waits on a `rejected/` branch for a later bundle.

### Result: not queued

The local timing (`intra-chroma/local-ab/`: `plan.txt`, written before the run, `ab.txt`, `ab-classes.txt`;
information, not a bar), on a VM of the bar class (Intel Xeon @ 2.90 GHz, family 6, model 106), `base` = `main` at
`b6a0bc6` and `k` = `b9824c9`, six interleaved rounds over the 32 training streams, one thread pinned, discard, CPU
time: `k` over `base` 0.9986 [0.9969, 1.0030], 17 of 32 faster; per class sd 0.9995, 720p 0.9961, 1080p 0.9973, 4k
1.0072. `9db41aa16b5a`, where the probe's second call cost 5.2%, reads 0.9826. The upper end of the interval is
above 1.000, so the request rule is not met and the round was not queued; IC-1 to IC-4 were not measured, so the
round neither met nor missed them. The code is on `rejected/h264-intra-chroma` (`b9824c9`; `k.diff`) for a later
bundle.

What the change does to the work is clear (`instructions.txt`, callgrind, the first 150 pictures of
`1d4b1775d78a.0.720p`): 74,656 calls, the kernel's instructions 24.05 million to 15.22 million (322 to 204 a call),
`reconstruct_chroma`'s own 33.4 million to 31.2 million, the decode 0.38% fewer. Output is identical to `base` on
the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads (`identity.txt`). The probe priced a whole call (2.65% at 720p); the
change removes a part of it, a third of its instructions and the flag stall, and the residual, the stores of both
blocks and the predictions stay. The timing does not resolve that part: the 720p median reads 0.9961 with an
interval that includes 1.000, the 4k median 1.0072, and the 32 together 0.9986. The probe does not say how a call's
time divides between the parts it removes and the parts it keeps, so a later round on this kernel needs that split
(for example a probe that doubles only the part it would remove) before it is built.

### For later probes: what a doubled call prices

A probe that makes a call twice prices the whole call in place, and only that: it says neither how the call's time
divides between the work a change would remove and the work it keeps, nor in which direction the doubled call is off
(a second call finds its edges and rows in L1, which makes it cheaper than the first; it also repeats the first
call's stalls and stores). So it bounds no cut smaller than the whole call. Here it priced the call at 2.65% at
720p, and removing a third of the instructions and the flag stall moved the 720p median to 0.9961, not resolved. A
probe that is to decide whether a partial change is built doubles, or skips where the output allows, only the part
the change removes, and its bar is set against that part.

## MB layer: a layout that stores only what later stages read, a probe

The MB layer is the largest gap left against FFmpeg (0.078 of its time at one thread, 1.73 times; at 4k 1.67), and
seven single fixes to it did not show in time ("Why the MB layer's instruction cuts move little time", "Stalls at the
macroblock record, moved not removed", "Where the stores go"): the layer is bound by its store traffic, and a stall
removed at one store surfaced at the next. This probe bounds a structural change instead, before building it
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/mb-layout-probe/`; `plan.txt` fixed the bound and the threshold before the run).

The layout in view stores only what later stages read: a compact record (the fields deblocking and the neighbours'
availability read in the picture-sized array, those only neighbours read in a ring of about one macroblock row), a 16-byte head a
macroblock (its motion, and whether its sixteen blocks are stored; an intra one's holds no motion) where the sixteen
entries are written only by a macroblock with more than one motion (readers resolve them through one accessor), no clearing of
per-macroblock state beyond what the next macroblock reads, and the co-located motion read from that compact form.
Its removed set R is the record copy and an intra macroblock's motion fill (`finish_mb`), the record's
initialisation in `start_mb`, `store_mb` and the picture-motion writes of `store_motion`, and `MbData::reset`; C is
`colocated`.

Method: `main` with line tables, the AVX2 kernels in both runs so that sampled and simulated runs execute the same
instructions, one thread, the class frame counts, all 32 training streams; perf `cpu-clock` (five runs a stream,
pinned) against callgrind with the host's L1 simulated, per source line. The bound per stream, in % of its time,
is generous on purpose: all of R's instructions; the larger of R's own excess (time share less instruction share)
and R's share of the simulated L1 write misses times the excess of every line that stores, since a store's wait
surfaces wherever the next store is; and all of C's excess.

| Class | bound, median | range | without the share of other lines | streams at 1.5% or more |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sd | 6.09% | 4.24% to 12.63% | 5.85% | 8 of 8 |
| 720p | 6.50% | 5.69% to 9.29% | 5.03% | 8 of 8 |
| 1080p | 6.31% | 5.12% to 8.66% | 3.57% | 8 of 8 |
| 4k | 11.38% | 3.62% to 15.26% | 11.38% | 8 of 8 |

Where it sits (`bound.txt`): the record copy in `finish_mb` (excess 0.3% to 6.8% of a stream's time, 4.1% to 6.8% on
five of the 4k streams) and `store_mb` (0.2% to 3.9%), then `MbData::reset` (0.2% to 0.9%) and
`colocated` (up to 1.5%); R's instructions are 1.1% to 4.3%. R stores 340 to 1,640 bytes a macroblock of the
decoder's 2.1 to 13.2 KB, but 3.3 of its 11 to 15 simulated L1 write misses (3.8 of 39 on `f8d92a911e72`): nearly
every macroblock writes the three lines of its sixteen motion entries, an intra one included, and the records add
about a third of a line. With the head alone for the one-motion macroblocks (a median 0.78 to 0.95 of them by class, from the bytes
of `store_mb`'s copy of rows 1 to 3) and the intra ones, those write a quarter of a line where they wrote three (16
bytes, four heads a line, where 13 would do: aligned, a head never straddles two lines).
`colocated`'s own lines store 15 to 130 bytes a macroblock on the 17 streams where it runs, on the stack.

The bound clears an earlier change's threshold, applied to time as `plan.txt` sets it, in every class and on every stream, by a
wide margin, also without the share of other lines' excess. It is an upper bound: it takes every stall at R's lines
as removable, where the earlier fixes moved such stalls rather than removed them, and counts all of `MbData::reset`,
whose coefficient clears the layout keeps (without it the medians without other lines' share are 4.65%, 4.15%,
2.68% and 11.03%); the round's own bars decide what
is reached. So the layout is the next MB-layer round, built and timed against bars fixed before its run.

## MB layer round: only what later stages read

The probe above bounds this round at 3.6% to 11.4% of the time by class (medians, without the share of other lines'
stalls). Unlike the single fixes before it, it removes stores rather than moving them: the lines a macroblock writes
that were last touched a picture ago.

### Design

As measured at `e480d9cc` (`rejected/h264-mb-layout`); the round was not queued and none of it is in `main` (the
result below).

1. **The record split.** `MbInfo`, the per-picture record array (`PictureWork::mbs`, allocated and filled each
   picture), keeps what is read beyond the macroblock's neighbours A and B: `slice` (availability, deblocking), `kind`
   (availability under constrained intra prediction, contexts, deblocking), `qp`, `t8x8`, `nz` and `uniform`
   (deblocking), 12 bytes where it held about 60. What only A and B read (`cbp`, `chroma_mode`, `ref_gt0`,
   `intra_edge`, `cbf`, `entropy`) is `NbInfo`, 48 bytes, kept in a ring of `next_power_of_two(mb_w + 1)` entries
   indexed by `addr & mask`: A (`addr - 1`) and B (`addr - mb_w`) are among the last `mb_w + 1` addresses, so their
   entries are not overwritten before they are read. A neighbour is read only where it is available, so in the same
   slice and decoded before by the same `SliceDecoder`; its entry is then the one its `finish_mb` wrote, whatever an
   earlier slice or picture left in the rest of the ring. The ring is kept with `MbData` across slices and pictures
   (`Spare`), and at 4k is 12 KB, which stays in L1 and L2, where the record array's lines were last written a picture
   ago.
2. **A motion head a macroblock.** Each band keeps `heads`, one `MbHead { m: Motion, split }` a macroblock beside the
   sixteen `Motion` entries. A head that is not split stands for all sixteen blocks, and the entries are not written:
   `store_mb` (one motion: P_Skip, one partition, direct with equal quadrants, 0.78 to 0.95 of the macroblocks by
   class) and intra macroblocks (`NO_MOTION`) write 16 bytes instead of 192. A macroblock with more than one motion
   writes its entries as before, and its head marks them. `finish_mb` writes every decoded macroblock's head, and
   `clear_macroblock`, `fill_black` and `conceal_from` write the heads of those no slice covers, so a picture reused
   without clearing never shows another's motion. Readers go through one accessor, `BandData::blocks`, which gives a
   `Blocks` whose `get(i)` reads `m[i & mask]`, mask 0 over the head's motion or 15 over the entries: `fill_ctx`,
   `predict_p_skip`, `colocated` (a corner of a one-motion co-located macroblock is its head, one line for four
   macroblocks), deblocking's `strengths`, and the test helper `all_motion`. `predict_merged` reads the entries
   directly: it runs after its four `direct_8x8` calls have written all sixteen. The head is 16 bytes, aligned, so
   four share a line and none straddles two; 13 would do.
3. **No clearing of what is written before it is read.** `MbData::reset` clears `t8x8` and the coefficient blocks
   with their masks, which the next macroblock reads without writing; `kind`, `cbp`, `sub`, `ref_idx` and `mvd` (256
   bytes) are written on every path that reads them, for exactly the list and partition pairs prediction reads, and a
   macroblock that fails ends its slice, whose `MbData` is dropped.

The memory budget counts the heads (`MOTION_BYTES_PER_MB` is 208) and the ring (`THREAD_BYTES_PER_MB` gains two `NbInfo`
a macroblock of the picture, a loose bound on a ring of at most twice the picture's width).

Rejected: one motion entry in the sixteen's place, with the macroblock's record saying whether it stands for all
(a later picture's co-located read has no record: the record array is per picture and dropped); a flag in a spare bit
of `Motion` (`ref_slot` and `ref_idx` use their ranges, and every reader would decode it); the ring as two rows indexed
by row parity (needs the neighbour's row and column at each read, where the mask needs the address alone); clearing
the ring at each slice (nothing reads an entry of another slice).

Bit-identical by test and by run: decoded output equal to `main` on the 32 training streams at one and eight threads,
64 of 64; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads with detected and with scalar kernels, and without `fast`. The
deblocking test `masks_match_the_derivation_per_segment` fills the entries of one-motion macroblocks with random motion,
so that a read of them fails it. Callgrind, one thread, `--discard` (`sd` 240 pictures of `6f7799768413`, 720p 120 of
`1d4b1775d78a`, 1080p 60 of `a81de82106be`, 4k 30 of `3b1b441e23ae`; information, not a bar): simulated L1 write
misses 0.708, 0.766, 0.741 and 0.751 of `main`'s, instructions 1.0068, 1.0135, 1.0078 and 1.0167 (the accessor's
tests in deblocking and `colocated`, and `finish_mb`'s three stores).

### Bars

Fixed before any timing of `k`, by round 25's method: the 2.90 GHz class (`--require-cpu 'Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor
@ 2.90GHz'`, the host-health gate before and after each call, the training set, one call per class with its frame
count), FFmpeg 9.0.2 (BtbN `n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068`) the reference of every call. Two arms built on the run's host with
one toolchain, `cargo build --locked --profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`: `main` at `40a656fe`, the base,
and `k`, the branch's code commit `e480d9cc` (`main` plus this round's change to `crates/coreav-h264`). Calls: `g`,
`--pin 2 --rounds 10`; `t8`, `--threads 8`, unpinned, ten rounds; and `gm`, as `g` with `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072`
for the whole call, the placement guard ("Where the allocator puts the planes": `k` allocates a smaller record array
each picture, so what each picture frees changes). Each bar is a median of per-stream ratios with its 95% bootstrap
interval.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| ML-1 | `k` over `main`, one thread, discard, all 32 (the primary) | at most **0.990**, upper end of the interval below 1.000 |
| ML-2 | the same, write | at most **0.995** |
| ML-3 | the same, each class, discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| ML-4 | eight threads, discard, all 32; each class | at most **1.000**; at most **1.010** in each |
| ML-5 | output | `k` byte-identical to `main` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads, with and without `fast`; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads, with and without `fast`, detected and scalar kernels |
| ML-6 | `gm`: ML-1's quantity with every buffer above 128 KB mapped | reported beside ML-1; a verdict that differs from ML-1's is reported as placement-sensitive |

The gating run is requested only if an interleaved local timing of the 32 streams (`luma8x8/ab.py`, one thread, five
rounds or more, a VM of the 2.90 GHz class) shows a median at ML-1's level, at most 0.990; otherwise the round ends
there, with the local result recorded here. The change ships only if ML-1 to ML-5 all pass; one run decides, and a
re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a recorded host fault.

### Result: not queued

Local timing (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/mb-layout/`: `local-ab.jsonl`, `local-ab.txt`; `luma8x8/ab.py`, six
interleaved rounds, one thread pinned, `--discard`, the 32 streams at the class frame counts, a development VM of the
2.90 GHz class; `base` = `main`'s crates, `k` = `e480d9cc`): **1.0001 [0.9841, 1.0054]**, 16 of 32 faster; sd 1.0038,
720p 0.9923, 1080p 1.0170, 4k **0.9473** [0.9007, 1.0025], 6 of 8 faster. The median is not at ML-1's level, so by the
bars the round ends here and is not gated; ML-1 to ML-4 and ML-6 were not measured, and of ML-5 the identity and
conformance checks above were run (with scalar kernels only with `fast`). The timed `k` has the md5 of a build of
`e480d9cc`.

What it shows is where the layout pays. Per stream the gain follows the probe's bound (Spearman's rank correlation
-0.745 over the 32): the six streams whose bound is 10% or more gain 3.4% to 10% (`ed75c044e944` 0.8994,
`81ed4778ece2` 0.9007, `3b1b441e23ae` 0.9163, `e624cbe0d2be` 0.9464, `ae16bb7c7192` 0.9482, `ec473c99c538` 0.9665),
five of them 4k streams where `finish_mb` and `store_mb`, what the round removes, held 6.8% to 10.7% of the time
as excess (`mb-layout-probe/bound.txt`). The largest losses (`76e0b1692494` 1.0833, `175433794e02`
1.0566, `a6af290d9053` 1.0467) are not separated from the spread between rounds (their per-round ratios run from
0.83 to 1.18) or from where the allocator puts the planes, which changes with a smaller record array each picture
("Where the allocator puts the planes"); this local run separated neither. The added instructions (0.7% to 1.7% on
the four streams measured, most in deblocking's lookups and `finish_mb`'s three stores) may contribute but do not
account for losses of that size alone. A later round could keep the layout and remove the added instructions
(deblocking reading a uniform macroblock's head once rather than through `Blocks` at each segment, one store of the
record and its ring entry), timed with the placement guard and with bars that name the classes where the stall is.

## Kernel round: deblocking thresholds built in vector registers

### What the measurement says

- The profile at `6c9e240` (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/profile-6c9e240/items-rest.txt`, of FFmpeg 9.0.2's total,
  mean per stream) puts `luma_columns` at 0.0319 against FFmpeg's vertical-edge functions at 0.0212, and `luma_rows` at
  0.0187 against its horizontal-edge functions at 0.0337. Taken together, the two luma kernels (0.0506) are already
  below FFmpeg's four luma functions (0.0549). The split by direction does not compare like with like: FFmpeg is read
  at function level only, and which of its functions a cycle is charged to depends on how its code is laid out. So
  the luma kernels are not where the deblocking gap is. Chroma is: `filter_chroma_mb` 0.0255, plus 0.0058 in
  `<Auto as Kernels>`, against 0.0219 for FFmpeg's two chroma functions.
- A local microbenchmark (a row of 40 macroblocks, each kernel called as the driver calls it, best of 25) gives:
  - luma: 167 ns for a macroblock's four vertical edges and 121 ns for its four horizontal ones;
  - chroma: 78 ns for one `filter_chroma_mb` with all four edges filtered, 46 ns for its horizontal pass and 51 ns for
    its vertical pass.
- Store forwarding is not what costs: filtering the vertical luma edges in macroblock order (each edge's loads overlap
  the previous edge's stores) and in an order where no edge follows its neighbour take the same time, 167 and 168 ns.
- `llvm-mca` (icelake-server) puts `luma_columns` at about 212 vector µops for an edge with both filters, over three
  ports: about 80 in the transposes and 110 in the filter. Port 5 is the busiest, at 83 cycles. Nothing there is
  spent twice.
- In the chroma kernel, building one pair of edges' lanes cost about 40 instructions, as many as the filter itself:
  - `spread8` per plane (a load, a clamp, two packs and two shuffles);
  - scalar clamps of alpha and beta with `cmov`, and four broadcasts from general registers;
  - four inserts of a half.
  A macroblock with all four chroma edges filtered builds four pairs.

### Design

1. The chroma kernel builds a pair of edges' lanes in vector registers, Cb's in the low half and Cr's in the high half:
   - each plane's alpha and beta are combined into one 64-bit value (the compiler makes it one read where the fields
     are adjacent). They are packed to 16 bits with
     signed saturation (the clamp to −32768 to 32767), broadcast to both halves, and picked out by two byte shuffles.
   - tC0: both planes' four values in one vector, `min` with 255, an unsigned pack (the clamp at 0), and one shuffle
     that gives each segment's value to its two lines.
   - bS: both planes' four bytes in one 64-bit value and one shuffle that widens them.
   This is about 13 instructions in place of about 40. The test for a lane with bS above 0, made after the lanes were
   built, is dropped: `filters` has already found a segment with bS above 0 before the lanes are built.
2. The AVX-512 tier's luma `thresholds` does the same for alpha, beta and `(alpha >> 2) + 2`: one 64-bit value, a
   saturating pack, two word broadcasts, and a shift and an add. It replaces the scalar clamps and three broadcasts
   from general registers.
3. `Auto::filter_chroma_mb` moves its edge-by-edge path (taken where no vector kernels exist) out of line, as a cold
   function. The wrapper inlined that path, so it saved and restored six registers on every macroblock's call. Now it
   is a test and a jump to the kernel. Where no x86 kernel exists (aarch64, or x86-64 without AVX2), every macroblock
   now pays an out-of-line call to that path: a call and a return beside four edges' filtering, which is not
   measured by this round's run (x86-64 only).

Every lane equals the one the code before built, for every input the trait allows:
- the signed pack of a 32-bit value is its clamp to 16 bits;
- tC0 is clamped to 0 to 255 as `segment_bytes` does;
- each bS is a byte widened to 16 bits.
The kernels' tests pass: every threshold and strength and the tightest edges (both tiers), and the chroma macroblock
against the reference. Those sweeps hold alpha, beta and tC0 to the decoder's ranges, so two tests check the lanes
lane by lane against their definition on extreme inputs (alpha, beta and tC0 at and around every clamp, from
`i32::MIN` to `i32::MAX`, and every class of bS byte up to 255). No memory access changes. The new `unsafe` is register intrinsics only; `tc0` is read through
`load4_i32` from the slice.

Rejected:
- The AVX-512 tier's two rounds of byte permutes for the chroma vertical pass. Its sixteen lines of eight bytes (Cb's
  rows, then Cr's) have the shape of a vertical luma edge, so `luma_columns`' transposes apply unchanged. The
  microbenchmark put that pass at 52 ns against 51: it is not bound by its shuffles. Its arithmetic was not changed.
- Filtering a macroblock's vertical luma edges in one call, to keep the columns in registers between edges. The
  store-forwarding test above finds nothing to win there, and earlier rounds found 1.2 live edges per direction per
  macroblock.

Microbenchmark, `base` against `k` (interleaved, three alternations, best of 25 each), information:
- the chroma macroblock: 78.1 → 72.3 ns;
- its horizontal pass: 45.5 → 41.0 ns;
- its vertical pass: 51 → 51 ns;
- four vertical luma edges: 167.8 → 167.1 ns;
- four horizontal luma edges: 120.7 → 119.6 ns.

A local timing A/B (information, not a bar) on this VM's 2.90 GHz class:
- method: `scripts/h264_parity.py`, two decoders in the same rounds, one thread pinned to core 2, six rounds, the 32
  training streams at the class frame counts;
- discard: median `k` over `base` 0.9932 [0.9911, 0.9984], 24 of 32 faster;
- write: 0.9959 [0.9924, 0.9995];
- discard per class: sd 0.9919, 720p 0.9856, 1080p 0.9984, 4k 1.0016.

### Bars

These bars are fixed before the gating run. The method is that of the deblocking-driver round:
- two decoders in the same rounds, built alike from one tree each (`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example
  decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset);
- on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106). The run records the class, and the script stops on any other host;
- `base` is `main` at `baa6d0a`. `k` is the branch's code commit `d7e7fb0`: `base`'s tree plus this round's change to
  `lib.rs`, `simd/avx512.rs` and `simd/x86/chroma_mb.rs` of `crates/coreav-kernels-h264`;
- the run is `scripts/h264_parity.py` of the base tree on the training set, with FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference
  command;
- each call sits between two host gates; a failed gate after a call voids it, and it runs again;
- the class frame counts are sd 1800, 720p 900, 1080p 300 and 4k 150;
- per class, one call at one thread pinned to core 2, at twenty rounds, and one at eight threads, unpinned, at ten;
- the script is `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/deblock-lanes/run-ab-helper.sh`, and `analyze.py` beside it prints the

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |

## Threading round: slack rows at the picture's edges in every layout

### What eight threads decline

A picture of one band keeps `LUMA_SLACK` (4) luma and `CHROMA_SLACK` (2) chroma rows before and after its planes, so
`Kernels::predict` takes a window that passes the picture's top or bottom row where it lies in the buffer, as long as
every sample its fraction uses is inside the picture. A picture of several bands kept none. The bands holding row 0
and the last band could not hold such a window, so the block went to `predict_list_any`, which looks the band up
again for each plane and copies each window through `edge_window`. With one thread no block takes that path on the
sd stream `ec473c99c538`; at eight threads 69,798 of its 416,620 banded blocks did. A count by reason (a throwaway
counter build on an earlier change's branch, whose kept views do not change which blocks are declined;
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/band-slack/counts-summary.txt`) puts 68,985 of them (16.6% of the banded
blocks) at the picture's top or bottom with every used sample inside. Over the 32 training streams these blocks are
0.3% to 16.6% of the banded ones (median by class: sd 9.3%, 720p 3.1%, 1080p 1.6%, 4k 1.9%). The other declines are
windows whose used samples leave the picture, which one thread declines too, and chroma windows that start above the
chroma apron of the band they are read from (763 on this stream, up to 11.7% of the banded blocks on others). This
change leaves both alone.

A probe priced these blocks before anything was built (`band-slack/plan-probe.md`, bars committed before the run).
It sent them through the declined path twice, putting the block's samples back between the two passes, so the
output stayed byte-identical. Both timing runs were void under the plan's own host check, PS-2: the null arm, the
same binary timed twice, left [0.990, 1.010] in two classes each time (up to 1.021), and the plan allowed one
re-run. The probe arm read 1.042 and then 1.025 overall (sd 1.050 and 1.069), against PS-1's 1.015; these are
observations, not a result (`band-slack/README.md`). PS-2's 1% per class was narrower than this host's same-binary
spread at eight threads. This round uses the parity harness's host checks (3% per stream, "Measurement method: host
faults inside a call") and no window of its own. With PS-1 never judged, the plan's rule did not call for a build;
the round was built anyway, as a small and reversible change, to be judged by its own bars.

### Design

As measured at `c27c8be5` (`rejected/h264-band-slack`; `band-slack/k.diff`). The round was not queued (the result
below). Bundle 2 ("Bundle 2: ten small changes together") brought it into `main` as item E, its origins taken once a
row.

Slack rows belong to bands, not to pictures. `Geometry::luma_slack(k)` gives band `k` `LUMA_SLACK` rows before its
luma plane where its stored rows start at row 0 (`luma_first(k) == 0`: the first band, and any band whose apron
reaches row 0), and `LUMA_SLACK` rows after it where it is the last band. Every other band gets none.
`chroma_slack(k)` does the same with `CHROMA_SLACK` and `chroma_first`. `luma_origin(k)` and `chroma_origin(k)`,
where a band's first stored row sits in its buffer, now take the band. A picture of one band is its own first and
last band, so it keeps exactly what it kept before, and the one-thread path is unchanged. Every offset into a band
already went through `Geometry::luma_at(k, row)` or through the slice decoder's `luma_origin`. That field is now set
with `luma_first` when the slice enters a band. The deblocking filter, the reconstruction and the concealment copy
take the band's origin.

The kernel contract is unchanged. `Planes::band` already accepts an origin only for a plane whose first row is row
0. A band whose stored rows start below row 0 keeps origin 0, and a band other than the last keeps no slack after its
rows, so a window that leaves such a band still lies outside its slice and is still declined. Slack after a middle band would be read as rows it holds (`Interior::band` counts
the rows after the origin), and the kernel would take windows from rows the band does not hold final.

On that branch, `the_windows_at_a_banded_pictures_edges_are_taken_from_their_band` (picture.rs) builds a picture
in bands of one macroblock row. It checks that the kernel takes blocks at the top, at the top-left corner and at the bottom from the
band they are read from, and predicts the samples. It fails if either the slack before or the slack after is
removed (both checked). `bands_at_the_pictures_edges_keep_slack_rows` pins the layout.

Rejected: slack rows before and after every band, which would keep one origin for all bands. A middle band's slice
would then hold slack after its rows, which the kernel reads as held rows, and its origin would break `Planes::band`'s
rule for planes that start below row 0. Trimming every view to fix that costs work on every block. It would also add
8 luma and 4 chroma rows to every band, about 20% more samples at sd, where bands are one macroblock row. Taking
these blocks in `predict_list_any` without the copy (a window view that clamps): that keeps the per-plane lookups,
and the declined path is the part this removes.

Memory: a banded picture grows by the slack of the bands holding row 0 (one or two) and of the last band, 12 to 18
luma-row equivalents in all. `Geometry::stored_bytes` and the memory budget count them.

The checks pass. Output is identical to `base` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads

The one-thread cost is real, not noise (`instructions.txt`, callgrind). One thread runs 0.69% more instructions on
the sd stream, all of them in `deblock_rows`. `luma_origin(k)` reached `Geometry::bands`, a division the compiler
cannot drop, through `luma_slack(k)`; computing the origins without it (`4b512a85`, on the same branch;
`k-origin-fix.diff`) removes half of the increase, more than the division itself costs, so the rest of that half is
how the filter compiled around it. It leaves +0.35% on that stream, +0.28% on
a 4k one and +0.01% at 720p and 1080p. The rest is about 1 to 3 instructions a macroblock in the filter's
macroblock loop: the code around a band-dependent origin compiles differently, and even giving the filter band 0's
origin (a diagnostic) leaves +0.11% at 4k.

At eight threads the change does what it was built for: 0.922 of `base`'s instructions on the sd stream
`ec473c99c538`, consistent with the 16.6% of its banded blocks no longer taking the declined path (no per-function
split at eight threads was taken).

The code waits on `rejected/h264-band-slack` for a later bundle. `4b512a85` is the variant to take. Before it goes
into one, the filter's macroblock loop should take the band's origin and first row as one per-row base offset, so
that one thread runs the instructions it ran before.

## Threading round: band views kept for the slice

### What eight threads add

Against FFmpeg 9.0.2 at eight threads `main` (`2a3972b`) was 1.036 (median per stream, discard, 32 training
streams, five rounds on the development VM, Intel Xeon @ 2.90 GHz, 4 cores and 8 logical CPUs, the A/B helper's class;
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/band-views/scaling.txt`), against 1.144 at one thread. Per stream, the ratio at eight
threads is the product of three factors: our CPU time at one thread over FFmpeg's (W1, 1.144), our growth in CPU
time from one thread to eight over FFmpeg's (I, 1.116; sd 1.144, 720p 1.157, 1080p 1.079, 4k 1.092), and FFmpeg's
logical CPUs kept busy over ours (B, 0.851). So we wait less than FFmpeg does (B below 1 in every class) but do
more work at eight threads than at one, and more of it than FFmpeg adds. Our kernel time and page faults at eight
threads are below FFmpeg's, so the growth is our own code.

Callgrind counts 1.04 to 1.39 times the instructions at eight threads as at one (two streams a class,
`instructions.txt`), and the growth is work only a banded decode does (share of the one-thread instructions, one
stream a class, sd, 720p, 1080p and 4k):

| item | sd | 720p | 1080p | 4k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a band's view built for every block (`reference_band`, `Planes::band`) | 10.8% | 8.9% | 6.1% | 14.6% |
| the aprons (`copy_top`) | 12.0% | 5.6% | 3.3% | 2.2% |
| blocks whose window leaves the band (`predict_list_any`) | 15.8% | 4.4% | 2.2% | 2.7% |

and `colocated` up to 2.9% on streams with B slices. A one-thread decode builds each reference's view once per
slice ("Round 17"); a banded one built it for every block it predicted: about 250 instructions (190 in
`reference_band`, 60 in `Interior::band`, whose two divisions run for every block), 2.9 million times on a 4k stream.

Two probes, each byte-identical to `main` (plan and bars committed before the run, `plan-probe.md`): building the
view twice, the second time from opaque inputs, which doubles the part a kept view removes (68% of the view's
instructions), cost **1.022** [1.007, 1.041] at eight threads (sd 1.022, 720p 0.998, 1080p 1.048, 4k 1.034); copying
the aprons twice cost 1.008 [0.990, 1.019] (1080p 1.016). Both meet PB-1; the view is the larger and is this round;
the aprons are the next.

### Design

As measured at `a9e568bc` (`rejected/h264-band-views`, whose head `bc97fa55` adds the test below). The round
missed BV-1 (the result below). Bundle 2 ("Bundle 2: ten small changes together") brought it into `main` as item D.

A slice keeps the views of the bands its blocks read, `SliceDecoder::band_views`: per list, 16 slots, reference
`idx`'s band `k` in slot `(4 * idx + k % 4) % 16`, each holding the reference's index in its list, the band and its
`Planes`; the slots start empty with each slice.
`reference_band` finds the band as before (the band the luma window's last row is read from) and takes the slot's
view where the slot holds that reference's band; otherwise it checks the reference's size, waits for the band,
builds the view and keeps it in the slot. A view stays right for the slice: a band does not change once it is
published, and the slice's reference lists do not change while it is decoded. The slots are a direct map, not a
search: four consecutive bands of each of the first four references never share a slot, which covers the bands the
blocks of one macroblock row read (with bands of one macroblock row, sd, a row's blocks read up to three bands).
The index names the picture because the lists do not change within the slice; a view of another band of the same
reference would still give the same samples (a published band holds only final rows, and `Kernels::predict` declines
a window the view does not hold), so the band in the key is for the hit rate, the index for correctness.
References four apart share slots: a slice that alternates between them block by block, in the same bands, builds
the view as before and stores it, about 15 instructions on the 250. The training streams miss on 0.3% (4k, 1080p) to
5.7% (sd) of lookups (`Interior::band` calls under callgrind).

`many_references_give_the_pictures_one_thread_gives` (`tests/threads.rs` on the rejected branch) decodes slices of eight references with
vectors that reach many bands, at bands of one and two rows, against one thread; it fails if a kept view serves
another reference.

Rejected: a view for every band of every reference, built when the slice starts. It would wait for every band of
every reference before the first macroblock, which is what the bands are there to avoid, and with bands of one row
it is up to 68 bands a reference. A view per reference holding only the last band read: at sd the blocks of one
macroblock alternate between two bands. Making the view cheaper to build (no divisions in `Interior::band`, kept per
band in the picture): a change to the kernels crate and to each band, for part of what the kept view removes.

At one thread the only new work is the 32 empty slots each slice starts with: every reference is whole there, and
`reference_band` runs only for a picture that is not yet whole when a slice starts. `SliceDecoder` grows by the
slots, about 4.3 KB.

## Reconstruction round: coefficient scalings from per-QP tables

Not queued for a gating run; nothing merges from it (code on `rejected/h264-coeff-tables`, kept for a later
bundle).

### What the measurement says

The profile at `6c9e240` has reconstruction at 1.32 of FFmpeg's time at 720p and 1.25 at 1080p ("Again at
`6c9e240`"). After the kernels, its largest items are the scaling the entropy decoder applies to each level
(`CoeffScale::apply`, inlined in the CABAC and CAVLC level loops) and the per-macroblock preparation of those scalings
(`prepare_level_scales`, `CoeffScale::new`). The coreav-h264 crate is unchanged from `6c9e240` to `main` at `4f45698`.

A probe bounded what a change to the scaling could save before anything was built
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/recon-probe/`; `plan.txt` fixed the removed set, the bound and the threshold before
the run). It used the MB-layout probe's method: perf time and callgrind instructions per source line, one thread,
AVX2 kernels, all 32 training streams. The bound per stream is the sum, over the lines of `CoeffScale::new`,
`CoeffScale::apply`, `prepare_level_scales` and `chroma_qp`, of each line's larger share, time or instructions. Class
medians: sd **2.12%**, 720p 1.20%, 1080p **1.81%**, 4k 0.93% (`bound.txt`). Two classes clear an earlier change's 1.5%, so the
change was built. Reported as information: the rest of `recon.rs`'s lines (the reconstruction glue) are 1.14% to
2.31% by class, and the intra 4x4 kernel 0.16% to 0.95% of the time. No change in view removes either.

`apply` compiled to 14 instructions a level (`apply-asm.txt`, the CAVLC level loop): the multiplication, then a load of the round and of the shift from the
scaling, a `min` of the shift with 16 and a shift by a register, then the clip. The scalings were rebuilt whenever
the QP changed, a copy of 16 or 64 factors for each of up to three block kinds a macroblock. With adaptive
quantisation that is nearly every macroblock.

### Design

As measured at `d6e962f7` (`rejected/h264-coeff-tables`). The round was not queued (the result below). Bundle 2 ("Bundle 2: ten small changes together") brought it into `main` as item C.

Every QP takes one form of the scaling, with the shift `r` of the block size (4 for a 4x4 block, 6 for an 8x8 one):
`(level * (LevelScale << (qP / 6)) + 2^(r - 1)) >> r`.
- Below `qP / 6 = r` the clause rounds and shifts right by `r - qP / 6`. The form multiplies numerator and
  denominator by `2^(qP / 6)`, which leaves the quotient, and so its floor, unchanged.
- From `qP / 6 = r` up the clause shifts left. The form's product is the clause's value times `2^r`, and the
  `2^(r - 1)` it adds is below `2^r`, so the floor is the clause's value.

The round and the shift become constants of the block size, and `apply` is nine instructions (`apply-asm.txt`): the multiplication, an
add and a shift by constants, and the clip, which stays. The products are exact in 64 bits. `CoeffScale::IDENTITY`
is the factor `2^r`. The unit test checks the form against the equations written out, for 4x4 and 8x8 blocks.

`CoeffTables` holds the scaling of every QP, 0 to 51: luma 4x4 and 8x8, intra and inter, and chroma by component.
The chroma entries are indexed by QP_Y, so QP'C is derived once per entry rather than per macroblock. The tables
(about 47 KB) are built when a slice starts, but only if its scaling lists and chroma QP offsets differ from those the
tables were built from (`CoeffTables::fit`, comparing 232 bytes of the PPS). They are kept between slices and
pictures as the other per-slice buffers are. A macroblock's `prepare_level_scales` points `LevelScales` at its QP's
entries, and each block takes the reference as before. The slice decoder holds the tables by reference for the slice.

Rejected:
- **Building each entry the first time a slice uses it** (`05ba8f0c`, on the branch). Its tables were indexed by QP
  for every block. Its instruction counts are consistent with that lookup costing more than the rebuilds it saved on
  streams whose QP seldom changes. Over the 32 streams it ran 0.9987 of `main`'s instructions, and 1.0018 at most
  (`instructions.txt`; callgrind, one thread, the first 240, 120, 60 and 30 pictures by class). The tables built per
  scaling lists run **0.9911** (sd 0.9921, 720p 0.9909, 1080p 0.9902, 4k 0.9955), all 32 streams below 1, the most
  1.9% fewer.
- **Building every QP each slice**: 11,648 factors a slice, where most slices use a few QPs.
- **Keying the tables on the PPS's identity** rather than its lists: a new PPS can reuse the old one's memory, and
  stale tables would scale wrongly.
- **Dropping the clip**: a non-conforming stream's levels can leave the 16-bit range the kernels rely on.

### Bars (fixed before the timing run)

`base` is `main` at `4f45698`, and `k` the branch's code commit `d6e962f7`. Each bar is a median of per-stream
ratios, `k` over `base`, with its 95% bootstrap interval.

| | measure | bar |
|---|---|---|
| CT-1 | one thread pinned, discard, all 32 (the primary) | at most **0.995**, and the upper end of its interval below **1.000** |
| CT-2 | the same, write | at most **1.000** |
| CT-3 | one thread, each class, discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| CT-4 | eight threads, discard, all 32; each class | at most **1.005**; at most **1.010** in each |
| CT-5 | output | `k` byte-identical to `base` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads, with scalar kernels and in safe mode |

CT-5 is met (`recon-probe/identity.txt`, `conformance.txt`). The gating run uses the parity harness on the 2.90 GHz
class, as an earlier change did: the host-health gate before and after each call, FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference, both arms built
on the run's host. CT-4 is measured with the harness's eight-thread method as of the run. If the longer-call method
for eight threads has landed, the run uses it. The change ships if `k` meets CT-1 to CT-5. One run decides, and a
re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a recorded host fault.

A gating run is requested only after a local interleaved timing shows CT-1's gain: `base` and `k`, one thread pinned,
CPU time, six rounds over the 32 training streams at the class frame counts, discard (`ab3.py`, summarised by
`ab1sum.py`). The request is made if the median is at most 0.995 with the upper end of its bootstrap interval below
1.000. If the interval spans 1.000, the change is a small gain: it is not gated alone, and it waits on a `rejected/`
branch for a bundle round.

### Result: not queued

The local timing (`recon-probe/local-ab/`), on a development VM of the bar class (Intel Xeon @ 2.90 GHz, family 6,
