## Profile with hardware events, on a host with a PMU

The cpu-clock profiles above sample time; they cannot say whether a stage's time is executed work or waiting. A
Compute Engine VM with its PMU exposed (Emerald Rapids, `c4-standard-8`; not the bar class, so diagnosis only) counts
both, by stage, for `main` at `b3664291` against FFmpeg 9.0.2 on the 32 training streams at one thread
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/pmu-profile/`; FFmpeg attributed at function level from a build with symbols and no
debug information).

- The gap is executed work: CoreAV uses 1.10 times FFmpeg's slots, and the excess is retiring (+0.082 of FFmpeg's
  slots) and fetch bandwidth (+0.028), while it is less backend-bound than FFmpeg (−0.035). It retires 1.30 times
  FFmpeg's instructions at a higher IPC (2.76 against 2.29).
- Nearly all of it is entropy decoding and the MB layer together (FFmpeg inlines its motion prediction into its
  macroblock parse, so the two are compared as one): +1,355 of the +1,451 instructions a macroblock and +0.105 of
  FFmpeg's cycles of the +0.098. Deblocking adds +0.022 (+103 instructions and 1.2 more branch misses a macroblock,
  in `edge_strengths`, `deblock_row` and the threshold setup).
- Store stalls are where the MB layer probe found them (`finish_mb`, `store_mb`), but small on this core: store
  buffer full in the MB layer is 1.4% of FFmpeg's cycles, and `store_mb`'s copy of the row it has just stored blocks
  store forwarding 4.5 times a macroblock (FFmpeg's MB layer 0.03). The bar class has a smaller store buffer, so the
  timing rounds there decide what the stores cost.

### Again at `acf3ee2f`, ranked by excess over parity

The same profile after the MB layer round 2 (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/profile-acf3ee2f-pmu/`; diagnosis only,
same host class), with each stage's excess over 1.00 times FFmpeg. CoreAV takes 1.092 times the BtbN build's cycles
(sd 1.026, 720p 1.130, 1080p 1.136, 4k 1.011). Entropy and the MB layer together are the largest excess in every
class but 4k (+0.069 of FFmpeg's cycles over the 32 streams; +0.098, +0.074, +0.076 at sd, 720p, 1080p; 1,165 more
instructions a macroblock over the two, whose split FFmpeg's inlining hides); inter prediction is second (+0.028) and first
at 4k (+0.056, with the reference prefetch at twice FFmpeg's), deblocking third (+0.024). Reconstruction (0.92) and
the rest (0.61) are below parity.

### Again at `ae609547`, at one thread and at eight, stream by stream

The same profile after bundle 2 (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/profile-ae609547-pmu/`; diagnosis only, same CPU
model on a `c4-standard-16` with one thread a core), now also at eight threads and with each stream's time. At one
thread, CoreAV's wall time over FFmpeg's is 1.028 (median per stream; sd 0.961, 720p 1.072, 1080p 1.066, 4k 0.917),
14 of 32 streams faster. Entropy and the MB layer together are still the largest excess (+0.036 of FFmpeg's cycles;
+0.075 at sd, +0.043 at 720p) and inter prediction second (+0.030; first at 1080p, +0.031, and 4k, +0.059, in the
reference prefetch and the placement); deblocking is now below parity (−0.005). Of the ten slowest streams (1.065 to
1.154), entropy and the MB layer are among the first two stages in all ten, inter in six. At eight threads CoreAV's
wall time is 0.903 of FFmpeg's (29 of 32 faster) but it spends 1.077 times FFmpeg's cycles. Inter prediction is the
largest excess in every class (+0.074, 1.47 times FFmpeg's): its instructions a macroblock grow by a tenth over one
thread and its IPC falls from 3.15 to 2.48 (FFmpeg: 2% more instructions, IPC 3.42 to 3.04), in `predict_fast_body`,
`reference_band` and the luma kernel's stores, with CoreAV more memory-bound than FFmpeg only at eight threads.

## MB layer round 2: the layout without the added instructions

The first round ("MB layer round: only what later stages read") showed the layout paying where the probe put the stall (4k 0.947 locally, the gain per stream
following the bound) but not overall (1.000), with 0.7% to 1.7% more instructions than `main`, most in deblocking's
lookups of motion through the accessor and in `finish_mb`'s stores. This round writes the same layout again as new
code, with the instruction count held to `main`'s: a macroblock with one motion is read as its head once, not a block
at a time through a mask, and each of the record, its ring entry and the head is stored once a macroblock. It is
timed with the placement guard as a bar rather than a report, and with a 4k bar that must also hold on the held-out
streams, since the 4k gain was seen before the bars were chosen.

### Design

The layout is the first round's; what differs is how each piece is read and stored.

1. **The record split.** `MbInfo` (`PictureWork::mbs`) keeps `slice`, `kind`, `qp`, `t8x8`, `nz` and `uniform`, 12
   bytes (asserted). `uniform` stays although the head's `split` says the same: it fits the record's padding, and
   deblocking reads it from the line it loads for `kind` and `nz`, where `split` needs the head's line before the
   derivation knows whether it needs motion at all. `NbInfo` holds what only A and B read (`entropy`, `intra_edge`,
   `cbf`, `cbp`, `chroma_mode`, `ref_gt0`, 48 bytes) in a ring of `next_power_of_two(mb_w + 1)` entries indexed by
   `addr & mask`, kept in `Spare` across slices and pictures and never cleared; a neighbour is read only where it is
   available, so its entry is the one its `finish_mb` wrote (a test checks the indexing for widths 1 to 299). Each
   field is zero where the macroblock's type codes none of it, which the syntax already gives: a skipped or intra
   macroblock sets no `ref_gt0` bit (clause 9.3.3.1.1.6), only an intra macroblock other than I_PCM sets
   `chroma_mode` (clause 9.3.3.1.1.8), and I_PCM's `cbp` of 0x2f gives clause 9.3.3.1.1.4's I_PCM answers. So the
   CABAC contexts of `ref_idx`, `intra_chroma_pred_mode` and `coded_block_pattern` read the entry alone and not the
   neighbour's type. The entry is built in the `SliceDecoder` (`cur_nb`, started by `decode_mb`) and stored once by
   `finish_mb`; a skipped macroblock builds none, and its instance of `finish_mb` stores `NbInfo::NONE`, stores of a
   zero register. `MbInfo` is started in `start_mb` and stored once.
2. **A motion head a macroblock.** Each band keeps `heads`, one `MbHead { m: Motion, split }` a macroblock (16
   bytes, 16-aligned: four a line, none straddling two) beside the sixteen entries, which only a split macroblock
   writes. `store_mb` writes the head alone. `finish_mb` writes `{ motion_first, split: !uniform }` only for a
   macroblock built by partitions: `store_mb` leaves `motion_first` unset, and an intra macroblock writes its head
   (`NO_HEAD`) on its own path (`decode_mb`'s intra branch, `decode_pcm`), where its type is known, so `finish_mb`
   lost main's 192-byte fill and its test of the type. `store_motion` clears `MbInfo::uniform` in the record being
   built, which removes a separate flag, its reset in `start_mb` and its copy in `finish_mb`. `clear_macroblock`,
   `fill_black` and `conceal_from` write `NO_HEAD` for what they cover, so a picture reused without clearing never
   shows another's motion; debug assertions in `finish_mb` check that the head agrees with `uniform` and that an
   inter macroblock derived all sixteen blocks. Readers look a macroblock's head up once (`BandData::mb_motion`,
   one motion or the sixteen): `fill_ctx` fills a one-motion neighbour's cells from one motion (B's four in one row
   store); `predict_p_skip`; direct prediction looks the co-located macroblock up once (`colocated_mb`) and reads its
   corners or a quadrant's blocks from that lookup, a one-motion one answering from its head. `predict_merged` reads
   the entries its four `direct_8x8` calls wrote.
3. **Deblocking reads a one-motion macroblock as its head, once.** `Side` holds the record, the head and the
   macroblock's place in the band. Where the macroblock and both neighbours carry one motion (most macroblocks),
   `strengths` runs an instance of `edge_strengths` with no path that reads entries: edge 0 compares two heads, the
   internal edges settle on the masks. Where any of the three is split, one out-of-line call a macroblock
   (`split_strengths`) reads the entries: the internal edges as `main` does, and a mixed edge 0 decided once a side
   (the split side's blocks at fixed indices, the other's head), with no test a segment. The split paths kept in
   line, or one call an edge, measured more instructions: the extra live values cost the common path more spills
   than the call costs the rare one. `strengths` takes the current record from `deblock_row` rather than looking it
   up again.
4. **No clearing of what is written before it is read.** `MbData::reset` keeps `t8x8 = false` and the coefficient
   blocks with their masks, and drops `mvd` (512 bytes), `ref_idx`, `sub`, `kind` and `cbp`: prediction reads `mvd`
   and `ref_idx` for exactly the list and partition pairs the parse wrote (the same mode tables decide both; a
   `ref_idx` of 0 is written where one reference is active and for P_8x8ref0), skipped and direct macroblocks read
   neither, and CABAC's motion vector difference context reads the ring, not `MbData`; `sub` is written for the four
   8x8 blocks of the types that read it; `kind` on every path before a reader; `cbp` for every coded type before it
   is read, and skipped and I_PCM macroblocks never read it. A macroblock that fails ends its slice, whose `MbData`
   is not kept.

The memory budget counts the heads (`MOTION_BYTES_PER_MB` is 208) and the ring (`THREAD_BYTES_PER_MB` gains two
`NbInfo` a macroblock of the picture, a loose bound on a ring of at most twice the width).

Rejected: the first round's accessor, `m[i & mask]` over the head (mask 0) or the entries (mask 15), for every
reader, which put a mask and a lookup on every deblocking segment; `kind` copied into `NbInfo` (52 bytes, a fourth
move a macroblock, to save a second lookup on the cold path that still needs it, the Intra_4x4 and Intra_8x8 mode
cache); the ring in `MbData`, which a failed slice drops; and, as in the first round, one entry in the sixteen's
place with the record saying whether it stands for all, a flag in a spare bit of `Motion`, the ring as two rows by
row parity, and clearing the ring at each slice.

Bit-identical by test and by run: decoded output equal to `main` on the 32 training streams at one and eight threads,
64 of 64, and without `fast` at one thread, 32 of 32; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads with detected and
scalar kernels, with and without `fast`. The test `masks_match_the_derivation_per_segment` fills the entries of every
one-motion and intra macroblock with other motion, so that a read of them fails it. Callgrind, one thread,
`--discard`, the AVX2 kernels (the first round's four streams; information, not a bar):

| Stream | instructions, `k` over `main` | simulated L1 write misses |
|---|---|---|
| sd `6f7799768413`, 240 pictures | 0.9595 | 0.712 |
| 720p `1d4b1775d78a`, 120 | 0.9815 | 0.774 |
| 1080p `a81de82106be`, 60 | 0.9836 | 0.741 |
| 4k `3b1b441e23ae`, 30 | 0.9514 | 0.751 |

Where the first round added 0.7% to 1.7%, this one removes 1.6% to 4.9%: the store of one motion where `store_mb`
stored sixteen (`inter_pred`, -0.9% to -2.6% of the total), deblocking (-1.1% to +0.03%), the co-located lookup once
a macroblock (-0.8% and -1.9% on the two streams with direct prediction) and `start_mb` (-0.1% to -0.6%); the store
of the ring entry adds one to four instructions a macroblock to `finish_mb` (+0.01% to +0.33%).

### Bars

Fixed before any timing of `k`, by the first round's method: the 2.90 GHz class (`--require-cpu 'Intel(R) Xeon(R)
Processor @ 2.90GHz'`, the host-health gate before and after each call), one call per class with its frame count,
FFmpeg 9.0.2 (BtbN `n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068`) the reference of every call. Two arms built on the run's host with one
toolchain, `cargo build --locked --profile dist --example decode -p coreav-h264`: `main` at the commit the branch is
based on, the base, and `k`, the branch's code commit (`main` plus this round's change to `crates/coreav-h264`). Calls
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/mb-layout-2/run-ab-helper.sh`, read by `analyze.py` there): `g`, the 32 training
streams, `--pin 2 --rounds 10`; `t8`, `--threads 8`, unpinned, ten rounds; `gm`, as `g` with
`MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072` for the whole call, so that every buffer above 128 KB is mapped and where the
allocator puts the planes no longer follows what each picture frees ("Where the allocator puts the planes"); and `h`,
as `g` on the 64 streams of the held-out draw (`docs/measurements/h264-n2-heldout/list.json`, 16 a class) at its
frame counts. Each bar is a median of per-stream ratios `k` over `main`, with its 95% bootstrap interval, read only
over every stream it names.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| ML2-1 | `g`, discard, all 32 (the primary) | at most **0.995**, upper end of the interval below 1.000 |
| ML2-2 | `g`, write, all 32 | at most **1.000** |
| ML2-3 | `g`, each class, discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| ML2-4 | `t8`, discard, all 32; each class | at most **1.000**; at most **1.010** in each |
| ML2-5 | `gm`, discard, all 32 (the placement guard); `h`, discard, all 64 | at most **0.995**; at most **1.000** |
| ML2-6 | discard, 4k: `g`'s 8 streams and `h`'s 16 | at most **0.980** in each |
| ML2-7 | output | `k` byte-identical to `main` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads, with and without `fast`, and on the 64 held-out streams at 1 thread; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads, with and without `fast`, detected and scalar kernels |

ML2-1 asks for half the gain the first round's bar asked for, as the overall gain left once the 4k streams' share is
spread over all 32; ML2-3 that no class pays for it. ML2-5 asks that the gain not come from where the allocator put
the planes (the first round's losses were not separated from it), and that the held-out streams not lose. ML2-6
names the class where the stall is (`finish_mb` and `store_mb` held 6.8% to 10.7% of the 4k streams' time as
excess); as it was chosen after the first round showed the 4k gain on the training streams, it must hold on the
held-out 4k streams too, which no earlier round of the MB layer has measured.

The gating run is requested only if an interleaved local timing of the 32 streams (`luma8x8/ab.py`, one thread
pinned, `--discard`, eight rounds, a VM of the 2.90 GHz class) shows a median at ML2-1's level, at most 0.995;
otherwise the round ends there, with the local result recorded here. The change ships only if ML2-1 to ML2-7 all
pass; one run decides, and a re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a recorded host fault.

## Entropy decoding: the instruction excess by syntax element, and a decision probe

The PMU profile ("Profile with hardware events, on a host with a PMU") put +1,355 of the decoder's +1,451 extra
instructions a macroblock in entropy decoding and the MB layer. This breaks that down against FFmpeg, prices the
largest part with a probe, and times a cut (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cabac-decision-probe/`). Nothing merges
from it. Divided by decoded macroblocks, the breakdown's +1,377 on the CABAC streams agrees with that figure. The probe prices the engine's per-bin instructions (the CABAC verdict, "the rangeLPS tables in half the
lines", covered the decision chain's latency and the tables' footprint).

**Where the instructions are.** Method:

- Callgrind of `main` at instruction level, with inline chains from its line tables, against an FFmpeg 9.0.2 build at
  function level (symbol table only), on the 32 training streams.
- Each decoder is divided by the macroblocks it decoded, from its own call counts: both decode past the pictures they
  are asked to output, FFmpeg by up to twice as many.
- Exact bins come from a local counting build.

Per macroblock, on the 26 CABAC streams:

| Group | CoreAV | of which engine | FFmpeg | difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| residual: significance map, levels, signs, coded_block_flag, block dispatch | 1,757 | 1,017 | 974 | **+783** |
| mvd and ref_idx | 312 | 133 | 126 | +186 |
| MB header (skip, mb_type, sub_mb_type, transform_size_8x8_flag, cbp, mb_qp_delta, intra modes) and the MB loop | 769 | 345 | 863 | −94 |
| MB layer (neighbours, motion vector prediction, direct, motion stores, per-MB setup) | 620 | 0 | 292 | +328 |
| NAL units and RBSP | 100 | 0 | 19 | +81 |
| other code in these stages | 93 | | 1 | +93 |
| **total** | **3,650** | | **2,274** | **+1,377** |

- **Comparing the MB header and MB layer.** FFmpeg's symbol table has no separate functions for motion vector
  prediction or for most neighbour work, so they are inlined into `ff_h264_decode_mb_cabac` and count under its MB
  header. The two groups are therefore read together: CoreAV +234.
- **The CAVLC streams.** On the 6 CAVLC streams the excess is +778: the CAVLC syntax with its residual +334, the MB
  layer +240, RBSP +93.
- **Bins.** A CABAC macroblock decodes 41.0 bins: 34.3 regular, 5.7 bypass, 1.0 terminating.
- **The engine.** CoreAV's engine runs 36.8 instructions a bin. FFmpeg's out-of-line `get_cabac` runs 27.6 a call,
  its call and return included. FFmpeg's whole residual is 34.0 a residual bin, below CoreAV's engine alone.
- **Excess by kind:**
  - **Per-bin engine instructions** (about 9 a bin, about 380 a macroblock against FFmpeg's call). In the
    significance map's loop an inlined DecodeDecision is 40 instructions, from the context index to the refill test
    (`decision-asm.txt`). It takes three table addresses (`LPS`, `LPS_NORM`, `NEXT`), repeats a comparison whose
    flags the selections clobber, builds the next state's index from the decoded bin, and unpacks `LPS_NORM`'s packed
    shift. Where a syntax element decodes through `Cabac::decision` the engine's registers go through memory each
    bin, 43 to 48 instructions.
  - **Block dispatch:** 109 instructions a coded_block_flag bin, about 260 a macroblock. This is the call layers
    `residual` → `significance_map` → `levels`, each out of line with its prologue, plus `coded_block_flag_inc`.
  - **Glue around the MB header and motion syntax elements:** context increments from the neighbours, binarization
    loops and the macroblock's dispatch. Per macroblock that is cbp 121, mvd 167, and the skip flag with
    `decode_mb`'s loop 194 (53, 58 and 97 a bin).
  - **Level writes,** 22 a level bin. They hold the scan lookup and the scaling, which FFmpeg's residual also does.
  - **RBSP extraction,** a loop of one byte at a time with a `push`.
  - **No bounds checks.** The hot paths index through masks (`& CTX_MASK`, `& 2047`) rather than checks.

**The probe.** It adds twelve independent one-uop instructions to every DecodeDecision: as many as a smaller decision
would remove, added in place, +11.94 a regular bin. Its plan and rule were fixed before the run. Results, local
(2.50 GHz class, directional):

- CABAC streams: **1.0229 [1.0174, 1.0292]**, 26 of 26 slower.
- CAVLC streams, which decode no bins: 1.0010, the null control.
- All 32: 1.0191.

So on this host the engine's instructions are priced, about 0.19% of a CABAC stream's time for each instruction a
regular bin. This holds for instructions off the chain from one bin to the next, as the probe's are. A cut of
instructions on the chain would also shorten its latency. The rule to build the cut was met.

**The cut, and why it was not queued.**

- **Design.** One 8-byte entry for each state and quarter of codIRange holds rangeLPS, its renormalized value and
  shift, and both next states, behind one table address.
- **Branch-free forms.** In six such formulations LLVM saved −1.6 to +2.3 instructions a regular bin. It
  re-materializes the comparison and the zero constants of the selections, and splits the entry's fields again.
- **The timed branch-free arm, `v2`** (`select_unpredictable`). Its build saved 1.55; an earlier build of the same form
  with named fields saved 2.3. It reads 0.9995 [0.9928, 1.0036] on all 32 and 1.0010 on the CABAC streams, no gain.
- **Plain `if`/`else` selects.** LLVM compiled a branch on the bin and saved 10.68 instructions a regular bin, but
  read **1.0243 [1.0115, 1.0316]** on the CABAC streams, 4 of 26 faster. The mispredictions cost more than the
  instructions, as the branch-free decision's design assumed.
- **Outcome.** Neither arm met the request rule. Both are kept: `rejected/h264-cabac-decision-v2` and
  `rejected/h264-cabac-decision-branch`. `v2` showed no gain and also needs a toolchain above the MSRV, so it is not
  proposed for a bundle.

What this leaves:

- **The engine.** Its instruction excess is real and priced, but safe Rust does not reach it: the compiler's
  selections, not the tables, set the count. The way to remove it is a decision whose instructions are fixed, the
  `asm!` DecodeDecision of the hot-path module.
  - The earlier assembly sites read 0.9995 locally ("Result: no site merged").
  - This probe says a cut of about 12 instructions a regular bin is worth about 2% of a CABAC stream on this host.
  - Such a site needs its instruction count measured against the safe decision first, and a bar-class A/B before
    the hot-path work.
- **The rest.** RBSP extraction by runs rather than bytes (about 80 instructions a macroblock) is a smaller cut for a
  bundle. The residual's block dispatch (about 260) is a round of its own ("Entropy round: the residual's block
  dispatch").

## Entropy round: the residual's block dispatch

### What the measurement says

The entropy breakdown ("Entropy decoding: the instruction excess by syntax element, and a decision probe") puts about
257 instructions a CABAC macroblock outside the engine in the residual's dispatch: three out-of-line layers a coded
block (`Cabac::residual`, then the instance's `significance_map` and `levels`, each with its prologue and the engine's
load and store), and the macroblock layer's walk over the blocks (`parse_residual_blocks`, `parse_4x4_block`,
`parse_8x8_block`, `coded_block_flag_inc`). That is about 2.5% of a stream's instructions, above the 1.5% a
plain-instruction round needs to show ("Why the MB layer's instruction cuts move little time").

**The probe** (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/residual-calls/`, plan and rule committed before the run). It adds 156
independent one-uop instructions to every coded block, at the start of `Cabac::residual`: the whole part doubled in
place, so it bounds what any cut of the part can gain. Callgrind: +156.3 a coded block, a median +2.0% of the
instructions over the 32 training streams, from +0.2% (sd and 4k streams with few coded blocks) to +7.0% (high-rate
1080p). Local timing (2.50 GHz class, directional; `ab3.py`, eight rounds, one thread pinned, `--discard`):

- CABAC streams: **1.0254 [1.0076, 1.0388]**, 18 of 26 slower;
- CAVLC streams, which call no `Cabac::residual`, the null control: 1.0017;
- all 32: 1.0198 [1.0017, 1.0317].

The instructions reach time about one for one (+2.0% instructions, +2.0% time), as the decision probe's did. The
rule to build the cut (CABAC median at least 1.010, lower end above 1.000) was met.

### Design

- **One call a coded block.** `Cabac::residual` is inlined into the caller's test of coded_block_flag and calls one
  function of the slice's instance (`Tier::residual`): the significance map and the levels, both inlined, and the
  check for data run past the end. Two calls, two prologues and one load and store of the engine go. `fast`'s
  `v3-entry` site now has two per-block functions, `residual` and `predict_fast`.
- **The luma bits in raster order from the coded_block_flag bits.** Without the 8x8 transform, a 4x4 block's bit of
  `cur_nb.cbf` is set exactly where it holds levels, and no other luma bit is set by then, so `nz` is those 16 bits.
  The 16-step loop that turned `luma_nz` from block order to raster order goes.
- **An 8x8 quadrant's four bits from one mask** (`quadrant`), where two four-step loops built them.
- **The 4x4 luma blocks in one loop** (`parse_4x4_blocks`), with what is the same for every block of the macroblock
  (the scan, maxNumCoeff and the scaling) taken once instead of per block. CAVLC's 8x8 transform, four interleaved 4x4
  lists, keeps a function of its own (`parse_4x4_of_8x8`).

Rejected:

- **The arguments only the levels read, behind one pointer** (`Levels`), so that the significance map's loop keeps
  more registers. It saved what the first form saved on a 720p stream and less on a high-rate one: the caller's stores
  of the struct cost more than the loop gained.
- **Separate functions for the two halves**, as before. Merged, the significance map's loop reloads two values a bin
  from the stack; still, one call a block saves 19 to 33 instructions a block net.
- **coded_block_flag decoded in the out-of-line function**, with the engine in registers: an empty block would then
  cost a call, and most blocks with a coded_block_flag bin in a coded quadrant are empty.

Instructions (callgrind, a tenth of the class frame counts): a median **0.9862** of `main`'s over the 32 training
streams, 31 of 32 fewer, from 0.9645 (high-rate 1080p) to 1.0000. The CAVLC streams gain too, from the 4x4 loop.

## Entropy decoding after the residual dispatch and the asm decision, and the CAVLC block parse

The breakdown above, measured again on the code of change A (the residual's block dispatch) and change B (DecodeDecision in
assembly), with the same method (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/entropy-after-483/`). Per macroblock, against FFmpeg
9.0.2:

| | CoreAV | FFmpeg | excess | before earlier changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CABAC (26): residual | 1,120 | 974 | +147 | +783 |
| CABAC: mvd and ref_idx | 267 | 126 | +141 | +186 |
| CABAC: MB header and loop, MB layer (read together) | 1,123 | 1,154 | −31 | +234 |
| CABAC: NAL/RBSP | 100 | 19 | +81 | +81 |
| CABAC: unassigned (wrappers, closures) | 130 | 0 | +130 | +93 |
| CABAC: total | 2,741 | 2,274 | **+467** | +1,377 |
| CAVLC (6): total | 1,491 | 834 | **+657** | +778 |

The engine runs 22.5 instructions a bin, against FFmpeg's `get_cabac` at 27.6 a call. On five of the six CAVLC
streams the entropy and MB-layer excess is 8% to 24% of the stream's instructions. The largest single piece is the
CAVLC residual block parse, `cavlc::block_body`.

**The CAVLC block parse: probe** (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cavlc-block-probe/`, plan and rule fixed before
each run). Per stream, `block_body` takes 0.5% to 26.8% of the instructions, 239 to 566 a call. The cut in view
works on bundle 2 item A's level reading and leaves `levels()` and `CoeffScale::apply` alone. It has four parts:

- the code tables built at compile time, one shape per syntax element;
- coeff_token's table found from nC by a table;
- run_before from one table of three bits, with the zeros-led code words of runs above 6 read from the leading-zero
  count;
- once no zeros are left, the remaining levels placed without further reads.

From base's machine code that predicts 35 instructions fewer a call, 25 a total_zeros read, 27 a run_before read and
4 a level: a median of 1.60% of a CAVLC stream's instructions. The probe added that many one-uop instructions at those
sites (verified within 5% of the prediction, 0.981 to 1.021 a stream, output identical). It read
**1.0168 [1.0029, 1.0304]** on the six
CAVLC streams, 6 of 6 slower, against the null control of the 26 CABAC streams at 0.9983. The rule (at least 1.010,
lower end above 1.000) was met. The price, about 1.7% of time for a median 1.6% of instructions, is near one to one.

**The cut as built** (`rejected/h264-cavlc-block`, `97514aa6`):

- **Tables.** coeff_token's tables have rows up to 15 leading zeros of 8 slots each, 128 slots a class. Class 3
  (8 <= nC) has six-bit code words of fixed length, and its slot is those six bits. total_zeros has rows up to 9 of
  4 slots, 64 a table. A slot is a `u16` holding the length and the values.
- **No bounds checks.** Every index is masked to its table's power-of-two size.
- **The window.** A new window always holds the first coeff_token whole, so that read has no refill test.

Results:

- **Instructions:** 0.10% to 3.81% fewer, a median of 1.04% over the six streams, two thirds of the prediction. Where
  the rest went is not measured; one place is the window, which the body keeps in memory around `levels()`.
- **Checks:** output identical on 64 of 64; conformance 291 of 291 at 1, 2 and 8 threads, 97 of 97 with scalar
  kernels and 97 of 97 without `fast`.
- **Local timing:** **0.9844 [0.9734, 1.0008]** on the six CAVLC streams (5 of 6 faster), 0.9971 on all 32, sd
  0.9918.

The condition for a gating run was a median of at most 0.990 with the upper end below 1.000. The upper end, 1.0008,
missed it, so the run ends there. The cut touches `cavlc.rs` only and sits on item A; bundle 2 ("Bundle 2: ten small changes together") brought it into `main` as item J.

- **Noise on the CAVLC streams.** `6f7799768413` read 1.0382 under the probe for 0.12% more instructions and 0.9849
  under the cut for 0.10% fewer. A single CAVLC stream's local reading carries a few percent of noise, and only the
  six-stream median is read.
- **The slowest CAVLC streams.** Against FFmpeg at one thread (`mb-layout-2/gating/analysis.txt`),
  `6f7799768413` reads 1.25, `b71b6b31e54f` 1.114 and `9db41aa16b5a` 1.085. At a tenth of the class frame counts,
  the window the breakdown above used, the parse is 0.5%, 4.2% and 5.2% of their instructions; at the class frame
  counts, which the timing uses, `cavlc.rs` is 18.3%, 9.3% and 6.1% of their cycles ("The slowest streams against
  FFmpeg"). The first tenth of `6f7799768413` runs 1,234 instructions a macroblock, its whole class frame count
  5,839.
- **What is left in the parse:** `levels()` (bundle 2 item A), the scaling of each level (bundle 2 item C), and a
  window set up and checked for each block. A window kept across a macroblock's residual is the next cut there. It
  changes the `Syntax` trait's block call in `mb.rs` and `syntax.rs`.

## Deblocking round: the kernels' setup in the form the tables give

### What the measurement says

A probe bounded the time the deblocking driver's per-macroblock setup could give back, before anything was built
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/deblock-setup-probe/`; `plan.txt` fixed the bound and the threshold before the run,
"For later probes: what a doubled call prices"). It counts only what a change of the setup removes, by the line of
`deblock_row` each instruction is inlined into: a luma edge's view (`EdgeMut::new`) and parameters
(`Thresholds::params`), a macroblock's chroma windows (`ChromaMbMut::new`) and its eight chroma `EdgeParams`, and the
AVX2 kernels' reading of the parameters (the spreads of t'C0 and bS, the clamps of alpha and beta). The bS derivation,
the QPs and `Thresholds::new` stay and are not counted. Bound per stream: those lines' instruction share plus their
excess of sampled time over it, in % of the time with the detected kernels (`bound.txt`):

| Class | bound, median | range | streams at 1.5% or more | luma windows | luma params | chroma windows | chroma params | kernels' reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sd | 4.23% | 2.89% to 5.50% | 8 of 8 | 0.69% | 0.63% | 1.08% | 0.87% | 0.82% |
| 720p | 5.33% | 2.77% to 8.41% | 8 of 8 | 0.92% | 0.83% | 1.44% | 1.05% | 1.06% |
| 1080p | 2.04% | 0.00% to 5.11% | 4 of 8 | 0.38% | 0.34% | 0.57% | 0.39% | 0.39% |
| 4k | 0.55% | 0.00% to 4.09% | 1 of 8 | 0.09% | 0.08% | 0.12% | 0.11% | 0.12% |

The threshold (an earlier change's 1.5%, applied to the median in any class) is cleared in three classes, so the setup is built.
At 720p the counted lines run 50 to 73 instructions a macroblock each (part medians); per line, the most are the
chroma slots' copy of eight 40-byte `EdgeParams` (42 a macroblock on `1d4b1775d78a`), the four t'C0 lookups of each
`params`, `EdgeMut::new`'s checked arithmetic, and the AVX2 kernel's clamps of alpha and beta (16 to 20). Two streams
have the filter off (0.00%). The bound is generous: it takes every counted instruction as removed, and every excess
as removable, where the chroma windows' lines carry most of it (0.94 points of 0.96 on `1d4b1775d78a`), on lines that
follow the data-dependent test of whether any chroma edge filters; part of that may be a misprediction's cost, which
a cheaper setup does not remove.

### Design

1. **`EdgeParams` in the tables' form.** The kernels' parameters become fourteen bytes: alpha and beta as bytes, the
   t'C0 row of Table 8-17 by boundary strength (`tc0[b]` for bS `b`, entries 0 and 4 to 7 zero from the decoder), and
   the four bS. The driver's `Thresholds` holds that row already, so an edge's parameters are a copy of its
   thresholds with the bS beside them, where they were four lookups and a 40-byte structure of `i32`s. A kernel picks
   each segment's t'C0 with one byte shuffle of the row by the bS (`segment_bytes`, the chroma `lanes`, through them
   the AVX-512 `thresholds`), and broadcasts alpha and beta from bytes without clamps. The bS indexes the row modulo
   8 (`EdgeParams::tc0_at` in the reference, an `and` before the shuffle in the vector kernels), so every kernel
   agrees with the reference on every input, in range or not, and the tests' and fuzz targets' inputs outside the
   tables now cover every byte value.
   Rejected:
   - building the 40-byte form faster in the driver: the kernels' clamps and spreads stay, a fifth of the bound;
   - a QP pair and the bS, the kernel doing the lookups: the tables would move into the kernels crate and each edge
     would look them up again, where the driver has the row in hand per macroblock pair;
   - alpha and beta as 16-bit values, for a 16-byte structure one vector load reads: an alpha above 32767 would need
     the clamps back to agree with the reference, and the decoder is 8-bit only (`decoder.rs` refuses other depths,
     and the planes are bytes).
2. **One luma window a macroblock (`LumaMbMut`).** Like the chroma window ("Kernel round: a macroblock's chroma
   edges in one call"), twenty rows of twenty samples, four above and four left of the block, checked once with
   checked arithmetic and a stride of at least twenty, so that the rows do not overlap. Its eight edges are views
   inside it (`vertical(e)`, `horizontal(e)`) made without a check of their own: the `EdgeMut` holds the whole window
   and the edge's offset. That is sound because no kernel relies on an edge's slice being exactly its samples: each
   checks its rows against the slice it holds (`rows_at_mut`, `gather`, the reference's checked `get` and `set`), and
   the window's geometry puts every line of its edges inside it, so those checks pass as before. Where the window
   does not fit (the plane holds less before the block: the first macroblock of a picture of one band, the first row
   of the first band of a picture of several, and a picture one macroblock wide) each edge is checked on its own, as
   before. `luma_edges` walks the edges and their thresholds once for both paths, and each path calls the kernel once
   per direction, so that the kernel's choice of direction still folds where the edge is built.
   Rejected:
   - a window per macroblock row, checked once a row: it would hold the plane across the row, which clearing a
     macroblock no slice covered also needs, and a macroblock's check is about ten instructions;
   - an exact slice per edge cut from the window: two compares and a branch an edge, for an exactness no kernel uses.
3. **Both chroma windows at once (`ChromaMbMut::pair`).** The two planes share the block's position and stride, so
   the range is worked out once and each plane's slice is taken from it, where two `ChromaMbMut::new` calls worked it
   out twice and paired the results through two `Option`s.

4. **The per-edge paths out of line.** The luma and chroma edges of a macroblock whose windows do not fit go through
   `luma_by_edges` and `chroma_by_edges`, `#[cold]` and not inlined, and each row's first sample is one offset a row
   (`luma_row`, `chroma_row`). Inlined, the luma path's second copy of the edge walk and of the kernels' dispatch made
   `deblock_rows` 19.4 KB where it is 15.1 KB on `main`; out of line it is 15.5 KB.

The bS derivation (`strengths`, `edge_strengths`, `Side`) is not touched; the MB layer layout round changes its motion
lookup. The `unsafe` in the changed kernel functions is register operations only; no pointer is formed differently,
and `docs/unsafe-sites.md` notes the window's edges.

Instructions on the first pictures of the 32 training streams (callgrind, AVX2 kernels; sd 90, 720p 30, 1080p 12, 4k
4 pictures), `k` over `base`: median 0.9787, 32 of 32 fewer; sd 0.9880, 720p 0.9697, 1080p 0.9817, 4k 0.9798 (on
`b366429`); rebased onto `70a4cec`, median 0.9752, 32 of 32 fewer; sd 0.9842, 720p 0.9687, 1080p 0.9803, 4k 0.9769. Output
is identical to `base` on the 32 streams at the class frame counts, at 1 and 8 threads with the detected kernels and
at 1 thread with the AVX2 and the scalar kernels.

A first local timing A/B of the code without point 4 (`fad4826`; one thread pinned, six rounds, the 32 streams; round
spreads up to 1.57 on this host) read, discard, 0.9932 [0.9899, 1.0017], 21 of 32 faster: sd 0.9906, 720p 0.9898,
1080p 0.9977, 4k 1.0087. The 4k streams that were slower barely filter (`f8d92a911e72`, whose bound is 0.07%: 1.0058
over fifteen alternated pairs). Their time had moved into the CABAC residual loops, which the round does not touch
but whose place in the binary it moves (`levels::<64>` from offset 32 of a 64-byte line to 0, `significance_map::<64>`
from 0 to 32); with every function aligned to 64 bytes in both builds the same stream read 1.0021. Placement differs
between any two builds ("Why the MB layer's instruction cuts move little time") and is not controlled here. Point 4
was added for the size of `deblock_rows` itself, and the bars below were moved to that code before it was timed; it

### Bars

These bars are fixed before any timing of the round. The method is that of the deblocking thresholds round, with the
harness options of "Measurement method: host faults inside a call", which apply to rounds whose bars are committed
after it:
- two decoders in the same rounds, built alike from one tree each (`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example
  decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset);
- on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106). The run records the class, and the script stops on any other host;
- `base` is `main` at `70a4cec`. `k` is the branch's code commit `e03cf436`: `base`'s tree plus this round's change to
  `deblock.rs` of `crates/coreav-h264` and to `lib.rs`, `scalar.rs`, `views.rs` and `simd/` of
  `crates/coreav-kernels-h264` (with their tests, fuzz targets and benchmark);

  command, `--shuffle-seed 20261026`, `--null-arm base`, and the in-call gate on `41e324ebb708.0.sd.h264` of the
  training set (`--gate-stream`, `--gate-every 4`, 300 frames); the eight-thread calls with `--min-seconds 3`, and
  the host-fault thresholds as calibrated in "Measurement method: host faults inside a call";

  bars.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| DS-1 | median per-stream ratio, `k` over `base`, one thread, discard (the primary) | at most **1.000**, and the upper end of its 95% interval below **1.000** |
| DS-2 | the same, write | at most **1.000** |
| DS-3 | the same per class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| DS-4 | the median over the 32 streams at eight threads, discard and write: a no-regression guard | at most **1.015** (1 + t, t the larger of 0.005 and the noise of that median at eight threads the method section publishes: about 1.5% either side) (per class, information) |
| DS-5 | output | the 32 training streams byte-identical to `base` with `k` at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads and with scalar kernels, on `k` |

DS-4 is measured with the harness's method for eight-thread arms whose calls last at least 3 s each, which the run uses once it is merged; on this host the eight-thread calls (0.17 to 0.7 s) fail the 10% round-spread rule. DS-4 is a no-regression guard, not a gain bar: the round removes per-macroblock work the threads share alike, so its expected gain at eight threads (about the one-thread 0.8% at most) does not clearly exceed the eight-thread noise the harness's calibration found even with calls of 3 s (the same binary against itself: per-stream deviation median 1.5%, p95 4.6%), and its tolerance is at least that noise as published for the all-32 median (the same binary against itself at eight threads, 95% range [0.9818, 1.0119] discard and [0.9838, 1.0119] write: t = 0.015). No other bar changes.

  the eight-thread calls ran again (`t8-aborted-2/` kept). That changed the gate, not the arms, and no ratio had been
  read.
- The eight-thread calls that count: none unresolved, 2 streams timed again, null deviation at most 6.4% (bar 8%).

The local A/B of the rebased commits had put the one-thread gain at 0.9857; the gating run measured 0.9848.

## Inter round: the placement checked once a band

**Result: rejected, by IP-2** (the eight-thread gain did not show; "Result" below). None of it is in `main`. The
code is on `rejected/h264-inter-place` (timed code `b6b5de86`, head `98e886ac`), a candidate for a bundle round.
Bundle 3 carried it at one thread and was rejected by its bar on the 1080p and 4k streams ("Bundle 3: one
thread's inter prediction at 1080p and 4k").

### What the measurement says

The PMU profile at `acf3ee2f` ranks inter prediction first in excess over FFmpeg at 4k (+0.056 of FFmpeg's cycles)
and second overall. Read again with each function named by its path (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/inter-place/`,
`plan-probe.md`), half of that excess at 4k (+0.034) and most of it overall (+0.024) is the safe placement
(`predict::place`), which turns a block's position and vector into checked offsets for the vector kernels; the
kernels themselves are at parity with FFmpeg's assembly. The placement is 147 instructions a macroblock over the 32
training streams, 2.4% of CoreAV's, run at five instructions a cycle. A probe that computed it twice cost 1.0475 of
`main`'s time (4k 1.0876), above the probe threshold fixed before the run, so the change was built.

On `1d4b1775d78a` (callgrind, per line), about 150 instructions a call were: the position and the planes' origins
bounded (23), the block's size (8), each weighting tested (6), the blocks written checked against the planes (20),
the reference's side (fractions, integer positions, window offsets and the interior test, 45), and moves and spills
(34). The first four depend on the picture being written and the block's shape, not on the vector.

### Design

`Kernels::predict_part` predicts the block `part` of macroblock `mb` and gives `Kernels::predict`'s result for the
same block, on the planes that a `Macroblocks` was found from. Three values carry checks made once, where their
inputs are made:

- `Macroblocks` (`PlanesMut::macroblocks`) holds the macroblock rows the picture's planes, or a band's, hold whole in
  every slice, the columns, where sample (0, 0) of each plane would sit, and the slice lengths it was found with. The
  decoder finds it each time it takes a band (`SliceDecoder::enter_row`), not for each block.
  A stride that is not a whole number of macroblocks, or first rows or origins past the bounds `place` assumes, hold
  none.
- `Part` is a block of 4, 8 or 16 samples each way inside its 16 by 16 macroblock, checked in `Part::new`. The
  decoder builds it where the block is chosen, before `motion_compensate`. The common shapes (P_Skip, direct 16x16,
  quadrants) are constants there, and their check folds away.
- `Ops` is the three planes' operations, each weighting tested by `Ops::new`. `Ops::PUT` and `Ops::AVG` are
  constants, so a block written or averaged, most blocks, is not tested. A weighted block is tested where the
  decoder converts its operations (`predict_fast_body`), as `place` tested it; one out of range goes the general
  way, as a block `predict` declined did.

Per block, `predict::place_part` compares the macroblock with the rows and columns held, each slice's length with the
length `Macroblocks` holds it to (the luma slice's, and the shorter chroma slice's; three comparisons), and the
reference's stride with the planes'. Then it computes the written offsets
from the macroblock, without bounds. The reference's side is `place`'s, shared as one function (`predict::read`),
so the windows are tested exactly as before. The kernels' safety contract is unchanged. Every region the vector
kernels read or write lies inside its slice. For the blocks written, it holds because the block lies inside its
macroblock, the macroblock's rows lie whole inside slices at least as long as those checked, and the offsets are
those `place` would compute. `simd::x86::predict::predict_placed` is the body both entry points share after their
placement, so the `unsafe` blocks are the ones `predict_body` had, with their comments now naming either placement.
`predict` stays as the general form (any position): it is the reference in the tests and the fuzz target.

Tests: `place_part` equals `place` wherever an independent per-row test says the planes hold the macroblock, and is
`None` elsewhere, over every existing placement test and a new one on macroblock-aligned pictures (bands, slack,
short slices, a luma or chroma band starting a row late, a different stride). `Macroblocks` is checked against the
same per-row test. Each slice cut below the length `Macroblocks` holds it to must be declined. Mutations of its first
and last rows, of the written chroma offset, of the row comparison and of each length comparison each fail them. The
three-plane equivalence test and the `predict` fuzz target run `predict_part` on every kernel set against `predict`,
with each slice in turn cut below its bound, which must be declined.

Instructions over `main` (`acf3ee2f`), callgrind, the callgrind class counts, as built in order
(`inter-place/instructions-round.txt`):

| stream | `Part` made in `motion_compensate` | made by its callers | and `Ops` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `41e324ebb708` (sd) | 0.9873 | 0.9723 | **0.9699** |
| `1d4b1775d78a` (720p) | 0.9951 | 0.9910 | **0.9904** |
| `175433794e02` (1080p) | 0.9984 | 0.9980 | **0.9977** |
| `3b1b441e23ae` (4k) | 0.9859 | 0.9704 | **0.9688** |
| `4b54de28c2b3` (4k) | 0.9958 | 0.9915 | **0.9909** |

With `Ops`, over the 32 streams: **0.9901**, all 32 below 1 (sd 0.9878, 720p 0.9913, 1080p 0.9944, 4k 0.9799), the
most 3.9% fewer (`b71b6b31e54f`, 0.9608).

Rejected:
- **A target checked once a macroblock.** A P_Skip macroblock, the most common inter macroblock, is one block, so
  its check would move rather than shrink. Once a band costs nothing a block sees.
- **The band's slices held in the target.** The decoder needs `&mut self` between blocks, so a target that borrows
  the band's planes cannot live across them. Comparing three lengths a block keeps the target a plain value.
- **`Part` made inside `motion_compensate`** (the first column above). That function is out of line, so the sizes
  are not constants there, and the check and the packing cost more than the size test they replace.
- **Keeping the per-block weighting test** (the second column). It is six instructions a block for a test that only
  weighted blocks need.
- **Replacing `predict`'s signature.** The general form is what the tests and fuzz target hold the new one to, and it
  serves callers that do not predict by macroblock.

### Bars (fixed before the timing run)

`base` is `main` at `acf3ee2f` (the code of `main` at `40cbc2e6`), and `p` the branch's code commit `b6b5de86`. Three arms,
`base`, `p` and a null arm (a second copy of `base`), built alike (`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example
decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset), with FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference command, seeded order,
calls of at least 3 s. Each bar is a median of per-stream ratios, `p` over `base`, with its 95% bootstrap interval.
One thread runs `scripts/h264_parity.py` on the helper VM class (Intel Xeon @ 2.90 GHz, family 6, model 106), pinned,
with the host-health gate before and after each call. Eight threads run `scripts/h264_parity_gcp.py` on
`c4-standard-16` with one thread a core, its bars and void rules, `--gate-threads 8`, and a cap of at most 10 USD.

| | measure | host | bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| IP-1 | one thread, discard, all 32 | helper VM | at most **0.995**, upper end below **1.000** |
| IP-2 | eight threads, discard, all 32 | `c4-standard-16` | at most **0.995**, upper end below **1.000** |
| IP-3 | write, all 32, one thread and eight threads | each its own | at most **1.000** each |
| IP-4 | each class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write, one thread and eight threads | each its own | at most **1.005** |
| IP-5 | output | | `p` byte-identical to `base` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 in fast and safe modes, AVX2 and scalar kernels |
| IP-6 | eight threads, discard, the 64 streams of the held-out draw (`docs/measurements/h264-n2-heldout/list.json`), five rounds | `c4-standard-16` | at most **1.000** |

IP-5 is met (`inter-place/identity-round.txt`, `conformance-round.txt`; the `predict` fuzz target ran 600 s, 2.4
million inputs, with the slice cuts, without a failure). Sizing: one thread's noise on the helper VM is about 0.6 to 0.7% either side. IP-1
asks for half of the median instruction cut (0.99) in time, the rate an earlier change found for instruction cuts; the
coefficient-table round moved by a fifth of its cut, so IP-1 may well not be met. Eight threads' noise on
`c4-standard-16` is about 0.1%, several times below IP-2's margin.
IP-6 holds the claim to streams the round never saw: the variants above were chosen by instruction counts on
training streams. It is a guard against a loss, as bundle 2's B2-7 is, and shares IP-2's cap.

The change ships if `p` meets IP-1 to IP-6. One run decides, and a re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a host
fault as the host's void rules define it.

A gating run is requested only if a local interleaved timing on the helper VM class shows IP-1's gain: `base`, `p`
and the null arm, one thread pinned, CPU time, six rounds over the 32 streams at the class frame counts, discard
(`inter-place/ab1t.py`), median at most 0.995 with the upper end of its interval below 1.000; and eight threads,
five rounds, discard, median at most 1.000, a guard against a loss. If the one-thread interval spans 1.000, the
change is a small gain: it is not gated alone, and it waits on a `rejected/` branch for a bundle round.

## Deblocking round: macroblocks below the thresholds

At one thread on the bar class, 23 of the 32 training streams are slower than FFmpeg 9.0.2 (`main` after an earlier change,
`mb-layout-2/gating/analysis.txt`, call `g`, discard). This section asks what the ten slowest have in common, ranks
the causes by the streams each would move, and takes the one that a single change can remove. Evidence: the
ranking in `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/slow-streams/`, the round in `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/deblock-quiet/`.

### The slowest streams against FFmpeg

**Method.** The PMU profile of "Again at `acf3ee2f`, ranked by excess over parity", run again with its `job.sh ipc`
on the same host class (Compute Engine `c4-standard-8`, Emerald Rapids at 2.30 GHz). The binary that run profiled was
not kept, so the run profiles one built from `main` at `dd85b381`, whose decoder is `acf3ee2f`'s. `per_stream.py`
splits the samples by stream: each stage's cycles as a share of the same stream's FFmpeg cycles. `causes.py` joins
each stream's coding features (`snapshot-outliers/features.tsv`, bits a macroblock from the elementary streams'
sizes). It also splits inter prediction, reconstruction and deblocking into a driver and kernels: CoreAV's Rust
around its SIMD modules, against FFmpeg's C functions around its assembly. The host is not the bar class: its cycle
ratios order the streams much as the bar class does, but the levels differ (`36501d448eaa` 1.144 here, 1.285 there).

**What the ten slowest have in common.** Over the 32 streams, the ratio to FFmpeg rises with bits a macroblock
(correlation +0.53 with its logarithm). Being CAVLC, B-frames, weighted prediction, slices and picture size do less
(each within ±0.21). The excess falls into six causes (`run/causes.txt`; excess as a share of FFmpeg's cycles, the
mean over the ten slowest first):

| | Cause | Excess, 10 slowest / all 32 | Streams it would move (bar-class ratio) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CABAC entropy decoding with the MB layer, read together since FFmpeg inlines its MB layer into its entropy functions. Most of it is in the residual and grows with bits a macroblock. The residual dispatch and the asm decision, in gating, cut its instructions from +1,377 to +467 a macroblock against FFmpeg ("Entropy decoding after the residual dispatch and the asm decision"). | +0.064 / +0.057 | `c7ecda16e4a7` 1.220 (+0.084), `4b54de28c2b3` 1.207 (+0.086), `b41f70a7fa60` 1.196 (+0.078), `36501d448eaa` 1.285 (+0.067), `65ec61f95a00` 1.163 (+0.066), and outside the ten `6da34958296c`, `278dbf5a63bb`, `76e0b1692494` (+0.07 to +0.10) |
| 2 | Deblocking of macroblocks whose QP is below the thresholds: no edge can filter a sample, yet the driver derives every strength and walks every edge. | in deblocking's +0.045 / +0.024 | `4b54de28c2b3`, `36501d448eaa`, `a6af290d9053` 1.151, `f8d92a911e72` 1.146, `6e90422a670a` 1.139, and five streams already faster than FFmpeg |
| 3 | CAVLC syntax and the MB layer. On `6f7799768413` they run 2,519 instructions a macroblock against FFmpeg's 1,421, and `cavlc.rs` takes 18.3% of its cycles. | (one stream of the ten) | `6f7799768413` 1.250 (+0.190), `b71b6b31e54f` 1.114 (+0.084), `9db41aa16b5a` 1.085 (+0.057), `5185721dda11` 1.024 (+0.125) |
| 4 | Deblocking of the macroblocks that do filter: the driver is 1.3 to 1.7 times FFmpeg's on P-only streams at moderate QP. | in deblocking's +0.045 | `6f7799768413` (+0.088 deblocking), `3c593b8f0809` 1.189 (+0.057), `65ec61f95a00` (+0.052), `c7ecda16e4a7` (+0.048) |
| 5 | Reconstruction's driver, mostly the scaling of each level (`CoeffScale::apply`, `prepare_level_scales`), which grows with bits a macroblock (+0.90). Bundle 2's item C aims at it. | +0.018 / −0.003 | `175433794e02` 1.154 (+0.038), `a6af290d9053` (+0.033), `6e90422a670a` (+0.027), `f8d92a911e72` (+0.026), `6f7799768413` (+0.037) |
| 6 | Inter prediction's driver (`prefetch.rs`, `predict.rs`, `inter.rs`), +0.047 / +0.075, mostly offset by kernels faster than FFmpeg's (−0.030 / −0.047). What is left is largest on low-rate streams with B-frames. | net +0.018 / +0.028 | `b41f70a7fa60` (+0.053 net), `4b54de28c2b3` (+0.058), `36501d448eaa` (+0.046), `b71b6b31e54f` (+0.062), `76e0b1692494` (+0.065) |

No single cause moves most of the 23 slower streams below 1.00. Cause 1 is the largest and appears on every CABAC
stream, but earlier changes change it, so it is measured again once they merge. Cause 2 is the one a single change
removes, since the spec says exactly which macroblocks it concerns, so this round takes it. Cause 3 reopens the CAVLC
items left for later (the block parse, `rejected/h264-cavlc-block`, and a window kept across a macroblock's residual)
for `6f7799768413`.

### What the measurement says

- **QPs.** Five of the ten slowest are coded at QPs low enough that the filter changes little. Slice QPs over the
  class frame counts, from FFmpeg's `trace_headers` filter (`qp.sh`, `run/qp.txt`), with the mean FilterOffsetA:
  `36501d448eaa` 13.3 (9 to 20), offset 0; `4b54de28c2b3` 10.4 (10 to 22), 0; `6e90422a670a` 19.9, −10.6;
  `a6af290d9053` 26.5, −11.4; `f8d92a911e72` 17.3, −1.3. Below an indexA of 16, α' is 0 (Table 8-16), and below an
  indexB of 16, β' is. mb_qp_delta moves a macroblock's QP away from its slice's, so the count below is taken by
  macroblock.
- **The share of macroblocks no edge can filter.** A counting build (`count.diff`; `run/deblock-counts.txt`, the class
  frame counts) counts macroblocks whose QP and whose filtered neighbours' QPs are all below the first QP whose luma
  or chroma thresholds are not 0. They are 98% of `f8d92a911e72`'s macroblocks, 91% of `6e90422a670a`'s, 85% of
  `4b54de28c2b3`'s, 66% of `a6af290d9053`'s and 59% of `36501d448eaa`'s, and 80% to 100% of five 4k streams. On
  `f8d92a911e72`, `6e90422a670a` and `a6af290d9053` almost every one of them has an edge whose bS is not 0, so the
  driver goes past its test for all-zero strengths and walks the edges. Round 7 skips such edges one at a time at
  the kernel call, after the strengths.
- **The cost.** On those three streams deblocking runs 837, 861 and 1,292 instructions a macroblock against FFmpeg's
  214, 310 and 894. The kernels take 0.002 to 0.024 of FFmpeg's cycles and the driver 0.047 to 0.052, against
  FFmpeg's 0.010 to 0.022.

### Design

Before the strengths, a macroblock whose QPY and whose left and top neighbours' (where the filter crosses into them)
are all below the slice's **first live QP** is passed over.

- **The first live QP** is the lowest QPY at which an edge's thresholds can filter, for luma or for either chroma
  plane. It is exact by three facts:
  - an edge's thresholds come from the average of two of the macroblocks' QPs, or of their QPC for chroma, and that
    average is at most their maximum's;
  - QPC (Table 8-15) and α' and β' (Table 8-16) do not decrease;
  - where α' or β' is 0, no sample passes filterSamplesFlag (Equation 8-468), whatever bS.
- **Its cost.** Four lookups in tables built at compile time:
  - the lowest average with α' above 0 for FilterOffsetA, and likewise with β' for FilterOffsetB; the larger of the
    two is luma's first live QP;
  - for each chroma plane, the lowest index of the QPC table that reaches that average, less the plane's offset.
  It is held for the slice and taken again when a row starts or the slice changes.
- **The test.** It reads the QPs as coded: QPY is 0 to 51, since the decoder takes 8-bit pictures only, so an I_PCM
  macroblock's QP is at least the 0 the filter uses for it, and the test stays safe. It checks the macroblock's own QP
  first, so where that QP is live it costs one comparison.
- **Checks.** Two unit tests check the first live QP against a search of every QP:
  - it equals the search for every FilterOffsetA and FilterOffsetB of −12 to 12 and the tables' ends, and every pair
    of chroma offsets of −12 to 12;
  - no pair of QPs below it filters, for luma or either chroma plane, with the offsets in steps of 3 over the same
    ranges (the thresholds rise with their index, so the first test and that sample cover the rest).

Rejected:

- **A search of the 52 QPs for the first live one,** held for the call. The decoder filters a row at a time, so the
  search ran for every row: 65 instructions a macroblock on a picture 20 macroblocks wide.
- **The maximum of the three QPs by `luma_qp`, which tests for I_PCM, through an iterator.** It cost 30 to 40
  instructions a macroblock on streams with nothing to pass over: 1.8% more on `6b18d9f0f88d`.
- **Precomputing the first live QP with each slice's filter parameters.** At the end of a picture the filter takes
  the chroma offsets of the picture's first slice, so a value computed from each slice's own parameter set could
  differ from the filter's.

**Instructions** (callgrind, one thread, discard, the class frame counts; `run/instructions.txt`):

- 10 of the 32 streams lose 1.5% or more, the plain-instruction cut that an earlier change found time can show. They are `81ed4778ece2`
  −11.1%, `ed75c044e944` −10.6%, `ae16bb7c7192` −8.7%, `e624cbe0d2be` −8.4%, `4b54de28c2b3` −8.4%, `f8d92a911e72`
  −7.3%, `6e90422a670a` −6.2%, `a6af290d9053` −3.3%, `3b1b441e23ae` −3.3% and `36501d448eaa` −2.3%.
- These ten are the **target streams** of the bars below, fixed before any timing.
- The other 22 change by −0.94% to +0.16%, a median of −0.02%.

Output is identical on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads (`run/identity.txt`). Conformance passes 97 of 97
at 1, 2 and 8 threads with detected kernels, with scalar kernels and without `fast` (`run/conformance.txt`).

### Bars (fixed before the timing runs)

`base` is `main` at the commit the branch is based on; `k` is the branch's code commit. T is the ten target streams
above, R the other 22.

| | measure | bar |
|---|---|---|
| QZ-1 | median per-stream ratio, `k` over `base`, one thread pinned, discard, T (the primary) | at most **0.975**, and the upper end of its 95% interval below **1.000** |
| QZ-2 | the same, write, T | at most **0.985** |
| QZ-3 | the same, discard, R | at most **1.003** |
| QZ-4 | one thread pinned, all 32, discard and write; each class, discard and write | at most **1.000**; at most **1.005** in each |
| QZ-5 | eight threads, discard, all 32; T; each class | at most **1.000**; at most **1.000**; at most **1.010** in each |
| QZ-6 | one thread pinned, discard, the 64 held-out streams (`docs/measurements/h264-n2-heldout/list.json`) | at most **1.000** |
| QZ-7 | output | `k` byte-identical to `base` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads, with and without `fast`; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads, with and without `fast`, detected and scalar kernels |

QZ-1 asks of T's median instruction cut, about 8%, a third in time. QZ-3 and QZ-4 ask that the streams with nothing
to pass over, and no class, pay for it. QZ-6 asks that it holds on streams no step of this round has seen.

Method: as the residual dispatch round's. `scripts/h264_parity.py` with `--shuffle-seed 20261026 --null-arm base
--gate-stream 36501d448eaa.0.720p.h264 --gate-every 4`, one call per class and mode: one thread pinned to core 2 at
twenty rounds, eight threads unpinned at ten, and the held-out streams at one thread pinned. The host-health gate
runs before and after each call, as HOST-GATE.md describes, on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106). The
harness's host checks are those `main` has when the run starts. A stream still `unresolved` after its retries stays
in the medians and is listed. A call is void only where the host-health gate fails. `analyze.py` in the evidence
directory prints the bars from the calls' reports. The change ships if `k` meets QZ-1 to QZ-7; otherwise this section
records the result and the change stays out. One valid run decides, and a re-run of the same arms is allowed only for
a recorded host fault. The ratio to FFmpeg 9.0.2 and the share of streams faster than it, overall and per class, for

## Threading round: the aprons' rows asked for ahead

### What the probe says

Probe AP (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/apron-copies/plan-probe.md`, Compute Engine `c4-standard-16`, `main` at
`13e4dfc4`): not copying the aprons' samples at all reads **0.9810** [0.9666, 0.9888] of the eight-thread wall time
over the 32 training streams (sd 0.9508, 720p 0.9779, 1080p 0.9907, 4k 0.9893), and copying them twice 1.0046 (sd
1.0072). A second copy costs a quarter to a seventh of what not copying saves, so most of the price is not the
bytes moved but the misses on the rows written: a band's buffer is reused from an older picture, often decoded on
another core, and of its top apron only the 4 luma and 2 chroma rows of the entry copy are written between the
buffer's reuse and the refresh (`Canvas::enter`, `Canvas::refresh_top`), which writes 23 luma and 9 chroma rows a
band one macroblock row later. The macroblocks' own rows do not pay this: from 720p up their lines are asked for a
cache line ahead ("Round 12"); the apron's are not asked for at all.

### Design

Three changes, in `picture.rs` and `mb.rs`:

1. **The apron's rows asked for ahead.** In the first macroblock row of a band (`k > 0`), the macroblock row whose
   end triggers the refresh, `SliceDecoder::request_apron` asks for the lines the refresh will write: each first
   macroblock of four asks for its 64-byte line of every luma apron row the entry copy did not write, each first
   of eight for its line of every such chroma row (`prefetch::rows_for_write`, the hint the macroblocks' own rows
   use). Spread so, the whole apron is asked for once by the row's end, at most 22 luma hints every four
   macroblocks and 8 a chroma plane every eight; asked for all at once, in `Canvas::enter`, the 360 lines of an sd
   apron would exhaust the core's fill buffers and wait like the copy does. It is not under `ahead`: an sd picture
   is below the 1 MiB at which a one-thread picture asks for its rows, but at eight threads its band buffers come
   back cold all the same, and sd is where the aprons cost most. A field set when a macroblock row starts,
   `apron_rows`, is non-zero only in a band's first row; a picture of one band (one thread) never sets it, so its
   only cost there is a branch a macroblock that is never taken.
2. **Entry copies of one row.** Between entering a band and its refresh, only intra prediction reads the apron, one
   luma row and one chroma row above the band (the deblocking filter, which reads four rows across the edge, runs
   after the refresh): `ENTRY_LUMA` 4 to 1 and `ENTRY_CHROMA` 2 to 1. The rows dropped there are then asked for
   ahead with the rest, and 4 of the 38 rows-of-width a band copied are no longer copied.
3. **One copy per run.** `copy_top` copied row by row; rows that come from the same band are consecutive in its
   buffer and in this one, a stride each, so each run is now one copy (`runs`): two or three luma copies a band
   where there were 23, and two or three a chroma plane where there were 9.

What it leaves: the entry row itself is written cold (one luma and one chroma row a band), and the refresh still
moves the bytes, which the `twice` arm prices at about 0.5% (0.7% at sd).

Rejected: asking for the lines in `Canvas::enter`, all at once (above); asking a macroblock row earlier, in the band
above's last row, which would need the band below's buffer while the one above is held, and leaves the lines longer
in a cache the decode is filling; a non-temporal or streaming copy, which writes around the cache the readers of the
band (the next band's predictions and filter) then miss in; dropping the apron (an earlier change ranks the alternatives, and
reading across bands is what the aprons exist to avoid); taller bands (`perf/h264-aprons`: bands of two rows at sd
were 8% slower at eight threads, and bundle 2 settles the 32-to-63-row case); `prefetchw` in place of `prefetcht0`,
which belongs to the prefetch module and would change every write hint (a separate measurement of the write hints).

are recorded in the result.

What the arms say: asked for as reads (`prefetcht0`), the apron's lines cost more than they save, 3.6% at sd; asked
for to be owned (`prefetchw`), the same lines save 1.0% over the 32 and 1.7% at sd, every stream faster. A reused
band buffer's lines were last read by other cores, whose predictions took the older picture's rows from them, so
they sit shared in those cores' caches: a read hint fetches a shared copy, and the copy's store still has to take the
line from the other cores, a second trip for each line; an ownership hint makes one. The copies' own changes (entry
rows, runs) are worth 0.4% on their own. The next round builds `kw`'s form with the hint the kernels crate offers.

## Threading round: the aprons' rows owned ahead

The round above, with the hint its information arm `kw` measured: the apron's lines asked to be owned
(`prefetchw`), not read. Its Compute Engine run put `kw` at 0.9904 [0.9882, 0.9915] over the 32 at eight threads,
sd 0.9829, every stream faster, where the read hints alone (`kh`) lost 3.6% at sd.

### Design

As the round above (entry copies of one row, one copy per run, the apron's lines asked for over the band's first
macroblock row), with two changes:

1. **Ownership hints.** `coreav_kernels_h264::prefetch::Ownership` is the right to issue `prefetchw`:
   `Ownership::detect` grants it where CPUID says the CPU has the instruction (leaf 0x8000_0001, ECX bit 8,
   PRFCHW; asked once and kept, as CPUID may leave to the hypervisor), and `Ownership::rows` walks rows as
   `rows_for_write` does. The instruction is written as `asm!`: its target feature, `prfchw`, is not stable to
   enable, and `_mm_prefetch` with `_MM_HINT_ET0` emits `prefetcht0` without it. A slice takes the right when it
   starts; without it a band's first row asks for nothing, as `kh` showed read hints cost more than they save there.
   The change would add one `unsafe` site and the CPUID calls to the kernels crate's SIMD module, listed in
   `docs/unsafe-sites.md` on its branch. `hint_write` and the macroblocks' own hints stay `prefetcht0`: whether they gain from ownership is
   the prefetch work's to measure.
2. **Out of line.** `request_apron` is `#[inline(never)]`, so the start of a macroblock keeps one compare where `k`
   inlined the walk; `k` cost 1.0027 at one thread, where it never runs.

Rejected: `prefetchw` for every write hint (above); `prefetcht0` where the CPU lacks `prefetchw` (`kh`: slower);
asking the operating system or the allocator for fresh pages instead of reusing buffers (a first touch costs more,
`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/first-touch/`).

## Threading round: the aprons' rows owned ahead, the decoder's layout kept

The round above, which met its eight-thread bars (0.9941, sd 0.9861) and missed its one-thread guard by the layout
its two new fields gave the decoder.

### Design

As the round above, except where the hint's state lives. `SliceDecoder::ahead`, a flag, becomes `hints`, a byte
holding `HINT_AHEAD` (the macroblocks' own lines, as before) and `HINT_APRON` (a band's first row, on a CPU with
`prefetchw`): the same size, so no field moves. A macroblock's start tests the byte once where no hint is issued (sd at
one thread, as before), and compares it with `HINT_AHEAD` where only the macroblocks' hints are (one compare more);
any other set goes to `request_hints`, out of line and cold. `request_apron` finds the rows to ask for from the band
(`rows_refreshed_first`) and the right to ask from `Ownership::detect` (kept after the first call) when it runs,
rather than from fields. The reference hints in `inter.rs` test `HINT_AHEAD`.

Rejected: the two fields of the round above (its one-thread result); a second, monomorphized macroblock loop for
pictures of more than one band, which would compile the whole loop twice for a hint.

## Bundle 2: ten small changes together

### Why

Ten changes were each shown correct (identical output on the training set, conformance, their tests) and each left
out because its gain alone was below what a run resolves, or, for round 23's CAVLC level reading, because one run
missed on a stream its code does not touch. Unlike round 25's bundle, each item here was drawn only from parts with a
measured effect of their own, and each bar sits on the host and class where its gain is expected. The plan, each
item's own reading, the overlaps and the bars are in `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/bundle2/plan.md`, committed with
the composition before any timing.

### The items

| | item | where its design is described | what the code now does |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | CAVLC levels | "Round 23: the CAVLC level loop" (written anew on `cavlc::block_body`) | below a prefix of 14, level_prefix, its terminating one and level_suffix are read as one field and consumed by one skip; levelCode becomes a level without a branch; a prefix of 14 or more goes out of line to clause 9.2.2.1's three cases |
| B | chroma intra prediction from one view of both planes | "Kernel round: chroma intra prediction from one view of both planes" | one checked view of both chroma planes (`ChromaIntraMut`, through `IntraRows::pair`), beside an earlier change's `ChromaMbMut::pair` for the deblocking filter |
| C | coefficient scalings from per-QP tables | "Reconstruction round: coefficient scalings from per-QP tables" | `CoeffTables` holds the scalings of every QP for the scaling lists in use, kept in `Spare` across slices and pictures and rebuilt only when its key (the lists and chroma QP offsets) changes; a macroblock points `LevelScales` at its QP's entries once (`prepare_level_scales`), and every residual path takes them from there, an earlier change's per-macroblock 4x4 and 8x8 paths included |
| D | band views kept for the slice | "Threading round: band views kept for the slice" | a reference band's `Planes` view is kept per (reference, band) for the slice |
| E | slack rows at the picture's edges in every layout | "Threading round: slack rows at the picture's edges in every layout" | a band's origin depends on the band (`luma_origin(k)`, `chroma_origin(k)`), taken once a row in an earlier change's per-row offsets |
| F | deblocking thresholds from a table by average QP | "Deblocking round: thresholds by average QP, and only live edges" | rewritten on change A's `Thresholds` (alpha and beta as bytes, t'C0 by bS): the table, keyed by the slice's two filter offsets and kept across pictures, is built by `Thresholds::of_average`, and the luma edges, the cold per-edge path and the chroma edges read `ThresholdTable::get`; `Thresholds::new` stays for the tests. That section's second point, the live-edge masks, was not taken. Change B's pass over macroblocks below the first live QP runs before it and is unchanged |
| G | bands of 4 rows at 32 to 63 macroblock rows | rule 4 above ("Band height") | `Geometry::band_mbs_for` gives 4 where the rule gives 2 |
| H | RBSP by runs | here | `nal::rbsp` copies the bytes between emulation-prevention bytes as runs: a removed byte is a 3 after two zeros, never one of the zeros before the next, so the test needs no state, and only a zero lets such a byte be one or two bytes on, so after any other byte the search moves on three. `runs_remove_what_the_byte_loop_removes` checks it against the byte-at-a-time loop |
| I | a chroma apron of 11 rows | rule 2 above (readers) | `TOP_CHROMA` is `(TOP_LUMA - 2).div_ceil(2)`, 11 rows: a block's chroma window is read from the band of its luma window, whose last row may be one of the filtered rows above the band, so the hot path no longer declines chroma windows above the 9-row apron |
| J | the CAVLC block parse from compile-time code tables | "Entropy decoding after the residual dispatch and the asm decision, and the CAVLC block parse" | coeff_token and total_zeros from tables built at compile time (each index masked to its table's power-of-two size), coeff_token's table found from nC by a table, run_before from one table of three bits, the remaining levels placed without further reads once no zeros are left; on A's level reading |

E and I store more per banded picture (slack rows at the picture's edges, 11 chroma apron rows rather than 9), and
G's bands of 4 at 32 to 63 rows change the number of bands; `stored_bytes` counts both, so a `max_memory_bytes` set
just under the former need at eight threads now gives a limit error. With one thread a picture is one band and its
size is unchanged. 576-line sd (36 macroblock rows) takes bands of 4 under G; 480-line sd keeps bands of 1.

## CAVLC round: one bit window across a macroblock's residual

### What the measurement says

`6f7799768413` is the slowest of the 32 streams against FFmpeg at one thread (1.250). Its gap is in the CAVLC syntax
and the MB layer, and `cavlc.rs` takes 18.3% of its cycles ("The slowest streams against FFmpeg"). At the class frame
counts the block parse runs 7.60 M times on it, out of line, at 220 instructions a call: 15.0% of its instructions
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cavlc-window-probe/`, `counts.txt`).

From the machine code, about 56 instructions of each call are fixed cost:
- the closure's captures stored and reloaded;
- the call, with six registers saved and restored;
- a new bit window: a bounds check, a load and a byte swap;
- the reader's checked skip at the end;
- the `Result` returned.

A probe added 45 independent one-uop instructions at each 4x4 block call: 1.78% of a CAVLC stream's instructions
(median), 3.5% on `6f7799768413`. It read **1.0196 [1.0124, 1.0317]** on the six CAVLC streams, 6 of 6 slower,
against a CABAC null control of 1.0035. That met its rule (at least 1.010, lower end above 1.000). The price is about
one to one, as for the CAVLC block parse probe.

### Design

- **One window a residual.** `CavlcSyntax` keeps a `cavlc::Window` from `Syntax::begin_residual` to
  `Syntax::end_residual`, which `parse_residual_cavlc` calls around the macroblock's blocks. Each block reads from
  it, with a refill check before coeff_token in place of a new window. The position is checked against the end of the
  RBSP once, at the end. A block reads at most about 1,100 bits (16 escaped levels) and a residual at most 25
  blocks; past the end the window reads zeros, so a truncated residual fails at that check or earlier, as
  `Truncated`. For CABAC the two calls do nothing.
- **No call a block.** The CAVLC `block` is `cavlc::block_in` on that window, inlined into the residual's loop. That
  loop already runs in the slice's instance of the hot paths (`parse_residual` enters it), so the per-block
  `tier.enter` goes.
- **Kept:** the reads themselves (bundle 2's items A and J), the placement and the scaling. `block_body`, a block on
  a window of its own, stays for the tests.

Rejected:
- **One out-of-line function a block shape taking the window.** That keeps the call, the saved registers and the
  captures, about two thirds of the fixed cost the probe priced.
- **The window in the `BitReader`.** Every other syntax element reads through it, so a change there touches the whole
  CAVLC parse and the slice header. The residual is the one place where many elements are read with nothing else in
  between.

Results:
- **Instructions:** −0.94% to −5.72%, a median of **−3.21%** on the six CAVLC streams (−5.72% on `6f7799768413`),
  1.35 to 1.87 times the prediction. With the call gone, the compiler also keeps the window and the block's context in
  registers across the loop. The CABAC streams do not change.
- **Checks:** output identical to `base` on the 32 streams at 1 and 8 threads (64 of 64); conformance 291 of 291 at
  1, 2 and 8 threads, 97 of 97 with scalar kernels and 97 of 97 without `fast`. The v3-against-baseline test now reads
  each case's blocks through one window and compares the positions and the end.
- **Local timing** (`ab3.py`, eight rounds, one thread pinned, the 32 streams): CAVLC 6 **0.9769 [0.9718, 0.9851]**,
  6 of 6 faster; `6f7799768413` 0.9715; all 32 0.9949, 27 of 32 faster. The plan's condition for a gating run (CAVLC 6
  at most 0.990 with the upper end below 1.000, all 32 at most 1.000) is met.
