## Kernel round: boundary strengths in vector registers

**Result: shipped**, BS-1 to BS-5 met (one thread 0.9802, eight threads 0.9891; "Result" below).

### What the measurement says

- The probe (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/bs-probe/`, its plan committed before any measurement) bounds what a
  kernel that derives a macroblock's boundary strengths could save: everything `strengths` in `deblock.rs` ran (the
  neighbours' records and heads, the masks, the motion comparisons, `split_strengths` and
  `differing_motion_strength`) and `deblock_row`'s test of the result for all zeros, taken as removed. The median
  bound is 9.31% (sd), 6.00% (720p), 4.09% (1080p) and 12.22% (4k) of the detected-kernel time, above an earlier change's 1.5% in
  every class. By part: the path of macroblocks with one motion 3.22%, 2.89%, 1.56% and 8.31%; the path where a
  macroblock or a neighbour carries more than one motion ("split") 2.88%, 1.38%, 1.31% and 0.26%;
  `differing_motion_strength` 1.22%, 0.86%, 0.34% and 0.12%; the test for all zeros 1.08%, 1.01%, 0.46% and 3.14%.
  The test is 8 instructions a macroblock, and its time is the branch on the result, which a kernel keeps.
- On the path with one motion, the comparison of two motions cost about 14 instructions with three branches: the
  compiler made the field-wise `==` an 8-byte compare of the vectors, then a vector compare of the four reference
  bytes. It was the costliest line of the derivation (callgrind, 4k stream `3b1b441e23ae`, 30 pictures, AVX2
  kernels: 11.7M of the derivation's 50M instructions).
- Developing the change found three costs that are not the derivation's own (same stream and tool):
  - Routing every macroblock through one out-of-line kernel was slower (quick pinned pairs, about 5% noise: sd
    1.011, 720p 1.038, 4k 1.057). The call needs the macroblock's description in memory (about 44 instructions a
    macroblock to build it) and a longer test of which kind of motion each side carries.
  - Moving `Motion` into the kernels crate left `SliceDecoder::store_mb` out of line: 6.8M instructions in it and
    2.5M more in `inter_pred`, 0.94% of the run.
  - The first build of the AVX-512 kernel used 512-bit registers. The compiler merged two adjacent 32-byte reads of
    the top neighbour's last row, and the two-source permutes over them, into one 64-byte read and three 512-bit
    permutes: the crate is built for the x86-64 baseline, without the tuning that prefers 256-bit vectors, so any
    function with AVX-512 F may get them. A local timing run (below) put that build at 1.0141 [1.0062, 1.0183] over
    the same code without the kernel, and at 1.0252 at 4k, where the kernel rarely runs. That fits what this host
    (Ice Lake-SP, model 106) does while 512-bit instructions run, lowering the core's clock for everything around
    them (not measured directly: this VM has no PMU). The decoder has no other 512-bit register.

### Design

1. `Motion` moves to `coreav-kernels-h264` (`strengths.rs`), `repr(C)`, twelve bytes without padding (a
   compile-time assertion), and `picture.rs` re-exports it. The derivation moves with it, as it was, into the
   reference of a new trait method, `Kernels::strengths`, which takes a macroblock and its usable neighbours
   (`StrengthMb`: each side's motion, `Motions::One` or `Motions::Each`, its coefficient mask and whether it is
   intra, and the transform size) and returns the 32 strengths in the words `deblock_row` reads.
   `differing_motion_strength` becomes `motion_strength`, unchanged except where neither block uses a list: it gives
   0 there, as clause 8.7.2.1 has nothing to compare. No decoded inter block uses neither list, and intra blocks are
   settled before any comparison, so the output is unchanged.
2. `deblock.rs`'s `strengths` keeps the path where the macroblock and both neighbours carry one motion inlined
   (`uniform_strengths`, from the heads, as before), and builds the description and calls `Kernels::strengths` only
   for the others.
3. `Auto` sends those to the AVX-512 tier's kernel where the CPU has it, and inlines the reference elsewhere (AVX2,
   arm64, `Scalar`). The kernel (`simd/avx512/strengths.rs`):
   - holds eight blocks a vector, one 32-bit lane a block, each of a block's three fields (list 0's vector, list
     1's, and the four reference bytes) in its own vector;
   - makes the reference field canonical, (unused 0, unused 1, picture 0, picture 1) with a list's picture 0 where
     the list is unused;
   - compares, for every boundary of both directions at once, the two blocks' reference fields straight and with
     one side's lists swapped, and the vectors of each list in use (a saturating difference, its magnitude against
     4). This is `motion_strength`'s rule for every case, which the tests check;
   - turns the masks of bS 2, 1, 3 and 4 into bytes (`maskz_mov_epi8`, one byte shuffle for the vertical edges'
     order) and stores the 32 bytes;
   - keeps the masks of coefficients in general registers, as the reference builds them.
   It uses 256-bit vectors only. The neighbours' rows are read so that no two-source permute takes two adjacent
   32-byte reads: the left neighbour's last column as four 16-byte reads that lie apart, gathered by two-source
   permutes of 128 bits and a blend; the top neighbour's last row as one 32-byte read and one of 16 bytes. The dist
   build's disassembly has no 512-bit register (`objdump -d` lists no `zmm`), as `main`'s has none.
4. `same_motion` compares two motions as one 96-bit key (a 128-bit integer of the vectors and the reference bytes):
   one 8-byte and one 4-byte exclusive or, an or and one branch. Writing it as the two words' exclusive ors, or-ed
   and tested against 0, does not survive: the compiler turns it back into a compare and branch per word and
   vectorizes the reference bytes (6.0M more instructions on the 4k stream).
5. `SliceDecoder::store_mb` gets `#[inline(always)]`, which restores what moving `Motion` cost. Inlined, `inter_pred`
   runs 5.8M instructions below `main` on the 4k stream; the attribute alone on `main` gives 4.4M of that. In time it
   gives nothing measurable: `main` with the attribute against `main`, 1.0004 [0.9969, 1.0045] (the local run below).

Rejected:
- Every macroblock through the out-of-line kernel, and a kernel for the path with one motion: the numbers above.
- Dropping the test for all zeros: its cost is the branch, which any derivation keeps.
- 512-bit vectors: the clock cost above. Sixteen blocks a vector would halve the comparisons of a split macroblock,
  which is not where the time goes.

A microbenchmark (information; 4,096 macroblocks of random motion drawn from three list patterns, 8x8 quadrants
that share or differ, sparse coefficients, best of 300) puts the kernel against the reference at:
- 36.8 against 138.4 ns a macroblock where the macroblock carries sixteen motions;
- 34.2 against 66.2 ns where only a neighbour does;
- 39.1 against 97.1 ns on a mix.

A local timing run (information, not a bar), on this VM's 2.90 GHz class:
- method: `scripts/h264_parity.py`, every build in the same rounds, one thread pinned to core 2, five rounds, the 32
  training streams at the class frame counts;
- first, before the deblocking setup round merged: `main` at `acf3ee2f`; `main` with item 5 alone; this
  round without the AVX-512 kernel (items 1, 2, 4, 5); this round as first built (`6eac9f55`, the left column read
  by unpacks);
  - this round over `main` with item 5: discard 0.9835 [0.9775, 0.9900], 28 of 32 faster (sd 0.9738, 720p 0.9830,
    1080p 0.9903, 4k 0.9831); write 0.9828 [0.9760, 0.9927], 28 of 32;
  - without the kernel, over the same: discard 0.9940 [0.9841, 0.9981], 25 of 32;
- then, on an earlier change: `base` and `k` of the bars below (builds of the same trees), six rounds: discard 0.9834
  [0.9729, 0.9926], 28 of 32 faster (sd 0.9663, 720p 0.9928, 1080p 0.9998, 4k 0.9732); write 0.9807 [0.9748,
  0.9850], 31 of 32.

### Bars

These bars are fixed before the gating run. The one-thread arms run as the deblocking setup round's did:
- two decoders in the same rounds, built alike from one tree each (`cargo build --locked --profile dist --example
  decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset);
- on the 2.90 GHz class (family 6, model 106). The run records the class, and the script stops on any other host;
- `base` is `main` at `bb7255cd`. `k` is the branch's code commit `193051ba`: `base`'s tree plus this round's
  change to `crates/coreav-kernels-h264` (with its tests and fuzz target) and to `deblock.rs`, `picture.rs` and
  `inter.rs` of `crates/coreav-h264`;
- the run is `scripts/h264_parity.py` of the base tree on the training set, with FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference
  command, `--shuffle-seed 20261026 --null-arm base --gate-stream 41e324ebb708.0.sd.h264 --gate-every 4`;
- each call sits between two host gates; a failed gate after a call voids it, and it runs again;
- the class frame counts are sd 1800, 720p 900, 1080p 300 and 4k 150;
- per class, one call at one thread pinned to core 2, at twenty rounds;
- the script is `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/bs-kernel/run-ab-helper.sh`, and `analyze.py` beside it prints the
  bars. More than four unresolved streams in its calls make the run a host fault.

The eight-thread arms run on Compute Engine ("Where the eight-thread arms run"): the same two builds, made the same
way, through `run-gcp.sh` beside it (`scripts/h264_parity_gcp.py`: one new `c4-standard-16` VM, one call a class at
eight threads, `--min-seconds 3`, ten rounds, seed 20261026, a null arm of `base`, the in-call gate and the host
check on the same stream, the null and spread bars of that host, at most 2.5 hours and 5 USD). A void verdict
(`verdict.json`) means a new run on a new VM.

| Bar | Quantity | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| BS-1 | median per-stream ratio, `k` over `base`, one thread, discard (the primary) | at most **1.000**, and the upper end of its 95% interval below **1.000** |
| BS-2 | the same, write | at most **1.000** |
| BS-3 | the same per class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write | at most **1.005** in each |
| BS-4 | the median over the 32 streams at eight threads on `c4-standard-16`, discard and write | at most **1.002** (per class, information) |
| BS-5 | output | the 32 training streams byte-identical to `base` with `k` at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2 and 8 threads and with scalar kernels, on `k` |

BS-4's 1.002: the null median of the 32 streams on that host stays within about 0.1% either side, so a guard twice
that far is above its noise and still sees a slowdown at eight threads.

The change ships if `k` meets BS-1 to BS-5. Otherwise this section records the result, and the change stays out. One
run decides each arm: a re-run is allowed only for a recorded host fault. Reported as information, each naming its
build's commit:
- the ratio to FFmpeg 9.0.2 for both builds, overall and per class, at one thread and at eight;
- the share of streams faster than FFmpeg, likewise.

### Result

One run decided each arm (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/bs-kernel/gating/` and `gating-gcp/`, branch

## CAVLC round: one bit window across the whole macroblock layer, rejected locally

Measured on the CAVLC window round's branch (`9ba67d12`: `main` with bundle 2 and that round), `6f7799768413`
is still the slowest stream against FFmpeg at one thread. Its largest parse item outside the residual is `BitReader::ue`: 3.23% of its instructions, 7.70 M calls, out
of line and compiled for the baseline target, about 43 instructions inside a call and 7 at the call site. Nearly all
come from the CAVLC macroblock layer (mb_type, sub_mb_type, ref_idx, mvd, coded_block_pattern, mb_qp_delta,
intra_chroma_pred_mode) and mb_skip_run (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cavlc-mb-window-probe/`).

- **Probe.** 36 one-uop instructions at every `ue` call (a median 2.27% of a CAVLC stream's instructions) read
  **1.0128 [1.0057, 1.0173]** on the six CAVLC streams, 6 of 6 slower, against a CABAC null of 1.0002: the plan's rule
  (at least 1.010, lower end above 1.000) was met, at a little over half the CAVLC window probe's price per
  instruction.
- **C.** `CavlcSyntax` starts a `cavlc::Window` when it is made, before mb_type, and every element of the macroblock
  layer reads from it (`ue`/`se`/`te`/`u` inlined, long codes on a cold path); `Syntax::check`, after the residual and
  before reconstruction, finishes it into the reader, and I_PCM finishes it before its samples. Instructions: a median
  of **−1.74%** on the CAVLC streams (−0.82% to −2.14%), output identical (64 of 64), conformance met.
- **Local timing:** CAVLC 6 **0.9914 [0.9775, 0.9992]**, 5 of 6 faster; all 32 0.9985; `6f7799768413` 0.9944. The
  condition for a gating run (CAVLC 6 at most 0.990 with the upper end below 1.000, all 32 at most 1.000) is not met in
  its first part, so there was no gating run.

The change is kept on `rejected/h264-cavlc-mb-window` (`c.diff`) as a bundle candidate: a gain of about 0.9% on the
CAVLC streams at one thread, about half its instruction cut, as the probe priced it.

## Entropy round: DecodeDecision in assembly

"Entropy decoding: the instruction excess by syntax element" priced the engine's instructions at about 0.19% of a CABAC
stream's time for each instruction a regular bin, and found that safe Rust does not reach them: LLVM's selections, not
the tables, set the count. This round builds one hot-path site, `decision`: DecodeDecision (clause 9.3.3.2.1, with
RenormD of clause 9.3.3.2.2) as an `asm!` block whose instructions are fixed.

### How it differs from the rejected sites

`rejected/h264-cabac-fast` ("Result: no site merged") read 0.9995 for its `decision` with the two map loops. This site
differs in what it removes and in how it is checked before any timing:

- **Instructions are counted first.** The rejected sites were timed without a count against their twin. This one
  is timed only if callgrind shows the cut the probe priced (the rules below).
- **The engine's representation is the safe engine's.** The rejected engine kept codIOffset at a fixed bit position,
  so every block converted the engine on the way in and out (`enter`, `leave`), and its refill, bypass bins and level
  suffix went through those conversions. Here the site reads and writes the safe engine's own `value`, `bits` and
  `range`, so nothing converts, and every regular bin of the slice can use it: the MB header, mvd and ref_idx, and
  coded_block_flag as well as the residual's loops. The rejected site served the residual's maps only.
- **One table entry, read by memory operands.** The rejected engine read a row per context state, four packed 16-bit
  fields that it unpacked with six instructions (`rorx`, `and`, `shrx`, `movzx`, `shr`, `and`), and loaded the next
  state after the bin had resolved, from an index built from it. Here one 8-byte entry per (state, codIRange quarter)
  holds rangeLPS, the renormalized rangeLPS, its shift, and the next state after the less probable symbol with the bin
  beside it. A second table by state holds the next state after the more probable symbol with its bin. `cmov` reads
  the three less-probable fields straight from the entry. The next state and the bin come out of one select of two
  values loaded before the bin resolves.
- **The loops stay safe Rust.** No significance-map or level loop is written in assembly. LLVM schedules the loops
  around the block, which takes registers and gives back registers.
- **The twin is the v3 build.** The rejected sites were measured against a twin compiled for the x86-64 baseline. The
  safe engine now runs in the x86-64-v3 instance, BMI2 included, and that instance is what this site replaces. The site
  runs only in the v3 instance, whose `V3` proves BMI1 and BMI2 (`rorx`, `shlx`). The baseline instance keeps the
  safe decision.

### Design

- **The decision.** In: the context state `s` (a byte), and the engine. With `q = codIRange >> 6 & 7`, the entry is
  `4 * s + q`. A state has an entry for each of its byte values, and `q` is 4 to 7 between decisions, so the entry of
  `(s, q)` is the one after `(s + 1, q - 4)`'s: 1,028 entries, 8 KB, of which the 128 state bytes (pStateIdx 0 to
  63) use 4 KB in one run. The masked `q` bounds the index whatever `range` holds, so the read is in bounds by construction. Values match the safe twin for every state the engine can reach, codIRange 256 to 510.
  - `range - rangeLPS` is codIRange for the more probable symbol. `shlx` scales it by `bits` to compare with `value`.
  - The more probable symbol's renormalization is one doubling at most, its shift `1 - (range >> 8)`.
  - The comparison is a subtraction of the scaled range from a copy of `value`, which borrows for the more probable
    symbol. Without a borrow, four `cmov` take `value` minus the scaled range, and the less probable symbol's range,
    shift and next state with bin from the entry.
  - Out: the engine, and the next state with the bin. Safe Rust stores the state, tests the bin and refills below
    [`RESERVE`] bits, as the twin does.
  - The block reads the two tables only, writes no memory and touches no slice data (`pure`, `readonly`, `nostack`).
- **Where it runs.** `Tier` gains `decision`. The baseline's is the safe `Engine::decision`; `V3`'s is the site.
  `Cabac::decision` and the residual's loops take the slice's `T: Tier` and call it, so each instance's copy of the
  chain compiles its own decision.
- **Predicted count.** About 17 instructions in the block, plus the state's load and store, the bin's test and the
  refill test in Rust, against 40 for the safe decision in the significance-map loop (`decision-asm.txt`). That is
  about 15 fewer a regular bin. At the probe's price that is about 3% of a CABAC stream, if LLVM keeps the loops'
  registers. The chain from one bin's codIRange to the next is about as long as the twin's (the index, the entry's
  load, the subtraction, the scaled compare and a `cmov`); the cut is off the chain.
- **As built.** The block is 17 instructions. `range` and `bits` go in as 32-bit operands, so LLVM does not
  zero-extend them each bin: the block's 32-bit subtraction clears the bits above `range`'s, and `shlx` reads only
  the low six bits of `bits`. In the significance-map loop of `v3::residual::<16>` a decision is 24 instructions,
  from the context index to the refill test, against the twin's 40.

`base` is the commit the branch is based on; `k` is the branch's code commit.

  than `base` on each of the 26 CABAC streams. If it does not, nothing is timed, and this section records the count.
- **The local timing.** `ab3.py`, eight rounds, one thread pinned, discard, the 32 streams at the class frame counts,

## Threading round: a new picture's first touch on the thread that decodes it

### What the measurement says

At eight threads the picture pool cannot serve the pictures decoded while the pipeline fills: 2 to 10 a stream at
the class frame counts, 1 to 4 at one thread (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/first-touch/plan-probe.md`). Each was
made new, and `Canvas::new` sized its bands on the caller's thread before the picture was dispatched
(`BandData::fit`): the chroma planes filled with 128, the motion with `NO_MOTION` and the heads with `NO_HEAD`, every
page touched for the first time there, one picture after another. The luma came zeroed from the allocator and its
pages faulted on the worker that first wrote them. A probe that touched a new band a second time, on the same
thread, cost 1.0382 [1.0295, 1.0779] at eight threads on `c4-standard-16` and 1.4162 at 4k
(`first-touch/README.md`), above PF-1's 1.015, so this round was built. Per luma sample a new band's caller-side
touch is 1.31 bytes (chroma 0.5, motion 0.75, heads 0.06) against the luma's 1, so `main` already did a little over
half of what the probe doubled on that thread, all of it ahead of the picture's dispatch.

### Design

Two changes, one cause:

- **A band is sized when the canvas is first asked for it.** `Canvas::new` only makes room for the bands.
  `Canvas::fit_through(k)` sizes every band up to `k` not sized yet, in order, and `Canvas.fitted` counts them. It
  runs in each method that hands out, copies into or from, or publishes a band: `band_mut`, `take_band`, `copy_top`
  (so `enter` and `refresh_top`), `publish_ready`, `fill_black` and `conceal_from` (all bands). A band and every band
  above it are therefore sized before any of them is written, copied from or published, whichever path reaches it
  first: a slice starting in a later band, a band no slice covers (sized when the deblocking reaches it), or a
  canvas dropped part way (its `Drop` publishes, which sizes). The first touch of a new picture's planes now happens
  on the thread that decodes the picture, a band at a time just before the band is decoded, so it overlaps the
  decoding of the pictures in flight instead of holding back the next picture's dispatch. A reused picture's bands
  are already their size, so for them `fit` changes nothing, and the cost is one comparison per call.
- **A new chroma plane is zeroed memory from the allocator, like the luma**, instead of a plane written with 128.
  Its pages are then touched once, by the decoding that writes them, not first by a fill. Nothing reads a sample a
  new plane starts with: "Reusing a picture without clearing it" already requires every read sample to be written
  for the picture, since a pooled picture holds whatever its last picture left, and a macroblock no slice covers
  gets its grey from `clear_macroblock`, a gap picture from `fill_black` or `conceal_from`. The slack rows of a
  picture of one band are read only by windows whose used samples are inside the picture. `Picture::black` fills its
  chroma with 128 itself, so it is still the grey picture its name says.

The motion and the heads are still written by `fit`: a `Vec` of a struct cannot come zeroed from the allocator in
safe Rust. Output is unchanged by construction, and checked (FT-6).

Rejected:
- **Sizing every band at the start of the picture on the worker** (`PictureWork`'s first slice). It moves the touch
  off the caller too, but writes 12 MB at 4k before the first band is decoded, out of the core's caches by the time
  the band is written, and delays the first band's publication by the whole picture's fill instead of one band's.
- **Fewer pictures in flight while the pipeline fills.** It touches fewer new pages but gives up the parallelism the
  warm-up is for.
- **Making new pictures ahead of need** (a pool warmed on another thread). It needs a thread or a hand-off of its
  own, and it still touches every page; it pays only where the caller is idle, which the probe does not show.
- **Huge pages for the planes.** The allocator call needs `unsafe`, which the decoder crate forbids, and the gain
  depends on the host's transparent huge page setting.

### Bars (fixed before the timing run)

`base` is `main` at `538265c4` (the decoder's code of `main` at `13e4dfc4`); `ft` is this branch's code commit `68c8f059`.
Three arms, `base`, `ft` and a null arm (a second copy of `base`), built alike (`cargo build --locked --profile dist
--example decode -p coreav-h264`, one toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` unset), FFmpeg 9.0.2 as the reference command, seeded
order, calls of at least 3 s. Each bar is a median of per-stream ratios, `ft` over `base`, with its 95% bootstrap
interval. Eight threads run `scripts/h264_parity_gcp.py` on `c4-standard-16` (one thread a core) at its bars and
void rules, ten rounds, with a cap of 10 USD for the round. One thread runs `scripts/h264_parity.py` on the helper VM
class (Intel Xeon @ 2.90 GHz, family 6, model 106), pinned, with the host-health gate before and after each call.

| | measure | host | bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| FT-1 | eight threads, discard, all 32 (the primary) | `c4-standard-16` | at most **0.995**, upper end below **1.000** |
| FT-2 | eight threads, discard, the 4k class | `c4-standard-16` | at most **0.985** |
| FT-3 | eight threads, write, all 32 | `c4-standard-16` | at most **1.000** |
| FT-4 | eight threads, each class (sd, 720p, 1080p, 4k), discard and write | `c4-standard-16` | at most **1.005** |
| FT-5 | one thread pinned, discard and write, all 32 and each class | helper VM | all 32 at most **1.005**, each class at most **1.010** |
| FT-6 | output | | `ft` byte-identical to `base` on the 32 training streams at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 in fast and safe modes, AVX2 and scalar kernels, at 1, 2 and 8 threads |
| FT-7 | eight threads, discard, the 64 streams of the held-out draw (`docs/measurements/h264-n2-heldout/list.json`), five rounds | `c4-standard-16` | at most **1.000** |

Sizing. The gain is expected at eight threads, so the gain bars are there: FT-1 asks for 0.5% where the probe's
doubling cost 3.8% and `main` did about 57% of the doubled bytes on the caller's thread; FT-2 asks for 1.5% in the
class where the probe cost 41%. Eight threads' noise on `c4-standard-16` is about 0.1% over the 32 (the probe's null
arm −0.05%) and up to about 0.6% in one class (the inter round's 4k reading of 1.0062 for a change without an
eight-thread effect), below both margins. At one thread a picture is one band and only one to four pictures a
stream are new, so no gain is expected there: FT-5 is a guard against a loss, sized to the helper VM's one-thread
noise of about 0.6 to 0.7% per stream. FT-7 holds the claim to streams the round never saw and shares FT-1's cap.

The change ships if `ft` meets FT-1 to FT-7. One valid run decides; a re-run of the same arms is allowed only for a
host fault as the hosts' void rules define it. The ratio to FFmpeg 9.0.2 at one and eight threads is reported as
information.

A gating run is requested only if a local interleaved timing on the helper VM class shows the eight-thread gain:
`base`, `ft` and the null arm, eight threads unpinned, wall time, five rounds over the 32 streams at the class frame
counts, discard (`ab8.py`), median at most 0.995 with the upper end of its interval below 1.000; and one thread
pinned, CPU time, six rounds, discard (`ab1t.py`), median at most 1.005. If the eight-thread interval spans 1.000,
the change is a small gain: it is not gated alone, and it waits on a `rejected/` branch for a bundle round.

## Entropy round: the CABAC motion vector differences

### What the measurement says

After earlier changes the largest entropy group left over FFmpeg on the CABAC streams is mvd and ref_idx: 267
instructions a macroblock against 126, a median excess of 2.49% of a CABAC stream's instructions ("Entropy decoding
after the residual dispatch and the asm decision"). Three sites hold most of it (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/
mvd-probe/`, `sites.txt`), measured per call on the code of an earlier change:

- the mvd call, one per component, with DecodeDecision and the bypass bins inlined: 73 to 389 instructions;
- `store_mvd`, one per partition and list: 116 to 159;
- `fill_mvd_cache`, one per inter macroblock that is not skipped or B_Direct_16x16: 68 to 103.

A probe added independent one-uop instructions at the three sites, as many as the cut below was predicted to remove
(60 a component call, 115 a store, 55 a fill: a median of 2.09% of a CABAC stream's instructions, above an earlier change's 1.5%).
It read **1.0108 [1.0066, 1.0154]** on the 26 CABAC streams, against a CAVLC null control of 0.9988. That met its rule
(at least 1.010, lower end above 1.000) at the edge. The price, about 1.1% of time for 2.09% of the instructions, is
the half that an earlier change found for plain-instruction cuts.

### Design

- **The caches packed a list.** `NbCache::mvd` holds one `u16` per block and list: the horizontal component's capped
  absolute value in the low byte and the vertical one in the high byte. `store_mvd` writes a partition's row of both
  components with one store of 2, 4 or 8 bytes. The cache is 40 entries long and indexes are masked to 31, so that
  a row from any block is inside the array and no bounds check is left. A macroblock keeps list `l`'s bottom row in
  `NbInfo::entropy[2l]` and its right column in `entropy[2l + 1]`, four packed blocks each. That is the same 32 bytes
  the four per-component edges took, so `NbInfo` does not grow.
- **Only the slice's lists.** A P slice fills and keeps list 0 alone. List 1's edges stay 0, and no macroblock of
  another slice reads them (a neighbour is available only in its own slice, clause 6.4.9).
- **Both components in one call.** `Syntax::mvd` returns both components. The CABAC instance reads the neighbours'
  pair once and enters the slice's instance of the hot paths once a vector instead of once a component.
- **The prefix as its own loop.** TU with cMax 9: bin 0 at the neighbours' ctxIdxInc, bin `b` from 1 to 8 at
  `base + min(b + 2, 6)` (clause 9.3.3.1.1.7). There is no closure, no compare against an optional cMax and no
  overflow check: the prefix is at most 9 bins. The suffix's addition saturates, and the existing range checks reject
  what overflows.
- **Unchanged:** DecodeDecision, the bypass bins, the Exp-Golomb suffix and ref_idx. ref_idx's context reads two
  neighbours through `neighbour_4x4`, which is MB-layer work.

Rejected:
- **Two `u8` caches a list, as before, with masked indexes.** This halves neither the stores nor the fills.
- **No cache at all, reading the neighbours' stored motion.** The context needs the absolute differences, which no
  later stage keeps, so they would have to be stored per block in the ring.
- **A table for the prefix's contexts.** `min(b + 2, 6)` is two instructions with no load.

Results:
- **Instructions:** −0.02% to −3.32%, a median of **−1.92%** on the 26 CABAC streams (0.85 of the prediction), and
  −0.02% to +0.04% on the CAVLC streams. `parse_mvd` is `#[inline(always)]`. Without that, its CAVLC instance went out
  of line at +0.19%.
- **Checks:** output identical to `base` on the 32 streams at 1 and 8 threads (64 of 64); conformance 291 of 291 at
  1, 2 and 8 threads, 97 of 97 with scalar kernels and 97 of 97 without `fast`.
- **Local timing** (`ab3.py`, eight rounds, one thread pinned, the 32 streams): CABAC 26 **0.9869 [0.9831, 0.9921]**,
  24 of 26 faster; all 32 **0.9876 [0.9848, 0.9959]**, 28 of 32 faster; sd 0.9965, 720p 0.9834, 1080p 0.9847, 4k
  0.9970. The plan's condition for a gating run (CABAC 26 at most 0.990 with the upper end below 1.000, all 32 at most
  1.000) is met.

### Bars (fixed before the gating run)

`base` is the commit the branch is based on at the run: change A's code. If change B or change A does not merge, the branch is
first rebased onto `main` and `base` is that `main`. `k` is the branch's code commit.

## Threading round: a banded picture's lines asked for ahead

### Why

At eight threads inter prediction is CoreAV's first stage by excess over FFmpeg in every class. The miss probe
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/miss-8t/`) placed the eight threads on one core and on eight: from one to eight cores
CoreAV's inter cycles a macroblock grow by 113, 47 more than FFmpeg's, at sd by 133 more and at 720p by 58. Of the 47,
load stalls are 40 and store-buffer stalls 22 (they overlap); the misses do not grow in number from one core to eight,
the same accesses wait longer for lines another core holds. An earlier change (a new picture's bands first touched by the worker
that decodes them) changes this by under 2 cycles a macroblock.

Two facts of the code meet that cost:

- **The size rule turns the hints off where the excess is.** Round 12's `ahead` asks for a picture's lines, and for
  its reference's, only where the picture holds more than 1 MiB of samples, because a smaller picture "stays in [the
  core's second-level] cache from one macroblock row to the next, with the part of its reference a row reads". That
  holds with one thread. With more, a picture is decoded beside others: its references were written by other cores,
  and its buffer was last written for an older picture and read since by other cores. Every sd picture of the
  training set, and three of the eight 720p ones, are below 1 MiB, so at eight threads they ask for nothing.
- **A read hint does not take a line from another core.** `request_destination` asks for the picture's lines with
  `prefetcht0`, which brings a line other cores hold as shared; the store that follows still has to take it from
  them. At sd CoreAV's store-buffer stalls are 95.9 cycles a macroblock against FFmpeg's 25.9.

A third was a candidate: the reference's request asks for the block's rows (`Planes::request`), not the window's two
rows above and three below, which interpolated blocks read too and which at eight threads come from another core.

### Design

1. **A banded picture asks, whatever its size.** `SliceDecoder::ahead` (a flag) becomes `hints`, one byte holding
   `HINT_AHEAD` (the macroblocks' own lines and the reference's, as before) and `HINT_OWN`; the same size, so no field of the decoder moves (the lesson of "the aprons' rows owned ahead"). `mb::hints` sets it from the
   picture's size and band count: in one band (every picture at one thread, and at any count a picture no other reads,
   which `decoder.rs` cuts into one), `ahead`'s rule, unchanged; in more, every hint. A
   macroblock's start tests the byte once where nothing is asked for, compares it with `HINT_AHEAD` where only the
   one-band hints are, and goes to `request_banded`, out of line, otherwise, so that the one-thread decode keeps its
   code.
2. **The picture's lines owned** (`HINT_OWN`): `request_banded` issues `request_destination`'s hints through
   `prefetch::Ownership` (`prefetchw`, on a CPU that has it, found once by CPUID; a CPU without it keeps the read
   hints). The kernel crate's `Ownership` and `simd::hint_own` are those of `rejected/h264-apron-keep`; their
   `unsafe` (one `prefetchw` in `asm!`, two `__cpuid`) has its rows, with their preconditions, in `docs/unsafe-sites.md` on the change's branch.

Hints change no value: the output is the same by construction.

Not done here: a non-reference picture is one band at any thread count, so it keeps the size rule and is not owned;
it is decoded beside others too, and hinting it is a later candidate with its own measurement.

Rejected:
- **The reference's window rows** (`h + 5` rows from `y - 2` in a banded picture; the probe's `W`): the load stalls
  fell by 5.5 cycles a macroblock and the instructions rose by 17.6, and inter's cycles did not move (−0.4 against a
  bar of 10). As one thread, its second call site of `Planes::request` also cost `predict_fast` instructions on every
  block, hinted or not (+0.5% of the decode's at sd at one thread, where nothing is asked for; out of line +0.14%).
- **A lower size threshold for every thread count** (say 256 KiB): one thread measured the sd and small 720p
  pictures' hints as a cost (1.028 and 1.010, "Motion round: the reference's lines requested ahead, cheaply"), and the
  reason they cost there, a picture and its reference in this core's cache, is what more threads take away; the band
  count says which case a picture is in, a size does not.
- **Keeping a picture's workers on cores** (affinity): pictures are decoded in parallel and each reads several
  others, so no placement keeps a reference on its reader's core; it would also need thread pinning, which the
  library does not do.
- **Owned hints at one thread too:** at one thread the picture's buffer was written and read by this core, a read
  hint brings it in a state the store can use, and the guard would test a change that has no reason to help.
- **A second macroblock loop for banded pictures**, monomorphized on the hints: the whole loop compiled twice for
  three hints ("the aprons' rows owned ahead, the decoder's layout kept").

### Part-only probe

Before any timing, `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/hints-8t/` (plan and criteria committed before its run) measured on
the miss probe's host which parts remove the stalls they aim at: `E` (point 1 with read hints only), `EW` (with the
window's rows), `EO` (with point 2) and `EWO` (the three). Per macroblock at eight threads, over the 32:

- `E`: at sd inter's cycles fall by 46 (bar 20) and its load stalls by 66; over the 32 the hints' own walk takes what
  inter saves, and every stage's cycles stay where they were (+0.8).
- `W` (`EW` − `E`): inter −0.4 (bar 10): left out (Rejected, above).
- `O` (`EO` − `E`): every stage's cycles −39.7 (bar 10), the store-buffer stalls in inter −9.6; inter, the entropy
  and the macroblock stages, which all write the picture, fall by 8 to 16 each.

So the change is `E` with `O`: `E` alone is no gain over the 32 (its walk costs what inter saves), but it is what
gives sd and the small 720p pictures any hint to own, and `O` is measured on top of it. An arm of `O` alone on `main`'s
size rule was not built: it would leave those pictures, the excess's classes, as they are. In the probe's `perf stat`
(two rounds, information) the change's median wall time is 0.994 of `main`'s (20 of 32 faster); HB-1 below was set
with that figure known, before any timing of its own. At one thread a picture is one band and the change issues `main`'s hints; the decode's
instructions at one thread are +0.04% (sd) and +0.02% (1080p) of `main`'s (callgrind, 60 pictures).

### Bars (fixed before the timing run)

`base` is `main` when the run is made, and `k` this change rebased on it; the commits are recorded in the result.

## CAVLC round: the slice loop, runs of skipped macroblocks and one bit window a slice

### What the measurement says

After the CAVLC window round, the PMU profile of `6f7799768413` (`profile-6f-af20b62e`) puts its gap to FFmpeg in
entropy and the macroblock layer (+0.115 of FFmpeg's cycles). Outside the residual, the macroblock layer takes about
975 instructions a macroblock, against about 640 for FFmpeg (function-level counts only).

A callgrind count of `6f7799768413` with line tables (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cavlc-slice-loop-probe/`,
`plan.txt`) splits that cost:
- 58.5% of its macroblocks are P_Skip, in runs of 9.3 on average. Before motion compensation, a skipped macroblock
  costs about 280 instructions:
  - `start_mb`, out of line, about 102, of which 47 derive the four neighbours;
  - the skip loop and `decode_skip`, about 40;
  - the P_Skip prediction's entry, its neighbours' motion and the zero test, about 64;
  - `store_mb` and `finish_mb`, about 70.
- A coded macroblock spends about 237 on its Exp-Golomb reads: 3.55 out-of-line `BitReader::ue` calls a macroblock.

Two probes priced these parts:
- **The macroblock layer window probe** priced the Exp-Golomb part: 36 pads a `ue` call, 2.27% of the instructions,
  read CAVLC 6 1.0128 [1.0057, 1.0173].
- **This round's probe** priced the skipped macroblocks: 200 one-uop pads a skipped macroblock, a median of 2.84% of a
  CAVLC stream's instructions. It read CAVLC 6 **1.0357 [1.0252, 1.1091]**, 6 of 6 slower, against a CABAC null
  control of 0.9984. That met its rule (at least 1.010, lower end above 1.000). The price is above one to one: the
  skipped macroblocks' path has little latency to hide work behind.

### Design

The CAVLC slice data loop (`decode_cavlc_body` in `mb.rs`) is restructured in two parts. CABAC's machine code does not
change: a normalized disassembly diff of every function shows only the per-slice dispatch differs.

- **(S) Runs of skipped macroblocks.**
  - A run of `mb_skip_run` macroblocks is decoded in one loop (`decode_skip_run`).
  - Clause 8.4.1.1 gives a P_Skip macroblock a zero vector when A is not available, or when A has refIdx 0 and a
    zero vector. Inside a run, A is the previous skipped macroblock (refIdx 0). So after the first zero vector of a
    run, every later macroblock of the run in the same row has a zero vector, and a row start has no A.
  - Those macroblocks take `decode_still_skip`: no neighbour loads, and the still head is rebuilt from the reference
    slot. The shortcut starts only where the head the full path wrote for the macroblock before is byte-equal to that
    still head, and debug asserts check the macroblock state the shortcut leaves as it was.
  - The first skipped macroblock of a run, and any after a non-zero vector, take the full derivation.
  - Coded macroblocks start through an inlined `start_mb_body`. Their neighbours' availability comes from the slice's
    first address: a slice is one run of macroblocks in raster order, because slice groups and arbitrary slice order
    are rejected. A debug assert compares this with the load-based derivation.
  - The checks on `mb_skip_run` are unchanged: its value and the end of the data before any macroblock of the run is
    decoded, and a run past the picture at each macroblock, as before.
- **(W) One bit window a slice.**
  - `cavlc::Window` is `Copy`, with `left` a `u64` so the struct has no padding. With a `u32` the compiler packed the
    fields into shifted words, which cost about 180 instructions a macroblock in the residual.
  - `CavlcSyntax` owns the window by value. It is a local of the slice loop, created once a slice.
  - `Syntax::residual` moves the window into the residual's out-of-line closure and back, so its state stays in
    registers. CABAC's version reads the residual in place, and the `begin_residual`/`end_residual` hooks go.
  - `ue`, `se`, `te`, `u` and `flag` are inlined on the window, and `se` uses `u32` arithmetic. Codes with 16 or more
    leading zeros go to a cold path through `BitReader`, so their errors are exactly the old ones.
  - The position is checked against the end of the RBSP once after each `mb_skip_run` and once a macroblock. Past
    the end the window reads zeros, which start no short Exp-Golomb code, so a read that runs past the end fails on
    the cold path or at the next check. A macroblock's reads are bounded, so the position stays far from wrapping.
  - `more_rbsp_data` is a compare against the position of the stop bit, found once a slice (`bits::stop_bit`).
- **Errors.** Each element still returns a `Result`; after inlining, the hot path has no error branch beyond the
  existing cold-path test. A truncated CAVLC element is still `Truncated`, but its message is now `"a syntax
  element"` where some reads said `"an Exp-Golomb code"`. An mb_skip_run above its range whose code also runs past
  the end is now `Truncated` too, where it was `Invalid`.

Rejected:
- **A window a macroblock, held in `CavlcSyntax` in memory** (the macroblock layer window). It cut 83
  instructions a macroblock on `6f7799768413` of the about 190 predicted, and its local timing missed. The window
  crossed the residual's out-of-line call in memory.
- **A sticky error flag checked once a macroblock** in place of a `Result` per element. Once the reads are inlined,
  the `Result` adds no branch to the hot path beyond the cold-path test each read already has. The flag would save
  nothing, and errors would be found a macroblock later than the element that failed.
- **Deferred to later rounds:**
  - neighbour edge lines for the context fills, whose split branch mispredicts;
  - a fused CAVLC P macroblock path;
  - a CABAC skip shortcut.
  Each needs its own measurement; this round keeps CABAC unchanged.

The slice loop's function grew (its x86-64-v3 instance from about 18.7 KB to about 25.4 KB of code). The timing below
includes any instruction-cache cost of that.

Results:
- **Instructions** (`c-identity.txt`): −2.08% to −9.65%, a median of **−4.34%** on the six CAVLC streams.
  - On `6f7799768413`, −4.76%, which is −226 a macroblock. The plan predicted about −330.
  - W gives about −150 a macroblock: the Exp-Golomb work drops from about 222 to about 85.
  - S gives about −180 a skipped macroblock. A zero-vector skip in a run costs about 65 outside motion compensation,
    against about 280 before.
  - The CABAC streams change by less than 0.01%.
- **Checks** (`c-identity.txt`, `c-nofast-identity.txt`, `c-conformance.txt`):
  - output identical to `base` on the 32 streams at 1 and 8 threads (64 of 64), and without `fast` on the six CAVLC
    streams (12 of 12);
  - conformance 291 of 291 at 1, 2 and 8 threads, 97 of 97 with scalar kernels and 97 of 97 without `fast`;
  - a debug build, so that the new asserts run (the neighbours from the slice's first address against the
    load-based derivation, and the state the shortcut keeps): 194 of 194 at 1 and 8 threads.
  - A differential fuzz: 410 corrupted streams cut from three CAVLC streams, decoded by `base` and
    by a debug build of `k` with overflow checks; every one fails, with the same output, exit code and last error in
    410 of 410.
  - New tests: the window's codes read as the `BitReader` reads them, 100,000 cases including long codes, codes cut
    by the end, the errors and the position. `more_rbsp_data` is a compare against the stop bit.
- **Local timing** (`ab3.py`, eight rounds, one thread pinned, the 32 streams; `c-ab-summary.txt`):
  - CAVLC 6 **0.9813 [0.9504, 0.9854]**, 6 of 6 faster, and `6f7799768413` 0.9857;
  - all 32 0.9962 [0.9923, 1.0031], 19 of 32 faster;
  - the 26 CABAC streams, whose code does not change, 0.9993;
  - sd 0.9882, 720p 0.9959, 1080p 1.0023, 4k 1.0027.

  The plan's condition for a gating run (CAVLC 6 at most 0.985 with the upper end below 1.000, all 32 at most 1.000)

## CAVLC round: the slice loop in a function of its own

The slice loop round met its gain bar on the CAVLC streams and was rejected by its no-regression bars ("CAVLC
round: the slice loop, runs of skipped macroblocks and one bit window a slice"). Its 26 CABAC training streams, whose
functions were identical in machine code, read 1.0010 (discard) and 1.0024 (write). That moved the all-32 write, 4k
and held-out medians over their bars. The CAVLC slice loop was inlined into the per-slice dispatch,
`decode_slice_data`, so growing it changed that shared function and the placement of the code after it. This round
takes the same design with the CAVLC slice loop out of line. The plan, the build's requirements and the bars were
committed before the build (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/cavlc-slice-fn/plan.txt`, with an addendum before any
timing).

### Design

- **The design of the rejected round.** Runs of skipped macroblocks take the zero-vector shortcut, and one
  `cavlc::Window` serves a whole slice. It is rebuilt on `main`, which since gained the asm decision site and the
  packed mvd caches.
- **`decode_cavlc` is `#[inline(never)]`,** as `decode_cabac` already was. The dispatch now calls the CAVLC slice loop
  in each instance (`Base`, `V3`) instead of holding the baseline instance inlined.
- **The CAVLC residual's out-of-line instance is a decoder method, `residual_cavlc`.** It returns the window through
  an out-parameter. I_PCM's samples are copied as whole bytes after the alignment bits, with the bit reader's exact
  errors, and a test checks that.
- **CAVLC mvd reads both components from the window.** An earlier change made `parse_mvd` inline, so its call sites are `main`'s
  and the rejected round's CAVLC copy of `parse_mvd` is gone.
- **`fast::decision::Tables` is `#[repr(C, align(64))]`.** Its entries are 8 bytes at alignment 2. In `base` they
  happen to sit 8-aligned. On the first build of this round they moved to 4 modulo 8, so one entry in eight straddled
  a cache line in the DecodeDecision site. Aligned, no entry straddles a line in any layout. This is the one change
  outside the CAVLC code: a placement attribute on read-only data. The site's code and results do not change, and
  SF-4 judges it with the rest.
- **Errors.** As in the rejected round, a truncated CAVLC slice is still `Truncated`, but some messages now say "a
  syntax element" where they said "an Exp-Golomb code" or "a fixed-length code". The neighbours from the slice's
  first address rely on arbitrary slice order being rejected, and a comment at that check says so.

What the build shows (`r1-code.txt` to `conformance.txt` in that directory). `base` is main `3f918b38`; `k` is
`983e8bc3`.
- **Code (R1).** 794 of 799 functions are identical in normalized disassembly: every CABAC function, the decision
  site, motion compensation, deblocking and the kernels. The ones that differ are the CAVLC-only functions and the
  dispatch, whose callees differ only in the call to the CAVLC slice loop.
- **Placement (R2): not kept.**
  - 9 of 65 hot functions keep `base`'s start modulo 64; the others move by 16, 32 or 48 bytes.
  - `.text` starts after the read-only data and the unwind tables, whose sizes change with the code. The generic
    instances are ordered by symbol name, with `base`'s CAVLC functions between the CABAC ones.
  - On the round's first base (`82a23b66`, the addendum in `plan.txt`), the CAVLC-only variants tried kept at most
    58 of 65, and that one cost a third of the CAVLC instruction cut.
  - The aligned table's padding moves more of the code: without it, 45 of 65 keep their placement. So the CABAC
    streams' time, SF-4, is the test of the placement, not the addresses.
- **Instructions (R3).** On the 26 CABAC streams, within 0.0002% of `base` (at most 1,544 instructions a stream). On
  the six CAVLC streams, −1.92% to −7.99%, a median of **−4.03%**.
- **Output (R4).** Identical to `base` on the 32 streams at 1 and 8 threads (64 of 64), and without `fast` on the six
  CAVLC streams (12 of 12). Conformance:
  - 291 of 291 with detected kernels at 1, 2 and 8 threads;
  - 97 of 97 with scalar kernels;
  - 97 of 97 without `fast`;
  - 194 of 194 in a debug build at 1 and 8 threads.

Rejected:
- **Keeping the CABAC placement by shaping the CAVLC code.** The variant that came closest lost a third of the CAVLC
  instruction cut, and any later change reshuffles the order again.
- **Leaving the decision table as it falls.** Its placement in `base` is an accident, and one entry in eight
  straddling a line costs in the hottest CABAC function.

## Kernel round: chroma deblocking on bytes

### What the measurement says

- An earlier change (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/kernel-gaps/`) put the chroma deblocking kernel (`filter_chroma_mb`, the AVX2
  kernel of "Kernel round: a macroblock's chroma edges in one call", which the AVX-512 tier also runs) at 1.58 times
  the cycles of FFmpeg's assembly over the 32 training streams (sd 1.94, 720p 1.51, 1080p 1.72, 4k 0.98) on an earlier change's PMU
  host, for 122 instructions a macroblock against 120: a gap in cycles per instruction, not in work. Its part-only
  bound, the median share of CoreAV's cycles, is 3.16% (sd), 4.13% (720p), 1.62% (1080p) and 0.50% (4k), above
  an earlier change's 1.5% in three classes.
- Where the cycles go (`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/chroma-bytes/README.md`): an earlier change's cycle and instruction samples
  at each of the kernel's addresses give about the same cycles per instruction, 0.43, across its parts (the vertical
  pass 0.31 to 0.45, the horizontal pass 0.47 to 0.48): no single stall. The horizontal pass's reads of rows 0 to 5
  overlap the vertical pass's writes of the same rows only in part, so they cannot take the stored bytes from the
  store buffer; a timing-only build whose reads match the writes ran in the same time (1.0025 and 1.0014 on two sd
  streams). Branch misses in the kernel are under 2% of the deblocking stage's in an earlier change's records. What is left is the
  vector ports: `llvm-mca` of the kernel, with the Sapphire Rapids and Ice Lake models, finds port 5 the binding
  resource (185 of 187 cycles a run through the whole function on the first), and on the 2.90 GHz class, measured,
  in-lane shuffles issue two a cycle (ports 1 and 5), cross-lane inserts, extracts and packs one, and `vpblendvb`
  about one in 1.2 cycles. The kernel on 16-bit lanes spends about 74 port-5-only operations a fully filtered
  macroblock (inserts, zero extensions, word broadcasts, moves from general registers, extracts) and 80 in-lane
  shuffles, besides two runs of the filter over sixteen lanes a pass: 483 instructions.

### Design

1. **Samples as bytes, 32 lines a vector.** Each of p1, p0, q0 and q1 of a pass is one vector of 32 bytes: Cb's lines
   in the low 128-bit half and Cr's in the high half, and in each half the first edge's eight lines (bytes 0 to 7)
   then the second's. One run of the filter covers both edges of both planes, where the 16-bit kernel ran it twice
   over sixteen lanes; nothing widens or packs. A pass runs where any line of it has a bS.
2. **The filter on bytes** (`filter`), from clause 8.7.2.3 with chromaStyleFiltering and Equations 8-484 and 8-488:
   - the threshold tests by saturating differences: a line is filtered where α − |p0 − q0|,
     β − max(|p1 − p0|, |q1 − q0|) and bS, each saturating at 0, are all above 0; α' or β' of 0 filters nothing;
   - the weak filter's t = (4(q0 − p0) + (p1 − q1) + 4) >> 3 is (d + g) >> 1 with d = q0 − p0 and
     g = (((p1 − q1) >> 1) + 2) >> 1, each shift a floor (nested floors of halves are the floor of the quarter).
     g + 64 is two rounding averages (`pavgb`), of p1 and 255 − q1, then of that and 1; d is a signed saturating byte
     difference and d + g a signed saturating sum. Where either saturates, both the true t and the sum's half are 32
     or more in magnitude with the same sign, so both clip to the same bound while tC = t'C0 + 1 is at most 32. The
     half, offset by 192, is the rounding average of the sum offset by 128 and 255; its parts above and below 192,
     each clipped to tC (0 on lines not filtered), are added to one sample and subtracted from the other with
     unsigned saturation, which is Clip1;
   - the strong filter's (2p1 + p0 + q1 + 2) >> 2 is the rounding average of p1 and ⌊(p0 + q1) / 2⌋, the floor being
     the rounding average less the low bit of p0 ⊕ q1; likewise for q0. Lines with bS of 4 or more take it.

   t'C0 above 31 is outside Table 8-17 (its chroma entries are at most 25), but the trait takes any byte: where any
   t'C0 a segment selects is above 31, the macroblock goes to the paired kernel edge by edge (`chroma_mb_by_edges`).
   Tests check the filter against the clause's arithmetic on every p0 and q0 against extremes and a grid of p1 and
   q1 at t'C0 0, 25 and 31, on 3.2 million random lines, and the whole kernel against the reference on parameters of
   any bytes; the fuzz target takes such parameters too.
3. **Rows by sixteen-byte reads.** A row of both planes is one 16-byte read into each half (`vinserti128` from
   memory, which takes no port-5 operation, where joining two 8-byte reads did): the vertical pass reads rows 2 to 9
   of the window from column −8, so that the block's columns −2 to 5 are bytes 8 to 15 (the bytes before a row's
   first are the end of the row above, inside the window), and the horizontal pass reads rows 0 to 7 from column 2
   (past the window's ten columns, but before its last row ends). Both lie inside the extent of the one check per
   plane (ten rows of ten bytes) for any stride of at least ten. The vertical pass transposes with byte, word,
   doubleword and quadword interleaves within each half (12 shuffles), filters, and transposes back (12); the
   horizontal pass joins rows k and k + 4 by one quadword interleave. Writes are as before: eight bytes of rows 2 to 9
   from column 0, and rows 1, 2, 5 and 6 from column 2.
4. **Parameters from the records' bytes.** `EdgeParams` is `repr(C)` (fourteen bytes, no padding; a compile-time
   assertion), so a pass's four records are 56 contiguous bytes of the call's table. Each edge's two records are read
   as one vector (Cb's to the low half, Cr's to the high), and α, β, bS and t'C0 go to their lines by byte shuffles
   and blends: about 20 vector operations a pass and no scalar ones, where packing α and β in general registers took
   about 18 scalar operations and moves to vector registers on port 5. Whether a pass runs, and whether every
   selected t'C0 is in range, are one test each on those lanes.
5. **No early exit, no branch around the strong filter.** Counted on four training streams, a pass in which no line
   passes the thresholds is under 2% of passes, and passes with a bS of 4 on some line are 36% to 92%.

A fully filtered macroblock takes 302 instructions (483 before), and 36.4 ns against 51.5 in a microbenchmark on the
2.90 GHz class (`chroma-bytes/README.md`); on `41e324ebb708` the kernel runs 19.1 million instructions in 300 pictures
against 23.5 million.

Rejected:
- Reading the horizontal pass's rows where the vertical pass wrote them, to take them from the store buffer: no
  change in time (above).
- `xor`/`and` selects in place of `vpblendvb`: LLVM forms the blend again from them.
- Writing the high quadword of each half with `movhpd`: LLVM lowers it to a shuffle and a `movq` whatever the domain
  of the value; the 8 shuffles stay.
- AVX-512 on 256-bit registers for the lanes (`vpermt2b` in place of two shuffles and a blend): one port-5 operation
  for three on ports 1 and 5, and an AVX-512 path beside the AVX2 one for a few operations a pass; not built. The
  earlier rejection of compares into mask registers ("Kernel round: deblocking edges read into registers") stands.

### Local timing and what follows

Local interleaved timing on the 2.90 GHz class (`scripts/h264_parity.py`, `main` at `d95bb8b1` against the branch's
code commit, one thread pinned, six rounds, the class frame counts; `chroma-bytes/README.md`): discard 0.9996 [0.9853,
1.0052] over the 32 streams, 17 faster (sd 1.0025, 720p 0.9888, 1080p 1.0005, 4k 0.9991), write 0.9984 [0.9862,
1.0032]. The kernel is about a third cheaper, but it is 2% to 4% of the time where it matters, so the gain is under
1% and this host's interval spans 1.000. As such a change, it is not gated alone: the code waits on
`rejected/h264-chroma-deblock-bytes` for a bundle round, which fixes its own bars before its run.
Bundle 3 carried it with the inter placement and the straight prefetch hints, and was rejected by its
bar on the 1080p and 4k streams ("Bundle 3: one thread's inter prediction at 1080p and 4k").

## Bundle 3: one thread's inter prediction at 1080p and 4k

**Result: rejected, by B3-2** (the 16 streams at 1080p and 4k gained 0.9887 against a bar of 0.985; "Result" below).
None of it is in `main`; the code is on `rejected/h264-bundle3`.

### Why

The PMU profile at `ae609547` puts the largest one-thread excess over FFmpeg 9.0.2 at 1080p and 4k in inter
prediction (+0.031 and +0.059 of FFmpeg's cycles), and names the placement (`predict.rs` `place`) and the reference
hints (`prefetch.rs` `for_rows`) among its functions. Three changes that cut there were each shown correct and each
left out of `main` because its gain alone did not show in a run. This section records them together; the plan, each
item's own readings, the overlaps and the bars are in `docs/measurements/h264-rounds/bundle3/plan.md`, committed with
the composition before any timing.

### The items

| | item | where its design is described | what the code does |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | the inter placement checked once a band | "Inter round: the placement checked once a band" | `Kernels::predict_part` predicts a block of a macroblock from checks made where their inputs are made: the macroblock rows a band's planes hold (`Macroblocks`, found when the decoder takes a band and kept in `SliceDecoder`), the block's shape in its macroblock (`Part`) and each weighting (`Ops`); the vector kernels run the same code after either placement (`predict_placed`) |
| R | prefetch hints straight from the first row | "The reference hints against FFmpeg's prefetch: stall or issue", the cut (C) | once the last row's index is checked, `prefetch::for_rows` issues the hints for 16, 8, 4 and 2 rows from the first row's address a stride at a time; other counts walk a subslice as before |
| C | chroma deblocking on bytes | "Kernel round: chroma deblocking on bytes" | the macroblock's chroma kernel filters p1 to q1 as bytes, 32 lines a vector (both planes, both edges of a pass), with the parameters read as the bytes of `repr(C)` `EdgeParams`; a t'C0 above 31 goes to the paired kernel |

The sections named above keep their own results; this section records the result of the three together.

### Composition and bars

`base` is `main` at `974f46c1`; P, R and C applied in that order without a conflict in code. P adds a field to
`SliceDecoder` and C changes `EdgeParams`'s representation; since such layout changes have moved one-thread time by
about 0.3% on their own, the one-thread bars are read on the bundle as built. P and C change `unsafe` in
`simd/x86/predict.rs`, `simd/x86/chroma_mb.rs` and `simd/mod.rs`, and R the address `hint_read` is handed;
the list of `unsafe` sites on `rejected/h264-bundle3` names the sites.

| | measure | host | bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| B3-1 | one thread, discard, all 32 | helper VM (2.90 GHz, model 106), pinned | at most 0.990, upper end below 1.000 |
| B3-2 | one thread, discard, the 16 streams at 1080p and 4k | helper VM | at most 0.985 |
| B3-3 | one thread, write, all 32 | helper VM | at most 1.000 |
| B3-4 | one thread, each class, discard and write | helper VM | at most 1.005 |
| B3-5 | eight threads, discard and write, all 32 | `c4-standard-16`, one thread a core | at most 1.005 each |
| B3-6 | eight threads, each class, discard and write | `c4-standard-16` | at most 1.010 |
| B3-7 | one thread, discard, the 64 held-out streams, five rounds | helper VM | at most 1.000 |
| B3-8 | output | | identical to `base` at 1 and 8 threads with and without `fast`; conformance 97 of 97 in four configurations |

One-thread bars are gain bars; the eight-thread ones are a guard against a cost. The bundle ships only if it meets
all eight in one run, and the gating run is requested only if a local timing (the implementer's 2.50 GHz VM, a
screen, not the bar class) meets B3-1's values and an eight-thread local median of at most 1.005.

### Result

One gating run, no call void (`bundle3/gating/`, `bundle3/plan.md`, "Result"): one thread, discard, all 32 **0.9888**
[0.9820, 0.9908], 29 of 32 faster (B3-1 met); the 16 streams at 1080p and 4k **0.9887** [0.9787, 0.9911] (B3-2,
at most 0.985, missed); write 0.9873; every class at or below 0.9921; eight threads 0.9982 discard and 0.9988 write,
classes at most 1.0056 (B3-5, B3-6 met); held-out 64 at one thread 0.9884 (B3-7 met); output identical. A miss of one
bar rejects the bundle. The one-thread gain held on the held-out draw and in every class, but was spread over the
classes rather than concentrated at 1080p and 4k: the 4k instruction cut (0.9510) became 0.9853 in time, about

## Bundle 4: a banded picture's lines and its aprons' rows owned ahead

Two eight-thread rounds whose gain showed but missed a bar, tried together once, as "Bundle 2" was: "Threading round:
a banded picture's lines asked for ahead" (8T 0.9884 [0.9787, 0.9963], sd 0.9952 against a bar of 0.995; 720p
0.9796) and "Threading round: the aprons' rows owned ahead, the decoder's layout kept" (8T 0.9983 [0.9939, 0.9996]
against 0.995; sd 0.9871). Each round's gain lies where the other's is small: the banded hints at 720p, 1080p and 4k
and on the held-out set, the aprons at sd, where a band is one macroblock row and its top apron 23 rows. The two use
the same mechanism, `prefetch::Ownership`.

### Design

One `SliceDecoder::hints` byte for both rounds' hints, the field that was the `ahead` flag, so the decoder's layout
is the one-thread decoder's (the lesson of "Threading round: the aprons' rows owned ahead", whose two new fields cost
its one-thread guard). Its bits: `HINT_AHEAD` (the macroblocks' own lines and the reference's, as before), `HINT_OWN`
(a banded picture: its own lines asked to be owned) and `HINT_APRON` (a band's first macroblock row: the lines of its
top apron that the refresh will write asked to be owned). `mb::hints` sets `HINT_AHEAD | HINT_OWN` for every banded
picture, whatever its size, and `ahead`'s size rule for a picture of one band; `enter_row` sets `HINT_APRON` in a
band's first row of a banded picture and clears it in every other row. Every set but the empty one holds `HINT_AHEAD`,
so the reference hints in `inter.rs` keep one test.

A macroblock's start tests the byte once where no hint is issued, and compares it with `HINT_AHEAD` where only the
size rule's hints are (both as on `main`: a picture of one band, every picture at one thread). Any other set goes, for
the first macroblock of each four only, to `request_banded`, out of line: with an `Ownership` (a CPU with
`prefetchw`), the destination's lines owned and, with `HINT_APRON`, the apron's rows (`request_apron`, over
`picture::rows_refreshed_first`); without one, the destination's read hints. The apron round's other parts come with
it: the entry copy of one luma and one chroma row (the rows intra prediction reads before the refresh), and one copy
per run of consecutive rows from one band in `Canvas::copy_top`.

Rejected: each round's own request path side by side (two out-of-line calls a first macroblock of four, and two
copies of the ownership kernel); testing `mbx % 4` inside `request_banded` alone (a call for each macroblock of a
banded picture, three of four asking for nothing; the review's point on the banded hints); a second, monomorphized
macroblock loop for banded pictures (the whole loop compiled twice for a hint).

At one thread (callgrind, 60 frames, `--discard`), the bundle adds 0.03% of the instructions at 1080p
(`175433794e02`) and 0.04% at sd (`41e324ebb708`), as the banded hints alone did (0.02% and 0.04%).

### Stall check (before timing)

`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/bundle4/` (`README.md`, criteria P1 and P2 fixed before the run): on the miss probe's
host class, the bundle against `main` and against the banded hints alone, that the merged code removes the stalls each
part removed alone.

Result: both met (0.34 USD). P1: every stage's cycles a macroblock fall by 59.8 against `main` over the 32 (bar 20),
inter `resource_stalls.sb` by 19.4 (the banded hints alone 19.8). P2: at sd they fall by 47.9 against the banded hints
alone (bar 20), the aprons' copies by 115.3 less their hints' cost in inter, 67.9. The aprons' hints (22 luma and 10
chroma rows of a band's first row, every row at sd) are the walk of `prefetch::for_rows`, which the stall check's
instruction check had left out of its premise and so missed (16.2 instructions more in inter over the 32, against at
most 5). Output: the 32 training streams byte-identical to `main` at 1 and 8 threads; conformance 97 of 97 at 1, 2
and 8 threads, detected and scalar kernels (`bundle4/checks.txt`).

## Inter round: a band's view read where it is kept

**Result: rejected, by BV-2** (sd 0.9863 against a bar of 0.985; "Result: rejected, by BV-2" below). None of it is
in `main`; the code is on `rejected/h264-band-view`, and the names below (`band_view`, `make_band_view`, `BandViews`)
are its.

At eight threads a reference is banded, and each block that `predict_fast_body` predicts from it takes its view of
the band its window is read from (`Planes`, 120 bytes) from `SliceDecoder::band_views` ("Threading round: band views
kept for the slice"). The function-level profile of `main` at `82ad7c31` against FFmpeg 9.0.2
(`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/profile-82ad7c31/`) found inter prediction the gap left in every class at both thread
counts (+0.079 of FFmpeg's cycles at eight threads, +0.033 at one), and two parts of it that no open round addresses:

- `reference_band` returns the view by value. It stores the 120 bytes in 16-byte pieces, and the caller loads them
  back in 32-byte pieces to copy them to its own stack: a load wider than the stores it reads is not forwarded from
  the store buffer and waits for them to be written. The first such load carried 33% of `predict_fast`'s cycles at sd.
- `reference_band` itself, out of line with a prologue of six registers, finds the slot by the reference's own
  geometry, a chain of four dependent loads (`refs`, the list, the `Arc<Picture>`, its `band_mbs`) for every block,
  and copies the kept view out.

Together 6.0% of CoreAV's cycles at sd at eight threads, 4.1% at 720p, 3.0% at 1080p and 4.8% at 4k; none at one
thread, where every reference is one band (`SliceDecoder::whole`). The rest of the eight-thread inter gap is the
reference hints' walk and the luma kernels, which bundle 3b changes, so this round leaves them alone.

### Design

`band_view` (inlined into `predict_fast_body`) returns `Option<&Planes>`, a borrow of the slot itself, so the block's
kernel reads the view where it is kept: nothing is returned by value or copied. The slot is found by the band that
the window is read from in `BandViews::geometry`, the bands the slice's references are cut into, kept with the slots
(`SliceDecoder::band_views` holds both), so a kept view is found with no read of the reference: the band's index, the
slot's address and two compares. `make_band_view`, out of line, makes a view not kept, as `reference_band` did: the
reference's band, waited for until it is published, checked for the picture's size, and its `Planes::band`. Borrowing
only the `band_views` field (a free function over it, not a method of the decoder) leaves the decoder's other fields
free for the rest of the block.

`BandViews::geometry` is set when the slice starts: the geometry of its first reference of the picture's size cut into
more than one band, or the picture's own where it reads none. It is not the decoding picture's geometry: a picture
that is not a reference is one band (no other picture waits for its bands), so a slice of a B picture at eight threads
would key every view by band 0 of its own picture. The first version of this change did key by the decoding picture's
geometry; the local A/B (information, `band-view/local/`) read 1080p and 4k about 2% slower at eight threads, where
most pictures are such B pictures and each of their blocks made its view again, and the check was moved to the
references' bands before any bar was timed. Every reference picture of a size is cut alike; a reference cut otherwise (a picture made
where the stream had none, `Picture::black`, one band) has its band found by its own geometry, as before, and its slot
is keyed with no band, so that the next block makes the view again rather than taking a wrong one.

Rejected: keeping `reference_band`'s return by value and changing only the copy (whether a copy forwards depends on
how the compiler splits it on each side, which a later change may undo); a field of its own in the decoder for the
references' geometry (a new field changes the decoder's layout, which cost "Threading round: the aprons' rows owned
ahead" its one-thread guard; inside `band_views` it only lengthens a field that the one-thread path does not read);
keying slots by the macroblock row of the window's last row, with no geometry at all (at 720p and up a band is four
or eight rows, and a view would be made again for each of them).

At one thread (callgrind, 60 frames, `--discard`) the change removes 0.05% of the instructions at 1080p
(`175433794e02`) and 0.12% at sd (`41e324ebb708`); at eight threads (callgrind runs the threads one at a time, so the
totals move from run to run) `reference_band`'s 5.7% of the instructions at sd are gone and `predict_fast` gains 2.5%
from the lookup inlined into it; 1080p reads 3.0% fewer in all (`band-view/instructions.txt`).

### Stall check (before timing)

`docs/measurements/h264-rounds/band-view/check/` (`README.md`, criteria V1 to V3 fixed before the run): on the
profile's host class, eight threads, that the change removes the cycles the profile attributed to the band view.
Result: all met. Every stage's cycles a macroblock fall by 37.8 over the 32 (bar 30) and by 51.8 at sd (bar
50), and by 30 to 36 in each other class (bar: no rise above 10): `reference_band`'s 38.3 are gone and
